name: 1,4-Butanediol

tolerance.full: within several weeks of continuous use

addictionPotential: moderately physically and psychologically addictive
summary:
1,4-BD is a clear liquid with intoxicating effects. It is a pro-drug for GHB, and has similar though reportedly inferior effects. It also carries the potential for more health risks than GHB, such as liver toxicity.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to GHB, 1,4-BD has a slower onset (45-60 min vs 15-20 min) as it requires conversion via alcohol dehydrogenase, a slightly longer duration, greater liver load, and an equally critical overdose margin.
effectsSummary: Central nervous system sedation, marked anxiolysis, muscle relaxation, psychomotor slowing, and reduction of inhibitions.
saferUse: LETHAL DANGER: Never combine with alcohol, opioids, or other respiratory depressants.
Space out intake to prevent rapid tolerance and potentially life-threatening withdrawal.
Do not drive or operate heavy machinery while under the influence.
When discontinuing prolonged use, always taper gradually to avoid seizures.

addictionPotential: non-addictive with a low abuse potential
toxicities: extremely low toxicity relative to dose

Released in late 2018, and marketed agressively as a replacement for 1P-LSD. 1B-LSD does not yet have a clearly established safety profile,

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to classic LSD, 1B-LSD requires a slightly higher dose (+15-20% by weight due to the heavier butanoyl group), has a more gradual onset, and a slightly shorter duration (8-10h vs 10-12h).
effectsSummary: Intense sensory and visual alterations, altered perception of space and time, emotional amplification, deep introspection, and potential ego dissolution.
saferUse: Strictly respect Set & Setting (positive mindset, calm and secure physical environment).
Always have a trusted, sober tripsitter present during the experience.
Never combine with lithium, tramadol, or MAOI/SSRI antidepressants.
Test substances with colorimetric reagents prior to use and start with a low test dose.

name: 2,5-DMA

tolerance.full: after ingestion over the couse of multiple days

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary:
2,5-DMA (2,5-dimethoxyamphetamine) is a substituted phenethylamine synthesized by Alexander Shulgin. It is the direct unhalogenated structural backbone of the potent 'DOx' psychedelic series (DOB, DOC, DOI), acting as a partial 5-HT2A agonist and monoamine releasing agent.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to halogenated DOx derivatives (DOB, DOC) which are active at 1-2 mg and last 18-24 hours, 2,5-DMA is substantially less potent (active at 80-150 mg), lasts 6-8 hours, and produces a warmer, more physical stimulant push with subdued visual patterning.
effectsSummary: Physical stimulation, mood enhancement, mild perceptual sharpening, jaw clenching, and modest open-hearted warmth.
dosageRemark: Oral dose: 80-150 mg. Active duration: 6-8 hours. Always use an accurate milligram scale.
generalRisks: Tachycardia, elevated blood pressure, pupil dilation, and insomnia.
longtermRisks: Monoamine depletion and classical 5-HT2A cross-tolerance.
saferUse: Never confuse with halogenated DOx compounds which are 100 times more potent.
Avoid combining with stimulants or MAOIs.

name: 2-Aminoindane

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary: ⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to amphetamine, 2-AI is a mild noradrenergic stimulant that enhances alertness without major cardiovascular spikes.
effectsSummary: Heightened alertness and concentration, dopaminergic euphoria, physical and mental energy surge, increased heart rate, and appetite suppression.
saferUse: Stay hydrated regularly (water or electrolyte drinks, ~500 ml/h during exertion).
Avoid compulsive redosing which sharply escalates cardiotoxicity and hyperthermia.
Never combine with other stimulants, MAOIs, or decongestants.
Monitor blood pressure and body temperature, and ensure adequate recovery intervals.

name: 2-CMC

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to 3-CMC, 2-CMC acts as a nearly pure dopaminergic/noradrenergic psychostimulant devoid of empathogenic warmth, with prominent peripheral adrenergic load and rapid redosing urge.
effectsSummary: Moderate physical stimulation, focus, elevated heart rate, limited euphoria, redosing urge.
dosageRemark: Functional stimulant profile, but marked cardiovascular strain when escalating doses.
generalRisks: Tachycardia, hypertension, insomnia, anxiety, dehydration.
longtermRisks: Chronic fatigue, tolerance, psychological dependence, cardiovascular strain.
saferUse: Avoid repetitive compulsive redosing
Do not mix with other stimulants
Maintain adequate hydration

summary:

Unlike 3-MMC and 4-MMC, 2-MMC acts predominantly on dopamine and norepinephrine (NDRA/NDRI) with minimal serotonergic release. It produces clean physical stimulation, wakefulness, and euphoria, but notably lacks the warm empathogenic and entactogenic qualities of its isomers.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to 3-MMC, 2-MMC is significantly less entactogenic (minimal serotonin release) and delivers cleaner, more functional dopaminergic stimulation with a similar duration (3-5h), though carrying high overdose risks when users escalate doses searching for missing empathy.
effectsSummary: Physical and mental stimulation, increased energy, elevated heart rate, moderate vasoconstriction, and marked redosing urge upon comedown.
dosageRemark: Generally less euphorigenic per dose than 3-MMC, leading some users to dangerously escalate doses in search of missing empathogenic effects, drastically increasing cardiovascular strain.
generalRisks: Tachycardia, hypertension, dehydration, severe insomnia, anxiety, bruxism, and cardiovascular exhaustion during binge sessions.
longtermRisks: Dopaminergic depletion, post-use depression, tolerance buildup, psychological addiction, and chronic cardiovascular strain.
saferUse: Do not escalate doses in search of missing empathogenic effects
Stay hydrated (0.5L water/hour)
Set a strict maximum quantity before the session
Avoid combining with other stimulants or alcohol

name: 2C-B
addictionPotential: non-addictive with a low potential for abuse
summary:
A popular psychedelic in the phenethylamine family. Provides empathic experiences at lower doses and strong visual and psychedelic experiences at higher doses. Commonly used as a party drug as it is more clear-headed than most psychedelics. 2C-B has been in use since the early 1990s

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to LSD and mescaline, 2C-B provides a compact 4-to-6 hour duration, richly colorful and neon visual geometry, and an intact, grounded mental headspace. At low-to-moderate doses it produces warm tactile empathy and erotic enhancement reminiscent of MDMA, without post-session monoamine depletion or depression.
effectsSummary: Perceptions and feelings become more intense. From 10-15 mg (snorted already from 7 mg), the effect usually takes on a hallucinogenic character. The boundaries between inside and outside can dissolve. Often moving coloured patterns and luminous fields around objects and persons are perceived. However, the intoxication is felt to be less profound than with LSD.
dosageRemark: 2C-B is effective even in small doses; a gradual approach to the individual dose is recommended. Over the 12 to 24 milligram range, every 2 milligrams can make a profound increase or change of response. Doses above 35 mg can be experienced as unpleasantly strong even by experienced users.
generalRisks: The pupils dilate, blood pressure rises and nausea, sweating and dizziness may occur. Some users report stomach and intestinal problems, and mild allergic reactions (such as coughing due to increased mucus production) may occur. Disorientation, confusion and feelings of anxiety, even fear of death, are risks on a psychological level.
longtermRisks: There are no research results on long-term risks so far.
saferUse: 2C-B seems very setting-dependent and is only suitable for parties to a limited extent.
Be aware of set and setting: Use 2C-B only in places where you feel comfortable and safe. Do not use if you are afraid of the drug.
Never consume 2C-B alone and only when you feel mentally and physically well and are well rested.
Do not add more, dose carefully.
Drink enough water during the trip.
Follow the safer-sniffing rules when sniffing. Attention, 2C-B burns painfully in the nose!
People with cardiovascular diseases and diabetics are at increased risk when consuming 2C-B.

name: 3-CMC

summary:

⚠️ Major Harm Reduction Warning: As a chlorinated phenylalkylamine structurally related to 4-chloroamphetamine (4-CA), 3-CMC raises severe scientific concerns regarding potential direct serotonergic axon neurotoxicity. It is also exceptionally caustic to nasal and mucosal tissue.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to 3-MMC, 3-CMC (clophedrone) is slightly less potent by weight, much more caustic to nasal tissue, and carries a major toxicological suspicion of direct serotonergic axon neurotoxicity analogous to 4-chloroamphetamine (4-CA).

generalRisks: Suspected serotonergic neurotoxicity, serotonin syndrome with serotonergic drugs, mucosal tissue necrosis, tachycardia, hyperthermia, paranoid binge psychosis.
longtermRisks: Persistent serotonergic axon damage, severe refractory depression, chronic anxiety, sleep disorders, and heavy addiction.
saferUse: Avoid insufflation due to extreme caustic damage to nasal passages
Strictly limit session duration and avoid consecutive binge redoses
Never combine with antidepressants (SSRIs, MAOIs, tramadol)
Take into account the documented neurotoxicity risk of chlorinated stimulants

Acetyl-Fentanyl is an opioid analgesic substance that is an analogue of Fentanyl. It's potency is roughly ~6.67 times that of Morphine. Making it ~15 times less potent than its parent compound Fentanyl.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to Morphine and Fentanyl, acetylfentanyl is 15-30 times more potent than morphine (about 3 times weaker than pure fentanyl), with an ultra-short duration and lethal respiratory arrest risk.
effectsSummary: Potent analgesia, warm sedation, opioid euphoria, sense of deep contentment, pinpoint pupils, respiratory depression, and gastrointestinal slowing.
saferUse: LETHAL OVERDOSE RISK: Always keep naloxone (Narcan, Nyxoid) immediately accessible.
NEVER combine with benzodiazepines, alcohol, pregabalin, or any CNS depressants.
Never use alone, and test with fentanyl/nitazene test strips before use.
Space doses strictly to prevent severe physical dependence and debilitating withdrawal.

name: Adrafinil

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: not addictive with a low potential for abuse
summary:
A prodrug to modafinil, this compound is often used to increase wakefulness and alertness. Due to hepatic metabolism it has a slower onset than modafinil and may cause liver damage in excess. Some users have reported acne as an adverse effect. Unregulated in the US.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to Modafinil, adrafinil is its prodrug: it takes about 1 hour longer to kick in as it must be metabolized by the liver, placing greater demand on liver enzymes.
effectsSummary: Heightened alertness and concentration, dopaminergic euphoria, physical and mental energy surge, increased heart rate, and appetite suppression.
saferUse: Stay hydrated regularly (water or electrolyte drinks, ~500 ml/h during exertion).
Avoid compulsive redosing which sharply escalates cardiotoxicity and hyperthermia.
Never combine with other stimulants, MAOIs, or decongestants.
Monitor blood pressure and body temperature, and ensure adequate recovery intervals.

name: Agomelatine
addictionPotential: not habit-forming (no discontinuation syndrome)
toxicities: HEPATOTOXICITY (elevated transaminases and rare severe hepatic injury — mandatory liver function blood tests!)
60-fold toxic exposure spike if combined with Fluvoxamine or Ciprofloxacin!
summary:
Agomelatine (Valdoxan) is an atypical melatonergic (MT1/MT2 agonist) and 5-HT2C antagonist antidepressant taken at bedtime to resynchronize circadian rhythms and treat major depression without sexual dysfunction or withdrawal.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to SSRIs, agomelatine (Valdoxan) combines MT1/MT2 melatonergic agonism with 5-HT2C antagonism. It resynchronizes circadian sleep cycles with zero sexual dysfunction or discontinuation syndrome, but mandates regular hepatic transaminase monitoring due to rare hepatotoxicity.
effectsSummary: Promotes sleep onset/architecture at night and gradually lifts depressive mood without serotonin reuptake inhibition, weight gain, or sexual side effects.
dosageRemark: BEDTIME 24h SCHEDULE: Take once daily right at bedtime (25 mg standard, up to 50 mg max). The 'Heavy' threshold (50 mg) is the strict maximum single and daily dose. Requires baseline and periodic liver transaminase (ALT/AST) monitoring!
generalRisks: Headache, dizziness, somnolence or insomnia, nausea, and dose-related liver injury (stop immediately if dark urine, pale stools, yellow eyes/jaundice, right upper abdominal pain, or unusual fatigue occur!).
longtermRisks: Drug-induced liver injury (contraindicated in hepatic impairment or transaminases >3x upper limit of normal).
saferUse: Complete all scheduled liver blood tests (before starting and at 3, 6, 12, and 24 weeks).
STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED with Fluvoxamine or Ciprofloxacin (potent CYP1A2 inhibitors multiply Agomelatine levels up to 60x!).
Avoid Alcohol and excessive Paracetamol/hepatotoxic drugs to protect your liver.

name: AL-LAD

tolerance.full: almost immediately after ingestion

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary:
AL-LAD is a hallucinogenic drug, lysergamide and an analogue of LSD. It is reported as having some subtle experiential differences to LSD (such as increased visuals), and also appears to be slightly shorter lasting. AL-LAD doses are similar to those of LSD, depending on purity. Its availability on the Internet since 2013 has lead to strong popularity among the drug community.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to LSD, AL-LAD provides far more spectacular and colorful visuals while maintaining clear-headed cognitive lucidity and a more manageable duration (6-8h).
effectsSummary: Intense sensory and visual alterations, altered perception of space and time, emotional amplification, deep introspection, and potential ego dissolution.
saferUse: Strictly respect Set & Setting (positive mindset, calm and secure physical environment).
Always have a trusted, sober tripsitter present during the experience.
Never combine with lithium, tramadol, or MAOI/SSRI antidepressants.
Test substances with colorimetric reagents prior to use and start with a low test dose.

name: Alcohol

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: extremely addictive with a high potential for abuse
toxicities: Death from ethanol consumption is possible when blood alcohol levels reach 0.4%
summary:
Alcohol is a CNS depressant that acts through the GABAₐ receptor, and is one of the most common strong psychoactives used by humans. It has a long history of use and its intoxicating effects are well-studied and documented. It remains legal in most parts of the world.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to benzodiazepines and GHB, alcohol (ethanol) exerts a broad, diffuse neurochemical action (GABA-A positive allosteric modulation, NMDA antagonism, endogenous opioid and dopamine release). Despite cultural normalization, it carries high systemic organ toxicity (cirrhosis, neurodegeneration) and life-threatening physical withdrawal risks (delirium tremens, grand mal seizures).
effectsSummary:
Stimulation, relaxation, calming down, disinhibition, sociability, euphoria, reduction of the ability to react, overestimation of oneself and urge to talk, but also melancholy or irritability up to aggressiveness.
Absinthe ("The Green Fairy"), a high-proof spirit (usually 50 - 70 % by volume), contains the plant substance thujone. Together with the main active ingredient alcohol, thujone is said to have stimulating and mind-altering effects. In Europe, as in Switzerland, clear limits apply (max. 35 mg thujone per kg alcohol). Caution with chronic use! A thujone overdose manifests itself in seizures and epilepsy-like symptoms.
dosageRemark: Standard drinks such as 3 dl beer, 1 dl wine or 2 cl spirits contain about 12 g alcohol. The effect of alcohol is influenced by the amount consumed, the type of alcohol (sugary and/or carbonated), the period of consumption and individual factors (age, sex, weight). The blood alcohol concentration is measured in parts per thousand (‰). The higher the alcohol concentration in the blood, the stronger the effect of alcohol.
generalRisks:
Small amounts of alcohol generally have a relaxing and exhilarating effect, a general feeling of well-being spreads, fears are reduced and sociability increases. The consumption of larger amounts can lead to balance and speech disorders, visual disturbances (double vision or tunnel vision), stomach pain, nausea to vomiting, headaches (hangover) due to dehydration, loss of control and blackouts. There is a risk of accidents due to overestimation of one's own abilities and reduced ability to react. High doses can lead to hypothermia or overheating, deep sleep and coma. Very high doses (blood alcohol concentration of 3-4‰) can be life-threatening.
Binge drinking, i.e. the consumption of a large amount of alcohol in a very short time, causes the blood alcohol content to rise particularly quickly and strongly. This can quickly lead to alcohol poisoning. Consequences can be: comatose state, memory lapses (film tears), deactivation of important reflexes (danger of choking when vomiting, danger of freezing to death when cold) as well as epileptic seizures. There is also an increased risk of thrombosis, high or low blood pressure, respiratory depression and sudden cardiac death.
longtermRisks:
Since alcohol is a cytotoxin, regular heavy consumption can have consequences such as damage to all bodily organs, deficiency symptoms, disorders of the nervous system, coordination of movement and memory functions, and even alcohol-induced dementia. Alcohol is a co-carcinogen, i.e. it significantly increases the carcinogenic effect of other substances (e.g. nicotine).
Alcohol can produce a dependence with psychological and physical symptoms. Typical withdrawal symptoms are trembling, sweating, nausea and vomiting up to epileptic seizures. On a psychological level, irritability, anxiety disorders, depressive moods and hallucinations may occur. Tolerance develops with regular consumption.
saferUse: Do not consume alcohol out of boredom or when you feel bad.
Drink alcohol with pleasure and take your time.
Do not drink alcohol on an empty stomach.
Avoid mixed consumption of different alcoholic drinks, drink water with it (e.g. a glass of water after each alcoholic drink).

Be careful with mixed drinks (e.g. alcopops) or self-mixed drinks! With these sweet drinks you can hardly taste the alcohol, even though a 3-litre bottle contains about two schnapps. The danger of an unintentional overdose is high.

In general, refrain from consuming alcohol if you consume other psychoactive substances; their effect is altered by the alcohol, or sometimes life-threatening side effects occur (e.g. alcohol and GHB = danger of suffocation!).
If you drink, you don't drive. Use public transport, take a taxi or walk.
Alcohol consumption during pregnancy is a risk for the foetus. Severe damage to the child can be the result.
Follow the safe sex rules even when under the influence of alcohol.

name: ALD-52

tolerance.full: almost immediately after ingestion

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary:
ALD-52, or N-acetyl-LSD is a less common chemical analogue of LSD, first synthesised by Albert Hoffman. It was famously implicated in the 'Orange Sunshine' trial. A psychedelic lysergamide, this compound exhibits similar properties to LSD, and is thought to be a pro-drug for LSD.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to LSD, ALD-52 (1-acetyl-LSD) has a notably smoother, gentler onset with less initial come-up anxiety for an equivalent peak intensity.
effectsSummary: Intense sensory and visual alterations, altered perception of space and time, emotional amplification, deep introspection, and potential ego dissolution.
saferUse: Strictly respect Set & Setting (positive mindset, calm and secure physical environment).
Always have a trusted, sober tripsitter present during the experience.
Never combine with lithium, tramadol, or MAOI/SSRI antidepressants.
Test substances with colorimetric reagents prior to use and start with a low test dose.

name: Alimemazine

tolerance.full: develops rapidly within 3 - 7 days to hypnotic effect

addictionPotential: low-to-moderate psychological habit formation (sedative/opioid-potentiating and high-dose anticholinergic misuse)
toxicities: anticholinergic delirium, QT prolongation, orthostatic hypotension, photosensitivity, and respiratory depression synergy with opioids/alcohol
summary:
Alimemazine / Trimeprazine (Théralène 5 mg tablets & 4% oral drops) is a phenothiazine first-generation H1 antihistamine and anticholinergic widely used in Europe for occasional insomnia, closely related to promethazine.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Alimemazine (trimeprazine, Theralene) is a sedating phenothiazine H1 antihistamine widely utilized as a hypnotic, delivering profound sleep induction accompanied by noticeable next-day residual grogginess.
effectsSummary: Heavy, long-lasting drowsiness and sleep promotion with frequent next-morning hangover grogginess and dry mouth; high diverted doses cause dysphoric anticholinergic confusion and hallucinations.
dosageRemark: DIVERSION-ADAPTED DOSAGES: Therapeutic bedtime hypnotic dose in adults is 5-20 mg (taken 15-30 min before bed). Intakes >= 35-60 mg ('Strong'/'Heavy') exceed medical limits and trigger intense hangover sedation, orthostatic hypotension, QT risk, and anticholinergic delirium.
generalRisks: Pronounced next-day drowsiness, dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision, urinary retention, skin photosensitivity (avoid UV exposure!), QT prolongation, and restless legs.
longtermRisks: Rapid loss of sleep efficacy after a few days, anticholinergic cognitive impairment, and rebound insomnia.
saferUse: Limit medical use to occasional short-term insomnia (5-20 mg max at bedtime) and protect skin from sun/UV.
NEVER combine with Opioids/Codeine ('lean'-style potentiation risks fatal respiratory arrest!), Alcohol, Benzodiazepines, DXM, or anticholinergics.

name: Allylescaline

tolerance.full: almost immediately after ingestion

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary:
Mescaline analogue with a much lower dose, that seems to rely heavily on colours.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to natural Mescaline, allylescaline requires much lower doses (20-35 mg vs 300-500 mg) and produces less gastric nausea.
effectsSummary: Intense sensory and visual alterations, altered perception of space and time, emotional amplification, deep introspection, and potential ego dissolution.
saferUse: Strictly respect Set & Setting (positive mindset, calm and secure physical environment).
Always have a trusted, sober tripsitter present during the experience.
Never combine with lithium, tramadol, or MAOI/SSRI antidepressants.
Test substances with colorimetric reagents prior to use and start with a low test dose.

name: Alpha-GPC

tolerance.full: after prolonged and repeated usage

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary:
Alpha-GPC (L-alpha glycerylphosphorylcholine) is a highly bioavailable, brain-penetrant choline donor naturally found in neuronal membranes. Efficiently crossing the blood-brain barrier, it directly provides precursor choline for acetylcholine (ACh) neurotransmission and phosphatidylcholine membrane repair.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to basic choline bitartrate (which has poor blood-brain barrier penetration and causes gastrointestinal distress), Alpha-GPC delivers superior central cholinergic support and acutely enhances growth hormone release. It reliably abolishes the characteristic tension headaches induced by racetam nootropics.
effectsSummary: Sharpened working memory, increased verbal fluency, mental stamina, and optimized power output in resistance training.
dosageRemark: Standard supplemental dose: 300-600 mg daily taken in the morning or 45 minutes prior to mental exertion.
generalRisks: Cholinergic headache (if acetylcholine levels become excessive), insomnia if taken late, and mild dizziness.
longtermRisks: High-dose chronic choline supplementation may elevate gut-derived TMAO levels in susceptible individuals with dysbiosis.
saferUse: Take in the morning or early afternoon to prevent interference with natural sleep cycles.
Use as an essential co-factor alongside racetam compounds to avoid cholinergic depletion headaches.

name: Alprazolam

tolerance.full: within a couple of days of continuous use

addictionPotential: extremely physically and psychologically addictive
toxicities: potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like alcohol, opioids, or barbiturates
summary:
An extremely common benzodiazepine better known as Xanax, frequently prescribed for the treatment of anxiety and panic disorders. Alprazolam is short-lasting and primarily anxiolytic, though also possesses hypnotic properties. At high doses amnesia and loss of inhibition are common. Do not mix with other depressants.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to diazepam (Valium), alprazolam (Xanax) is roughly 10 times more potent by weight with a significantly faster onset and intermediate half-life (10 to 12 hours) devoid of ultra-long-acting active metabolites. While highly efficacious for aborting acute panic attacks, this sharp pharmacokinetic profile creates a far higher risk of rapid tolerance, inter-dose rebound anxiety, and severe addiction.
effectsSummary:
Anti-excitant and anti-anxiety, sedative, soporific and muscle relaxant. At high doses: slowing down, drowsiness, danger of memory lapses ("film tear").
Taking benzodiazepines increases the effectiveness of the neurotransmitter gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) at the GABA-A receptor. This triggers sedative (calming), hypnotic, anxiolytic (anxiety-relieving), anticonvulsant (anticonvulsant) and muscle-relaxing effects in the body. Benzodiazepines have a depressant effect on the central nervous system. The flow of information in the brain between the brain cells (neurons) is thereby reduced / disturbed and feelings and perceptions are dampened.
The breakdown of the individual active ingredients of benzodiazepines in the body is age-dependent and therefore varies from person to person.
generalRisks:
There is little information available on risks, toxicity, side effects and long-term consequences. Therefore, the general information on benzodiazepines applies:
When mixing with other downers (alcohol, GHB/GBL, heroin) there is a risk of respiratory paralysis!
Taking benzodiazepines can cause numerous undesirable side effects. In addition, regular and long-term use carries a very high risk of physical and psychological dependence. Benzodiazepines should only be taken as prescribed by a doctor and only for a short period of time (max. 4-6 weeks). Longer-term use should be discussed with the treating specialist. The dosages and duration of action of the individual benzodiazepines differ considerably.
Side effects of benzodiazepines may be as follows: Prolonged fatigue, gastrointestinal problems, impaired reactions, hypersensitivity reactions, headaches, dizziness, motor difficulties, visual disturbances, slowed breathing, muscle weakness, confusion, sexual dysfunction, aggression, outbursts of anger, restlessness, random movements, allergies, skin problems/rashes and speech and movement disorders. Some benzodiazepines can cause seizures in epileptics.
longtermRisks:
Regular and long-term use can lead to psychological and physical dependence (very high dependence potential). Immediate discontinuation of the drug after prolonged use can lead to negative withdrawal symptoms (including dizziness, physical weakness, inner restlessness, tremors, sleep disturbances, headaches, sweating, nausea, hallucinations and depression).
In addition, seizures and memory disorders/loss and listlessness (hangover effects) can occur. In case of possible dependence, withdrawal should be discussed with a doctor beforehand and the withdrawal should be medically accompanied. It is extremely important that the dose is reduced gradually.
saferUse: If medicines are obtained on the black market or on the internet and not from a pharmacy/medical facility, the contents are unclear. Have the medicine tested for the exact ingredients in a drug check!
Do not rely on dosage information from colleagues who regularly use benzodiazepines. Due to habituation or dependence, their doses can be much higher and fatal for new users.
Blisters of counterfeits may look identical to the original packaging.

The simultaneous consumption of depressant substances such as alcohol, ketamine, GHB/GBL, nitrous oxide, opioids and/or other benzodiazepines is dangerous as there is an increased risk of vomiting and unconsciousness. The risk of suffocation is high!

name: Amisulpride

tolerance.full: antipsychotic stabilization over 1 - 4 weeks
tolerance.zero: taper gradually to prevent rebound symptoms

addictionPotential: not habit-forming (abrupt cessation causes rebound insomnia, nausea, or psychotic relapse)
toxicities: QT interval prolongation / cardiac arrhythmia risk
extrapyramidal motor symptoms (akathisia, dystonia, parkinsonism) and rare neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS)
summary:
Amisulpride is a prescription antipsychotic (neuroleptic) medication used in schizophrenia, bipolar mania/maintenance, or severe agitation. Selective D2/D3 benzamide atypical antipsychotic (Solian): low doses (50-100 mg) preferentially block presynaptic autoreceptors to improve negative symptoms/dysthymia, while higher doses (400-800+ mg/day) treat positive psychotic symptoms.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Amisulpride (Solian) selectively targets D2/D3 dopamine receptors. At low doses (50-100 mg), it preferentially blocks presynaptic auto-receptors to increase dopamine transmission (alleviating negative symptoms and avolition); at high doses (400-800 mg), it acts as an antipsychotic postsynaptic antagonist.
effectsSummary: Dopamine D2 / serotonin receptor antagonism (or partial agonism) reducing hallucinations, delusions, mania, agitation, and psychedelic 5-HT2A/dopaminergic effects.
dosageRemark: SINGLE INTAKE CAP: Doses up to 400 mg/day are taken once daily; doses >400 mg/day (up to 800-1200 mg/24h max) MUST be split into two intakes (every 12 hours)! Dose-dependent QT prolongation risk. The 'Heavy' threshold (400 mg) represents the maximum single unit oral intake. Never stop antipsychotic treatment abruptly without medical guidance.
generalRisks: Sedation or akathisia (inner restlessness), orthostatic hypotension, dizziness, weight gain, elevated prolactin, extrapyramidal stiffness/tremor, QT prolongation, and rare Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (high fever + muscle rigidity = medical emergency).
longtermRisks: Weight gain, insulin resistance/type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hyperprolactinemia, and tardive dyskinesia with chronic exposure.
saferUse: Respect your prescribed schedule and never exceed 400 mg in a single intake.
Avoid Alcohol, Opioids, and unprescribed sedatives (additive CNS depression and hypotension).
Avoid combining with other QT-prolonging medications (Escitalopram, Citalopram, Hydroxyzine, Methadone) without ECG monitoring.
Seek immediate emergency care if high fever, severe muscle stiffness, and confusion occur (Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome).

name: Amitriptyline

tolerance.full: 2 - 4 weeks for antidepressant action (immediate sedation)

addictionPotential: not habit-forming (no recreational potential), causes cholinergic rebound withdrawal if stopped suddenly
toxicities: HIGHLY CARDIOTOXIC in overdose (sodium-channel blockade, QRS widening, fatal ventricular arrhythmias, seizures, coma)
serotonin syndrome with MAOIs/Tramadol/SSRIs and severe anticholinergic toxicity
summary:
Amitriptyline is a tricyclic antidepressant (TCA) acting as a serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor alongside strong antihistaminic, anticholinergic, and alpha-1 blocking properties. Widely prescribed at low doses (10-50 mg) for neuropathic pain, migraine prophylaxis, fibromyalgia, and insomnia, and at higher doses (50-150 mg/day) for severe depression (Laroxyl).

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to modern SSRIs, amitriptyline (Elavil) is a tertiary tricyclic antidepressant (TCA) with peerless efficacy for neuropathic pain and migraine prophylaxis at low doses (10-50 mg). However, heavy anticholinergic side effects and lethal cardiotoxicity in overdose severely limit its use at full antidepressant doses.
effectsSummary: Antidepressant, neuropathic pain relief, and strong sedation/sleep induction; causes dry mouth, constipation, orthostatic dizziness, and blurred vision.
dosageRemark: NARROW THERAPEUTIC MARGIN: The 'Heavy' threshold (100 mg) represents the maximum single outpatient unit dose per intake (higher daily totals up to 150-200 mg/24h are divided or strictly supervised). Often taken in the evening due to sedation.
generalRisks: Sedation, dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention, blurred vision, tachycardia, orthostatic hypotension, QT/QRS prolongation, lowered seizure threshold, and severe cardiotoxicity in overdose.
longtermRisks: Weight gain, dental caries (from chronic dry mouth), anticholinergic cognitive burden, and withdrawal symptoms if stopped abruptly.
saferUse: Never exceed 100 mg in a single outpatient intake — tricyclic overdose is rapidly cardiotoxic.
NEVER combine with MAOIs, Tramadol, MDMA, or Clonidine.
Avoid combining with LSD/psychedelics (markedly intensifies trips and lowers seizure threshold!), Alcohol, Benzodiazepines, Opioids, or anticholinergics.

name: Amphetamine

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: has high abuse potential and can cause psychological dependence with chronic use
summary:
A very popular CNS stimulant available on prescription and black markets. Recreational in high doses, producing mild euphoria and an abundance of energy. Popular in eastern europe and the US.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to cocaine, amphetamine provides a substantially longer duration of action (4-8 hours), smoother pharmacokinetics, and active presynaptic monoamine release that sustains functional focus without frantic redosing. Compared to methamphetamine, it has lower lipophilicity, slower blood-brain barrier penetration, and lower direct monoaminergic neurotoxicity.
effectsSummary: The release of the endogenous neurotransmitters noradrenalin and dopamine produced by the use of amphetamine can cause a feeling of increased performance, an increase in self-esteem, an increase in body temperature, the suppression of tiredness, hunger and thirst, an increased willingness to take risks and a suppressed feeling of pain, and can lead to euphoria as well as an increased urge to talk (babble flash).
dosageRemark: Because of the varying purity (the amphetamine content varies from almost 0 % to almost 100 %!), dosing is difficult and the risk of overdose is high. Doses of more than 25 mg of pure amphetamine increase the negative effects. A dose of 50 mg/night should be the maximum, whether snorted or swallowed.
generalRisks: Tremors, restlessness, nausea, palpitations and cardiac arrhythmias, sleep disturbances, headaches, nervousness, irritability, loss of appetite, aggressive behaviour and, in combination with alcohol, danger of alcohol poisoning. At high doses: hallucinations, circulatory failure, strokes as well as kidney, liver and heart failure and states of deep unconsciousness. An often underestimated danger is the rise in body temperature, which can lead to dehydration of the body. In high doses, acute amphetamine psychosis can occur. Signs of this are hallucinations in the form of colour spots and with features of schizophrenia. The risk of such an acute mental disorder increases with consumption over several days and/or if high doses are taken and food intake and sleep are neglected over a longer period of time. Such an experience usually normalises after sufficient sleep. During and after coming down: extreme need for sleep, exhaustion, strong feeling of hunger,depressive mood, irritability, etc.
longtermRisks: There is a risk of addiction with psychological symptoms, especially if the use takes on a (performance-enhancing) function in everyday life (e.g. at work) or physical/psychological exhaustion is combated with amphetamine. Frequent use of amphetamine not infrequently leads to physical deficiency symptoms (e.g. calcium deficiency, which can lead to bone and tooth problems) and to psychological problems such as dejection or listlessness. Regular and high-dose use can lead to constant restlessness (but also persistent fatigue), sleep and circulatory disorders as well as anxiety disorders up to persistent amphetamine psychosis with paranoid delusions. In addition, high blood pressure, cardiac arrhythmias, weight loss, skin inflammations ("speed pimples"), stomach problems as well as liver and kidney damage and cramps are possible. Snorting damages the nasal mucous membranes and the nasal septum, swallowing damages the stomach mucous membranes. Chronic consumption also favours brain haemorrhages and strokes with sudden paralysis.
saferUse: Dose low. Think about how long you want to be awake before you take it! Do not suppress your need for sleep.
The lowest-risk form of amphetamine use is to swallow it.
Eat enough after consumption to prevent weight loss.
Drink enough (non-alcoholic drinks).
Take extra vitamin C and D and minerals (iron, calcium and magnesium) with frequent use.
Follow the safer-sniffing rules when sniffing.
Refrain from mixed consumption! Make sure to take breaks from consumption.
Mentally ill persons, persons with high blood pressure, liver and kidney diseases, diabetics and pregnant women should refrain from using amphetamines.
It is better not to wear headgear (danger of overheating!).
Amphetamine pastes should always be well dried before consumption.

name: Aniracetam

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: non-addictive with a low potential for abuse
summary:
An anxiolytic nootropic which modulates the AMPA receptor. Significantly more potent than racetam. May have positive effects on memory and cognition. Little recreational value. Sold in Europe as a prescription drug, but not approved by the FDA in the US.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to Piracetam, aniracetam is fat-soluble, more potent per milligram, and provides mild anxiolytic qualities that support verbal fluency and creativity.
effectsSummary: Subtle cognitive enhancement, improved mental clarity, support of working memory, and neuroprotection without acute intoxication.
saferUse: Follow recommended physiological dosing guidelines and cycle periodic washout breaks.
Check hepatic and renal clearance pathways when co-administering with prescription medications.
Prioritize nutritional balance and consistent restorative sleep as the foundational baseline.

name: APICA

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary: ⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to THC, APICA (2NE1) produces an abrupt onset and profound cognitive disorientation without the safety margin of plant cannabis.
effectsSummary: Physical relaxation, altered sensory perception, appetite stimulation, short-term memory impairment, and gentle cognitive deceleration.
saferUse: For synthetic cannabinoids, dose at microgram precision: high risk of seizures and cardiac arrest.
Never drive or operate machinery during or shortly after consumption.
If acute anxiety or tachycardia occurs, rest in a quiet environment and consider CBD to mitigate effects.
Prefer dry herb vaporization or oral ingestion over harmful smoke inhalation.

name: Apomorphine
summary:
Apomorphine (Apokyn) is a morphine derivative produced by acid-catalyzed dehydration, completely devoid of opioid receptor activity. It functions as a potent, broad-spectrum dopamine D1 and D2 receptor agonist. Administered subcutaneously for advanced Parkinson's disease to rapidly rescue severe 'off' motor freezing episodes.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to oral levodopa, subcutaneous apomorphine rescues parkinsonian akinetic freezing within 4-10 minutes, but powerfully activates the brainstem chemoreceptor trigger zone (CTZ), necessitating prophylactic antiemetic co-therapy (domperidone or trimethobenzamide) to prevent emesis.
effectsSummary: Rapid reversal of akinetic motor freezing, relief of rigidity and tremor, reflex penile tumescence, and acute nausea if unpremedicated.
dosageRemark: ⚠️ SUBCUTANEOUS USE ONLY: 1-6 mg administered via subcutaneous pen injection. Never administer intravenously.
generalRisks: Violent emesis, severe orthostatic hypotension, sudden sleep attacks, and yawning.
longtermRisks: Subcutaneous panniculitis/nodules, dopamine dysregulation syndrome, and compulsive behaviors (hypersexuality).
saferUse: Always premedicate with an antiemetic prior to initiation.
Remain seated following injection to prevent syncope from orthostatic hypotension.

name: Aripiprazole

tolerance.full: antipsychotic stabilization over 1 - 4 weeks
tolerance.zero: taper gradually to prevent rebound symptoms

addictionPotential: not habit-forming (abrupt cessation causes rebound insomnia, nausea, or psychotic relapse)
toxicities: QT interval prolongation / cardiac arrhythmia risk
extrapyramidal motor symptoms (akathisia, dystonia, parkinsonism) and rare neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS)
summary:
Aripiprazole is a prescription antipsychotic (neuroleptic) medication used in schizophrenia, bipolar mania/maintenance, or severe agitation. Third-generation partial D2 / 5-HT1A agonist and 5-HT2A antagonist (Abilify) prescribed for schizophrenia, bipolar mania, and major depression augmentation. Less sedating than olanzapine/quetiapine, but frequently causes early akathisia/insomnia.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to full antagonists like haloperidol and olanzapine, aripiprazole (Abilify) functions as a dopamine D2 partial agonist and 5-HT1A partial agonist. Acting as a dopamine system stabilizer, it is weight-neutral and non-sedating, but frequently precipitates acute motor restlessness (akathisia) during initial titration.
effectsSummary: Dopamine D2 / serotonin receptor antagonism (or partial agonism) reducing hallucinations, delusions, mania, agitation, and psychedelic 5-HT2A/dopaminergic effects.
dosageRemark: 24h DAILY SCHEDULE: Taken once every 24 hours (often in the morning if activating; 5-30 mg/day). Very long 75-hour elimination half-life. The 'Heavy' threshold (30 mg) represents the maximum single unit oral intake. Never stop antipsychotic treatment abruptly without medical guidance.
generalRisks: Sedation or akathisia (inner restlessness), orthostatic hypotension, dizziness, weight gain, elevated prolactin, extrapyramidal stiffness/tremor, QT prolongation, and rare Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (high fever + muscle rigidity = medical emergency).
longtermRisks: Weight gain, insulin resistance/type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hyperprolactinemia, and tardive dyskinesia with chronic exposure.
saferUse: Respect your prescribed schedule and never exceed 30 mg in a single intake.
Avoid Alcohol, Opioids, and unprescribed sedatives (additive CNS depression and hypotension).
Avoid combining with other QT-prolonging medications (Escitalopram, Citalopram, Hydroxyzine, Methadone) without ECG monitoring.
Seek immediate emergency care if high fever, severe muscle stiffness, and confusion occur (Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome).

name: Armodafinil

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: mildly addictive with a low potential for abuse
toxicities: The median lethal dose at which 50% of participants die (LD50) from either armodafinil or modafinil for human beings has never been reached
summary:
The more potent of the two modafinil isomers, said to have a longer duration and lesser side effects. Sometimes prescribed for ADHD and daytime sleepiness.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to racemic modafinil (Provigil), armodafinil (Nuvigil) consists of the isolated (R)-enantiomer. It demonstrates slower systemic clearance and superior late-day plasma concentrations, providing sustained, seamless wakefulness across 12 to 15 hours from a lower milligram dose.
effectsSummary: Heightened alertness and concentration, dopaminergic euphoria, physical and mental energy surge, increased heart rate, and appetite suppression.
saferUse: Stay hydrated regularly (water or electrolyte drinks, ~500 ml/h during exertion).
Avoid compulsive redosing which sharply escalates cardiotoxicity and hyperthermia.
Never combine with other stimulants, MAOIs, or decongestants.
Monitor blood pressure and body temperature, and ensure adequate recovery intervals.

name: Aspirin
addictionPotential: not habit-forming (no recreational or diversion potential)
toxicities: acute kidney injury and renal toxicity
increased cardiovascular thrombotic risk with high doses or prolonged use
summary:
Aspirin is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID / AINS) used to treat pain, fever, and inflammation. Salicylate analgesic, antipyretic, anti-inflammatory, and irreversible platelet aggregation inhibitor (75-160 mg Kardégic for cardiovascular prevention; 300-1000 mg for pain/fever). Strict dosing intervals must be respected, and two different NSAIDs must never be combined.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to ibuprofen and modern NSAIDs, aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) irreversibly acetylates platelet COX-1 for the lifetime of the platelet (7-10 days), providing cardioprotective antiplatelet prophylaxis but presenting higher gastrointestinal mucosal bleeding risks and Reye's syndrome contraindications in children.
effectsSummary: Analgesic (pain relief), antipyretic (fever reduction), and anti-inflammatory effects via COX-1/COX-2 prostaglandin inhibition. No psychoactive or euphoric effect.
dosageRemark: STRICT INTERVAL: Wait at least 4 hours (for 500 mg) to 6 hours (for 1000 mg) between two intakes. The 'Heavy' threshold (1000 mg) represents the maximum single unit dose per intake. Maximum cumulative daily dose: 3000 mg/24h in adults (2000 mg/24h in elderly). Always take with food or a full glass of water to protect the stomach.
generalRisks: Stomach pain, heartburn, nausea, peptic ulcers, gastrointestinal bleeding, fluid retention, elevated blood pressure, and acute renal impairment (especially when dehydrated). Can trigger severe bronchospasm in aspirin-sensitive asthma. Must NOT be used during pregnancy (especially from the 6th month onward) or during bacterial infections like varicella/streptococcal infections without medical advice.
longtermRisks: Chronic or repeated high-dose use causes gastric/duodenal ulcers, gastrointestinal perforation, chronic kidney disease (analgesic nephropathy), hypertension, and elevated risk of myocardial infarction or stroke.
saferUse: Strictly wait at least 4 hours (for 500 mg) to 6 hours (for 1000 mg) between two doses and never exceed 3000 mg/24h in adults (2000 mg/24h in elderly) in 24 hours.
Never exceed 1000 mg in a single intake.
NEVER combine with another NSAID (e.g., Ibuprofen, Ketoprofen, Naproxen, Diclofenac, Aspirin at anti-inflammatory doses, Celecoxib).
Take during a meal with a large glass of water and stay well hydrated to protect your kidneys and stomach.
Avoid combining with Lithium (causes severe Lithium poisoning), oral corticosteroids, anticoagulants, or heavy alcohol use.

name: Atomoxetine

tolerance.full: full ADHD efficacy develops over 2 - 6 weeks
tolerance.zero: can be tapered without stimulant crash

addictionPotential: not habit-forming (non-stimulant ADHD medication with zero dopamine release in nucleus accumbens)
toxicities: 5-10x plasma spike with CYP2D6 inhibitors (Fluoxetine, Paroxetine, Bupropion)
summary:
Atomoxetine (Strattera) is a selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (NRI) non-stimulant medication prescribed for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children and adults.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Atomoxetine (Strattera) is a selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (NRI) approved for ADHD. Unlike psychostimulants, it does not elevate dopamine in the nucleus accumbens, possessing zero abuse liability or controlled substance scheduling.
effectsSummary: Gradually improves sustained attention, executive control, and emotional regulation across 24 hours without acute dopaminergic euphoria or abuse liability.
dosageRemark: DAILY SCHEDULE: Taken once every 24 hours in the morning (or split morning and late afternoon with food to reduce nausea). The 'Heavy' threshold (100 mg) is the strict maximum single and daily adult dose.
generalRisks: Nausea, decreased appetite, dry mouth, fatigue or insomnia, sweating, urinary hesitation, erection/ejaculation changes, increased heart rate (+5-10 bpm) and blood pressure, and rare liver injury.
longtermRisks: Sustained blood pressure/heart rate elevation (check vitals periodically); rare hepatotoxicity (stop if jaundice/dark urine occurs).
saferUse: Take with breakfast to prevent stomach upset and never exceed 100 mg/24h.
NEVER combine with MAOIs (14-day washout mandatory).
CAUTION: Fluoxetine, Paroxetine, and Bupropion strongly inhibit CYP2D6 and increase Atomoxetine exposure several-fold — dose adjustment and cardiovascular monitoring are required!

name: Ayahuasca
addictionPotential: not habit-forming
toxicities: LD50 is around 50 times a regular dose
summary:
A concoction made of two or more plants that contain at least an MAOI and DMT, the combination of which allows the DMT to work orally. Typically associated to south american cultures. Also, sometimes approximated synthetically by taking an external MAOI with extracted DMT. Causes intense, spiritually orientated hallucinogenic experiences.

⚖️ Comparative profile: A traditional Amazonian botanical entheogen combining DMT-rich plants (Psychotria viridis) with MAO-inhibiting Banisteriopsis caapi vines (harmine/harmaline), orally activating DMT for 4-6 hours of intense visionary journeying and purging.
effectsSummary: Intense sensory and visual alterations, altered perception of space and time, emotional amplification, deep introspection, and potential ego dissolution.
saferUse: Strictly respect Set & Setting (positive mindset, calm and secure physical environment).
Always have a trusted, sober tripsitter present during the experience.
Never combine with lithium, tramadol, or MAOI/SSRI antidepressants.
Test substances with colorimetric reagents prior to use and start with a low test dose.

name: Baclofen

tolerance.full: within a couple of days of continuous use

addictionPotential: moderately physically and psychologically addictive
toxicities: potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like alcohol, benzodiazepines or opioids
summary:
Baclofen (Lioresal, Baclocur) is a centrally acting muscle relaxant and selective GABA-B receptor agonist, prescribed for muscle spasticity and alcohol use disorder.

Comparative effects: Direct GABA analogue closely related to Phenibut, but with 5 to 10 times higher potency and near-exclusive selectivity for GABA-B receptors (without significant alpha-2-delta calcium channel subunit binding at therapeutic doses). Noticeably more muscle-relaxing and sedating, but less euphoric than phenibut or pregabalin.
dosageRemark: Warning: Strictly adhere to prescribed medical dosing (typically divided into 3 daily doses). NEVER discontinue baclofen abruptly due to high risk of severe acute withdrawal syndrome (delirium, hallucinations, seizures, malignant hyperthermia, muscle rigidity). Any reduction must be tapered gradually over several weeks.
effectsSummary: Central nervous system sedation, marked anxiolysis, muscle relaxation, psychomotor slowing, and reduction of inhibitions.
saferUse: LETHAL DANGER: Never combine with alcohol, opioids, or other respiratory depressants.
Space out intake to prevent rapid tolerance and potentially life-threatening withdrawal.
Do not drive or operate heavy machinery while under the influence.
When discontinuing prolonged use, always taper gradually to avoid seizures.

name: Benzydamine
summary:
NSAID with local anesthetic and analgesic properties, similar to ibuprofen or naproxen. Sometimes abused in overdose with reported delirant and stimulant effects.

⚖️ Comparative profile: A topical NSAID throat medication, benzydamine abused orally at supra-therapeutic doses (500-1000 mg) triggers bizarre visual deliriant hallucinations characterized by persistent light tracers and insectoid illusions, accompanied by severe caustic gastric distress.
effectsSummary: Central muscarinic receptor antagonism causing true delirious hallucinations (inability to distinguish visions from reality), total amnesia, extreme xerostomia, hyperthermia, and pupil paralysis.
saferUse: EXTREME PHYSICAL AND PSYCHIATRIC HAZARD: Recreational use is strongly discouraged.
Mandatory presence of a sober, capable tripsitter to physically prevent wandering into traffic or self-harm.
High risk of severe anticholinergic toxicity requiring emergency medical hospitalization (physostigmine).
Never redose: erratic absorption kinetics frequently lead to fatal systemic poisoning.

name: Biperiden

tolerance.full: develops with repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately habit-forming (documented anticholinergic mood/deliriant diversion)
toxicities: central anticholinergic syndrome (delirium, tachycardia, hyperthermia, urinary retention)
summary:
Biperiden (Akineton) is a central muscarinic M1 antagonist used for Parkinson's disease and antipsychotic-induced extrapyramidal symptoms (akathisia, acute dystonia), with documented diversion potential at supratherapeutic doses.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Biperiden (Akineton) is a centrally active antimuscarinic agent frontline for reversing acute neuroleptic-induced extrapyramidal dystonias (spasms of neck, tongue, eyes) and treating drug-induced parkinsonism.
effectsSummary: Relieves parkinsonian rigidity/tremor at 1-4 mg; higher diverted doses produce euphoria/agitation followed by confusion, memory loss, and deliriant hallucinations.
dosageRemark: DIVERSION-ADAPTED DOSAGES: Standard therapeutic single intake is 1-2 mg (up to 4 mg; max medical daily dose 12-16 mg divided). Single intakes >= 8-12 mg ('Strong'/'Heavy') provoke pronounced anticholinergic toxicity and delirium.
generalRisks: Dry mouth, mydriasis/blurred vision, urinary retention, tachycardia, drowsiness or agitation, disorientation, and hallucinations.
longtermRisks: Cognitive decline with chronic high anticholinergic burden and rebound symptoms on abrupt cessation.
saferUse: Avoid combining with TCAs, sedative phenothiazines (Tercian, Nozinan), first-generation antihistamines, Nefopam, or other anticholinergics.

name: Bromantane
summary:
An unusual stimulant and anxiolytic drug with dopamine and serotonin reuptake inhibition properties. Infamously used as a doping agent in the 1996 Olympics. There are some concerns it may exacerbate the underlying causes of Alzheimer's disease.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to typical stimulants, bromantane uniquely combines non-jittery dopaminergic energy with non-sedating anxiolytic properties.
effectsSummary: Heightened alertness and concentration, dopaminergic euphoria, physical and mental energy surge, increased heart rate, and appetite suppression.
saferUse: Stay hydrated regularly (water or electrolyte drinks, ~500 ml/h during exertion).
Avoid compulsive redosing which sharply escalates cardiotoxicity and hyperthermia.
Never combine with other stimulants, MAOIs, or decongestants.
Monitor blood pressure and body temperature, and ensure adequate recovery intervals.

name: Bromazepam
toxicities: potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like alcohol or opioids
summary:
A benzodiazepine drug with a medium-long duration, developed by Roche in the 1960s. Has primarily anxiolytic properties. May cause lowered inhibitions and amnesia in high doses.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to alprazolam and oxazepam, bromazepam (Lexotan) is an intermediate-potency benzodiazepine (6 mg equals 10 mg diazepam) with a 15-to-20 hour half-life. It delivers stronger skeletal muscle relaxation than alprazolam with lower incidence of anterograde amnesia than lorazepam, making it a balanced daytime anxiolytic.
effectsSummary: Central nervous system sedation, marked anxiolysis, muscle relaxation, psychomotor slowing, and reduction of inhibitions.
saferUse: LETHAL DANGER: Never combine with alcohol, opioids, or other respiratory depressants.
Space out intake to prevent rapid tolerance and potentially life-threatening withdrawal.
Do not drive or operate heavy machinery while under the influence.
When discontinuing prolonged use, always taper gradually to avoid seizures.

name: Bromazolam
summary:
A rather novel Benzodiazepine that is structurally quite close to Alprazolam.

⚖️ Comparative profile: As the brominated analogue of alprazolam (Xanax), bromazolam is an unregulated designer benzodiazepine sharing alprazolam's potency but with a longer 8-12 hour duration and heavier somatic sedation, significantly elevating risks of amnesic blackouts and polysubstance overdose.
effectsSummary: Central nervous system sedation, marked anxiolysis, muscle relaxation, psychomotor slowing, and reduction of inhibitions.
saferUse: LETHAL DANGER: Never combine with alcohol, opioids, or other respiratory depressants.
Space out intake to prevent rapid tolerance and potentially life-threatening withdrawal.
Do not drive or operate heavy machinery while under the influence.
When discontinuing prolonged use, always taper gradually to avoid seizures.

name: Bromo-DragonFLY

tolerance.full: almost immediately after ingestion

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
toxicities: one can easily overdose if this substance is not measured correctly
summary:
A psychedelic phenethylamine and benzofuran that is very potent and has a long duration. Was briefly sold as "2C-B-FLY" in 2005/6 and has lead to multiple deaths.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to DOB, Bromo-DragonFLY is extremely hazardous: its effects can persist for up to 3 full days (48-72h), carrying fatal risks of severe vasoconstriction and limb necrosis.
effectsSummary: Intense sensory and visual alterations, altered perception of space and time, emotional amplification, deep introspection, and potential ego dissolution.
saferUse: Strictly respect Set & Setting (positive mindset, calm and secure physical environment).
Always have a trusted, sober tripsitter present during the experience.
Never combine with lithium, tramadol, or MAOI/SSRI antidepressants.
Test substances with colorimetric reagents prior to use and start with a low test dose.

name: Bufotenin

tolerance.full: almost immediately after ingestion

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary:
Bufotenin (5-HO-DMT) is a naturally occurring tryptamine psychedelic found in Colorado River toad secretions and the seeds of South American trees (Anadenanthera colubrina/peregrina, used in Yopo and Vilca snuffs). It acts as a potent 5-HT2A and 5-HT1A receptor agonist.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to 5-MeO-DMT and N,N-DMT, bufotenin carries a substantially heavier peripheral physical load, marked by facial flushing, intense chest pressure, and nausea, accompanied by richly intricate, colorful geometric closed-eye visions.
effectsSummary: Intricate closed-eye geometric hallucinations, somatic heaviness, flushed skin sensation, altered time perception, and emotional awe.
dosageRemark: Vaporized freebase: 5-15 mg. Traditional Yopo snuff prepared with calcium hydroxide: 50-100 mg insufflated.
generalRisks: Nausea, emesis, elevated blood pressure, facial paresthesia, and acute psychological anxiety.
longtermRisks: Precipitation of latent psychiatric illness, severe distress in unprepared users.
saferUse: Separate pure alkaloid from cardioactive toad venom bufadienolides.
Ensure a sober tripsitter is present in a calm setting.

name: Buprenorphine

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary:
A semi-synthetic opioid analgesic also known as subutex. Often administered as Butrans patches, or in combination with Naloxone as Suboxone, a heroin replacement therapy drug. Will cause withdrawals if you have an opioid tolerance and don't wait long enough (typically around 48 hours) before taking this.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to methadone and full-agonist opioids, buprenorphine (Subutex, Suboxone) is a partial mu-opioid agonist with extraordinarily high receptor binding affinity and an intrinsic ceiling effect on respiratory depression, making unadulterated overdose rare. However, administering it too soon after a full agonist precipitates violent immediate withdrawal.
effectsSummary: Like all opiates, buprenorphine has analgesic and cough-irritant effects. However, its euphoric and sedative properties are less pronounced than those of other opioids, which is why it is also used for substitution treatment. Buprenorphine is a partial agonist. This means that, for safety reasons, only a submaximal effect is elicited. After a certain dose, a saturation effect (ceiling effect) occurs, which prevents a further increase in the effect. This makes the active ingredient so relevant for substitution treatments, as withdrawal symptoms can be alleviated and overdoses avoided.
dosageRemark:
From 16 mg, the saturation effect (ceiling effect) takes effect and no more effect enhancement is felt.
When consuming for the first time, low doses should be used, as the risk of respiratory arrest is increased.
generalRisks:
The side effects are less pronounced than with other opioids. Nevertheless, fatigue, constipation, drowsiness, sweating, nausea, vomiting, insomnia and irritability may occur. Buprenorphine has a lower risk of respiratory depression, which is why it is considered comparatively safe.
Overdoses with buprenorphine are difficult to treat with the opioid antagonist naloxone due to its high binding to the μ-opioid receptor. Therefore, agents from the group of respiratory stimulants (such as doxapram) are used.
longtermRisks: Unlike other opioids, the active ingredient floods on slowly, which is why the risk of dependence is considered lower.
saferUse: Opioids are highly effective drugs that should only be used for a limited time and at best under medical supervision.
Start with a low dose and wait for the effect and tolerance before adding more. Do not exceed the maximum daily dose.

If you inject opioids, dose even more carefully, as the range between desired effect (rush) and dangerous overdose is even more difficult to assess. Avoid injecting fentanyl; the risk of overdose is particularly high. Always use new (clean and sterile) injection material! Never exchange syringes, filters, water, disinfection swabs to avoid transmission of hepatitis and HIV.
Do not rely on dosage information from colleagues who regularly use opioids. Due to habituation or dependence, their doses are much higher and can be fatal for new users.
Take longer breaks (at least several days) between consumption.
After a period of abstinence, take a much lower dose! The usual dose before the abstinence phase can otherwise quickly have life-threatening consequences.

The simultaneous consumption of depressant substances such as alcohol, ketamine, GHB/GBL, nitrous oxide, benzodiazepines and/or other opioids is dangerous as there is an increased risk of vomiting and unconsciousness. The risk of suffocation is high!
Refrain from citrus fruits (especially grapefruit) before or during consumption. The combination can lead to an increase in the effect of the opiate and/or to respiratory depression.

name: Bupropion

tolerance.full: develops to acute stimulant effects within days

addictionPotential: low medically, moderately habit-forming when diverted/insufflated ('poor man's cocaine')
toxicities: HIGH DOSE-DEPENDENT SEIZURE RISK (convulsions occur rapidly above 300-450 mg oral or when crushed/insufflated!)
tachycardia, hypertension, and cardiac conduction delays in overdose
summary:
Bupropion (Wellbutrin, Zyban) is a substituted cathinone norepinephrine-dopamine reuptake inhibitor (NDRI) and nicotinic antagonist prescribed for major depression, seasonal affective disorder, ADHD, and smoking cessation. Sometimes diverted via crushing/insufflation for short-lived stimulation, which bypasses slow absorption and carries an extreme risk of sudden generalized seizures.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to serotonergic antidepressants, bupropion (Wellbutrin) is a norepinephrine-dopamine reuptake inhibitor (NDRI). It causes zero sexual dysfunction or weight gain (frequently promoting weight loss and smoking cessation), but carries an intrinsic dose-dependent risk of lowering the seizure threshold.
effectsSummary: Mild wakefulness, motivation, appetite suppression, and reduced nicotine cravings medically; jittery stimulation, anxiety, nasal burning, tachycardia, and high convulsion risk when diverted.
dosageRemark: DIVERSION-ADAPTED DOSAGES & SEIZURE WARNING: Medically, a single immediate-release oral dose must NEVER exceed 150 mg (with at least 6-8 hours between doses; max 300-450 mg/day divided or XL). Single oral doses >= 300-450 mg ('Strong'/'Heavy') or crushing/snorting tablets cause dangerous peak plasma spikes with high seizure incidence! Potent CYP2D6 inhibitor.
generalRisks: Dose-dependent generalized tonic-clonic seizures (contraindicated in epilepsy, bulimia/anorexia, or abrupt alcohol/benzo withdrawal!), insomnia, anxiety, tremor, dry mouth, sweating, hypertension, and severe nasal mucosa necrosis if snorted.
longtermRisks: Hypertension, chronic insomnia/irritability, and lowered seizure threshold.
saferUse: Medically, wait at least 6 to 8 hours between immediate-release 150 mg intakes (24 hours for XL) and never crush or split sustained-release tablets.
Avoid insufflation: snorting Bupropion causes intense nasal damage and rapid peak concentrations that frequently provoke sudden seizures.
NEVER combine with MAOIs, Tramadol, Nefopam, stimulants (Cocaine, Amphetamines, MDMA), or heavy Alcohol / abrupt Benzo withdrawal (extreme seizure risk!).

name: Buspirone
addictionPotential: not habit-forming (no recreational potential or withdrawal syndrome)
dosageRemark: STRICT 8-12h SCHEDULE: Taken 2 to 3 times daily consistently either always with food or always without food (food doubles bioavailability!). The 'Heavy' threshold (30 mg) is the maximum single unit intake (maximum 60 mg/24h divided). Full anxiolytic effect takes 2-4 weeks.
summary:
Buspirone (Buspar) is a non-benzodiazepine anxiolytic acting as a high-affinity partial agonist at serotonin 5-HT1A receptors. Unlike benzodiazepines, it is devoid of sedative, anticonvulsant, or muscle-relaxant properties, causing neither cognitive impairment nor physical dependence or withdrawal upon discontinuation.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to immediate-acting benzodiazepines, buspirone (Buspar) is a 5-HT1A partial agonist with zero GABAergic activity. It causes no sedation, motor impairment, or withdrawal, but requires continuous daily dosing for 2 to 4 weeks to achieve therapeutic anxiolysis.
effectsSummary: Central nervous system sedation, marked anxiolysis, muscle relaxation, psychomotor slowing, and reduction of inhibitions.
saferUse: LETHAL DANGER: Never combine with alcohol, opioids, or other respiratory depressants.
Space out intake to prevent rapid tolerance and potentially life-threatening withdrawal.
Do not drive or operate heavy machinery while under the influence.
When discontinuing prolonged use, always taper gradually to avoid seizures.

name: Butylone

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary:
Empathogen and stimulant of the cathinone class.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to methylone, butylone is more physically stimulating and less empathic, with a shorter plateau.
effectsSummary: Massive release of serotonin and dopamine, heightened empathy, deep feelings of interpersonal connection, tactile euphoria, and moderate physical stimulation.
saferUse: Respect the 6 to 12 weeks spacing rule between sessions to allow complete serotonin replenishment.
Stay hydrated reasonably (~250-500 ml water/electrolytes per hour during exertion to avoid hyponatremia).
Never combine with antidepressants (SSRIs, SNRIs, MAOIs) due to lethal serotonin syndrome risk.
Monitor body temperature closely and take frequent breaks in cool, ventilated areas.

name: Caffeine

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: develop with regular consumption, leading to cravings and withdrawal effects upon sudden cessation, but has low abuse potential
toxicities: The LD50 of caffeine in humans is dependent on individual sensitivity, but is estimated to be about 150 to 200 milligrams per kilogram of body mass or roughly 80 to 100 cups of coffee for an average adult
summary:
Caffeine is a a CNS stimulant, and also the most widely used psychoactive substance in the world. It is legal and unregulated in most parts of the world, and is found in many commonly sold products. It has a good safety profile, though regular heavy use can cause physical dependence and contribute to certain medical conditions.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to major dopaminergic stimulants (amphetamines, cocaine), caffeine does not force direct dopamine release, acting instead as a competitive antagonist at adenosine A1 and A2A receptors. It blunts perceived fatigue without inducing cognitive disinhibition or intense euphoria, remaining pharmacologically mild compared to prescription stimulants.
effectsSummary: Caffeine makes you awake, speeds up the heartbeat and temporarily increases mental performance. In higher doses (approx. 300 - 600 mg = approx. 8 cups of coffee) it produces euphoria.
generalRisks: Caffeine dehydrates the body (dehydration). At very high doses: sweating, fluttering of the heart, urge to urinate, cardiac arrhythmia, strong disturbances of perception, trembling, nervousness and sleep disturbances.
longtermRisks: With long-term, regular and high-dose caffeine consumption (also with coffee or energy drinks), there is a risk of dependence with physical symptoms. Possible withdrawal symptoms: headaches, nervousness, fatigue, vomiting and even movement and concentration disorders. The acidity of coffee also promotes the formation of stomach ulcers in the long term. Continuous consumption of caffeine with painkillers can lead to severe kidney damage with life-threatening complications.
saferUse: Do not consume pure caffeine, rather drink coffee or guarana. In addition to caffeine, energy drinks also contain a lot of sugar.
Pure (synthetic) caffeine in powder form is often mixed with amphetamine and sold as speed.

name: Cannabidiol
addictionPotential: low abuse potential
toxicities: well-tolerated and shows little to no toxicity
summary:
Cannabidiol (CBD, Epidiolex) is the major non-intoxicating phytocannabinoid in Cannabis sativa. Unlike THC, it does not agonize CB1 receptors directly (acting as a negative allosteric modulator) and produces no psychoactive intoxication, memory disruption, or perceptual changes. It is clinically approved for refractory childhood epilepsies (Dravet and Lennox-Gastaut syndromes) and widely used for anxiety and pain.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to THC, CBD is completely non-intoxicating and non-addictive, inducing neither paranoia nor tachycardia. In fact, co-administration with THC counteracts THC-induced psychotomimetic effects, memory blunting, and anxiety via CB1 allosteric modulation.
effectsSummary: Mild somatic relaxation, reduced physiological anxiety, muscle loosening, anti-inflammatory relief, and improved sleep latency without cognitive impairment.
dosageRemark: Typical wellness oral doses: 20-50 mg. Clinical anti-epileptic protocols: 5-20 mg/kg/day under specialist care.
generalRisks: Mild drowsiness, dry mouth, reduced blood pressure, and gastrointestinal upset at elevated doses.
longtermRisks: Potent inhibition of cytochrome P450 enzymes (CYP3A4, CYP2C19), substantially elevating serum levels of co-prescribed anticonvulsants, blood thinners, and statins.
saferUse: Select laboratory-tested sublingual oils free from heavy metals and pesticide contaminants.
Consult a physician if taking prescription medications metabolized by CYP450.
Consume alongside dietary fats to dramatically improve oral bioavailability.

name: Cannabis

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately habit-forming
summary:
A common and widely used psychoactive plant, which is beginning to enjoy legal status for medical and even recreational use in some parts of the world. Usually smoked or eaten, primary effects are relaxation and an affinity towards food - a state described as being 'stoned.'

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to full-agonist synthetic cannabinoids ('Spice'), natural herbal cannabis delivers THC as a partial CB1 agonist operating within a natural safety ceiling, balanced by modulatory CBD and therapeutic terpenes ('entourage effect') that prevent severe receptor saturation and acute toxicity.
effectsSummary:
The most important of a total of 400 active ingredients are THC (tetrahydrocannabinol) and CBD (cannabidiol), with THC being responsible for the majority of the psychoactive effects felt. CBD also has analgesic, sedative and narcotic effects.
The main cannabis active substances THC and CBD dock in the body to the cannabinoid receptors CB1 and CB2. This activates the body's own messenger substance endocannabinoid. This has a relaxing, appetite-stimulating, calming and pain-relieving effect. Feelings are intensified, serenity and/or groundless cheerfulness set in. The experience of time is changed, usually slowed down. In high doses and CBD-free varieties, cannabis can have hallucinogenic effects. Since it is usually consumed together with tobacco, the joint-typical effect is an interaction between cannabis and tobacco. This usually leads to an intensification and prolongation of the effect, as tobacco inhibits the degradation of endocannabinoids.
dosageRemark:
The main active ingredient content and the ratio of THC to CBD differ greatly depending on the product. Therefore, the dosage is difficult to determine. Hashish contains on average more THC and mostly CBD. Outdoor weed varieties contain less THC and less CBD, while indoor weed varieties contain mainly THC and rarely CBD.
CYP2C9 genotype affects THC sensitivity significantly: Subjects with the *3/*3 genotype had 3-fold higher THC levels in their blood than subjects with the *1/*1 genotype. Those subjects with one copy of each gene (*1/*3) had intermediate THC levels that were about 2-fold higher than subjects with *1/*1.
generalRisks:
Increase in heart rate and pulse rate, reddening of the eyes, dry mouth, excessive feeling of hunger (binge eating), dizziness, nausea and vomiting, general impairment of the ability to concentrate and remember during intoxication, as well as unpleasant intensification of feelings or introversion, drifting into one's own world of thoughts. At high doses and varieties with little CBD, circulatory problems up to circulatory collapse, in the worst case paranoia and depressive moods may occur.
When consuming cannabis products, the dosage is more difficult to estimate, making the risks and side effects more unpredictable.
longtermRisks:
With frequent and regular use, there is a risk of psychological dependence. Symptoms of mild physical dependence may also manifest themselves; in the case of sudden abstinence, sweating, hot/cold shivers, loss of appetite and difficulty falling asleep as well as irritability are possible. In the case of chronic use, there is a danger of loss of reality; latent psychoses can be triggered. In addition, long-term impairment of short-term memory and the ability to motivate oneself is possible.
Smoking, especially when mixed with tobacco, increases susceptibility to respiratory problems (bronchitis, tracheitis, pneumonia, etc.) when consumed chronically. Due to the deeper inhalation as well as poorer filtering methods (such as cardboard filters), joints are more harmful to the lungs than cigarettes.
saferUse: Currently, there are many misdeclared and stretched cannabis products in circulation. Therefore, if possible, use cannabis drug checking and follow the safer use instructions for synthetic cannabinoids.
When using new cannabis products for the first time, try a small amount first to see if you notice any suspicious effects (e.g. rapid onset of effects, unusually strong effects, etc.).
Cannabis products temporarily affect the ability to remember and concentrate. Consumption at work and at school is therefore not advisable.
When smoking, make sure you use good filtering methods (activated carbon filters) or use a vaporizer.

Since cannabis products are used mixed with tobacco, there is also a tobacco addiction with daily use. There are some tobacco substitutes such as damiana or coltsfoot that you can use instead of tobacco.

Eating or drinking cannabis products is easy on the lungs, but the effects are stronger and more unpredictable than smoking. The risk of very high and highly psychoactive doses is high. Carefully approach the right dose, don't add more right away!
Since the brain is developing until the age of 25, you should not use regularly until that age. You are more likely to be exposed to side effects and long-term risks from cannabis use.
Do not consume if you are not well, latent psychoses could be triggered.
In the case of mental illness, cannabis can aggravate the course of the disease or lead to relapses.
Cannabis use should be avoided in cases of lung disease and existing heart conditions or heart disease.

name: Carbamazepine

summary:

NEVER consume Grapefruit juice (inhibits CYP3A4 and spikes Carbamazepine to toxic levels!).
