Requires mandatory white blood cell monitoring (agranulocytosis risk) and carries seizure, myocarditis, and severe interaction risks.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Clozapine (Clozaril) remains the gold standard, most efficacious antipsychotic for treatment-resistant schizophrenia, uniquely proven to reduce suicidal behavior. However, its life-threatening risk of agranulocytosis (1-2% incidence) mandates strict, non-negotiable lifetime hematologic blood monitoring.
effectsSummary: Dopamine D2 / serotonin receptor antagonism (or partial agonism) reducing hallucinations, delusions, mania, agitation, and psychedelic 5-HT2A/dopaminergic effects.
dosageRemark: STRICT SCHEDULE & SINGLE INTAKE CAP: Doses >200 mg/day (up to 600-900 mg/24h) MUST be divided; single intake should not exceed 200-300 mg due to dose-dependent seizure and orthostatic collapse risk! If missed for >48 hours, MUST re-titrate from 12.5 mg! The 'Heavy' threshold (300 mg) represents the maximum single unit oral intake. Never stop antipsychotic treatment abruptly without medical guidance.
generalRisks: Sedation or akathisia (inner restlessness), orthostatic hypotension, dizziness, weight gain, elevated prolactin, extrapyramidal stiffness/tremor, QT prolongation, and rare Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (high fever + muscle rigidity = medical emergency).
longtermRisks: Weight gain, insulin resistance/type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hyperprolactinemia, and tardive dyskinesia with chronic exposure.
saferUse: Respect your prescribed schedule and never exceed 300 mg in a single intake.
Avoid Alcohol, Opioids, and unprescribed sedatives (additive CNS depression and hypotension).
Avoid combining with other QT-prolonging medications (Escitalopram, Citalopram, Hydroxyzine, Methadone) without ECG monitoring.
Seek immediate emergency care if high fever, severe muscle stiffness, and confusion occur (Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome).

name: Cocaine

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: highly addictive with a high potential for abuse
toxicities: individuals have died from as little as 30 mg applied to mucous membranes, whereas addicts may tolerate up to 5 grams daily
summary:
A highly popular, short acting CNS stimulant that works by blocking the reuptake of dopamine, serotonin, and norepinephrine. It is known to increase euphoria, confidence, sex-drive, focus, body temperature, and heart rate. Cocaine can cause severe vasoconstriction and is known to be cardiotoxic and have a high potential for compulsive redosing and addiction.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to amphetamines which actively force monoamine release over 4-8 hours, cocaine operates strictly as a triple reuptake inhibitor (dopamine, norepinephrine, serotonin) with an ultra-short half-life (30-60 minutes). This fleeting duration generates intense compulsive redosing urge alongside unique sodium-channel blocking cardiotoxicity, predisposing to fatal arrhythmias and myocardial infarction.
effectsSummary:
The increased release and additional reuptake inhibition of the body's own neurotransmitters dopamine and noradrenaline lead to the suppression of tiredness, hunger and thirst, euphoria, feelings of increased performance, greatly increased self-confidence, urge to move, restlessness, talkativeness, elimination of inhibitions and fears, suppressed sense of pain, as well as increased willingness to take risks.

Coca leaves are known as "Mate de Coca" or dried leaves. These dried leaves contain about 0.5 to 2.5 % alkaloids, of which up to three quarters consist of cocaine. The leaves are chewed or drunk as tea. However, a psychoactive effect only occurs when they are taken in combination with a basic substance (e.g. lime or plant ash). This combination activates a hydrolysis, resulting in the alkaloid ecgonine. Ecgonine can be absorbed by the body and a slightly stimulating effect sets in. In contrast to cocaine, ecgonine has no dependence potential. If coca leaves are chewed without alkaline additives, they only have a numbing effect on the tongue. Coca leaves are used in South America mainly for medicinal purposes, e.g. to combat nausea or altitude sickness.
generalRisks:
Sleep disturbances, irritability, aggressiveness, exaggerated egocentrism up to "megalomania", decrease in critical and judgemental ability, anxiety and delusions, depression, memory/concentration disorders, shortness of breath, hyperactivity, nervous twitching, muscle cramps and tremors, high stress on the cardiovascular system due to constriction of the blood vessels, increase in heart rate, increased blood pressure and hypertensive crises. In extreme cases, overdose can lead to a heart attack or stroke.
When the effect wears off: exhaustion, depressive moods, irritability, feelings of anxiety and a strong urge to take the drug again ("craving").
longtermRisks:
Chronic use: psychological dependence. "Craving" (irresistible and uncontrollable desire to consume) can be triggered quickly by so-called trigger effects (situations, memories, people, etc., which are associated with consumption). Other long-term risks are anxiety disorders, personality changes such as reduced empathy, emotional coldness, exaggerated mistrust, depression, mental disorders with paranoid delusions and hallucinations, alteration of thought processes, permanent disturbances of short-term memory and intellectual abilities. Nerve damage, nervous twitching, seizures, alteration of movement patterns, damage to: Heart, liver, kidneys, lungs, skin, blood vessels and teeth. General weakening of the immune system, in extreme cases with necrosis (death of skin cells), liver damage due to the breakdown of toxins and the risk of kidney damage due to extender.
Chronic inflammation and damage to the nasal mucous membranes and nasal septum, which is difficult to heal. When smoking freebase and crack, damage to the lungs and respiratory tract is possible due to the deposition of combustion residues (ash residues). When injecting or smoking (freebase), the phenomenon of "dermatozoan madness" (the idea that there are worms or insects under the skin, perception of a tingling sensation under the skin) is known. Colloquially also called "cocaine worms/bugs"). This delusion leads to excessive scratching of the arms and/or legs, up to open injuries, which can lead to abscesses if hygiene is poor.
saferUse: Attention, very high risk of psychological dependence! Take breaks from using, especially if it is difficult for you.
Keep the dosage low and avoid frequent refilling!
Drink enough soft drinks and take breaks in the fresh air.
Eat healthy before and after consumption and do not consume on an empty stomach.
Follow the safer sniffing and safer sex rules.
Snorting is the lowest-risk form of use. Smoking crack and freebase as well as injecting increase the risks (no syringe exchange!).
People with pre-existing cardiovascular conditions, asthma, liver disease, hyperthyroidism and pregnant women should not use cocaine.
Do not combine cocaine with other stimulants or drugs that increase blood pressure.
Do not use cocaine if you have used ecstasy; this will cancel out the ecstasy effect.
Do not mix cocaine with alcohol; the mixture makes you aggressive and you risk alcohol poisoning.

name: Codeine

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
toxicities: potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like alcohol or benzodiazepines
summary:
Codeine is a weaker opioid used to treat mild to moderate pain and to relieve cough. In many countries it is available over the counter in combination with paracetamol, which can easily be extracted to retrieve near-pure codeine. For this reason, it is used widely as a recreational opioid. It is metabolised into morphine in the body at a rate of 5% mg for mg.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to tramadol and morphine, codeine is an inactive prodrug that requires hepatic bioactivation via cytochrome CYP2D6 into active morphine (~10% conversion rate). Poor metabolizers (~10% of Caucasians) experience zero pain relief, whereas ultra-rapid metabolizers risk severe, unpredictable opioid toxicity even at standard clinical doses.
effectsSummary: Codeine is converted into morphine in the body. Taking it has a pain-relieving, cough-irritating, calming, euphoric and aphrodisiac effect. An increase in self-confidence is also possible. It should be remembered, however, that the effect varies greatly depending on the individual metabolism. While some people react very sensitively to codeine, others feel no psychoactive effect at all.
dosageRemark: ⚠️ RELATIVE POTENCY (~0.15x Oral Morphine) & CYP2D6 CEILING: Prodrug converted to morphine via CYP2D6. Oral Heavy aligned at 240 mg (above 240-300 mg, CYP2D6 saturates and severe histamine release occurs).
generalRisks:
Dry mouth, headache, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, itching, constipation, difficulty in urinating, tiredness/sleepiness, decrease in respiratory rate up to a life-threatening respiratory depression. In men, erectile dysfunction may also occur.
There is a risk of psychological and physical dependence. In the case of chronic use, tolerance may develop, so that the dose must be progressively increased to achieve the desired effect. When discontinuing codeine after a phase of continuous use, withdrawal symptoms such as restlessness, stomach and/or leg cramps, cold shivers, trembling, profuse sweating and muscle spasms may appear. Due to the high dependence potential, withdrawal can be as painful and long-lasting as heroin withdrawal (!).
longtermRisks: In men, there may be a reduction in sexual desire (libido). In women, menstruation may be absent or irregular and sexual desire may be reduced. Other long-term risks include allergic reactions, sleep disturbances and dizziness. The dependence potential of codeine is lower than that of other opiates, but should still not be underestimated!
saferUse: Do not use codeine with other depressant substances such as alcohol, cannabis, sleeping pills, MAO inhibitors (such as antidepressants) or GHB/GBL.
Dose low and don't top up straight away - it may be that you don't get a high.
With Sizzurp: The mixture with carbonic acid and sugar makes the codeine more difficult to dose. In addition, the effect is much faster and more intense.
When codeine is injected or snorted, severe side effects and unintentional overdose can result.
Codeine is a medicinal product and should therefore only be taken with medical supervision.

name: Coluracetam

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: not addictive with a low potential for abuse
summary:
A nootropic drug of the racetam class, originally developed to treat Alzheimer's disease, it is currently being investigated as a treatment for major depressive disorder and generalised anxiety disorder. May be a modulator of the AMPA receptor. Limited recreational value.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to other racetams, coluracetam specifically enhances high-affinity choline uptake and often noticeably enriches perceived visual color saturation.
effectsSummary: Subtle cognitive enhancement, improved mental clarity, support of working memory, and neuroprotection without acute intoxication.
saferUse: Follow recommended physiological dosing guidelines and cycle periodic washout breaks.
Check hepatic and renal clearance pathways when co-administering with prescription medications.
Prioritize nutritional balance and consistent restorative sleep as the foundational baseline.

name: Creatine
addictionPotential: not habit-forming with a low potential for abuse
summary:
Creatine is an endogenous amino acid compound synthesized from glycine, arginine, and methionine, stored predominantly as phosphocreatine in skeletal muscle and the brain. It acts as a rapid cellular energy buffer by regenerating ATP during high-intensity cellular demands, fatigue, and neurological hypoxia.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to classical psychostimulants, creatine provides non-adrenergic bioenergetic support with zero tachycardia, anxiety, or addiction. It functions as an essential cellular nootropic that significantly enhances working memory and cognitive endurance, particularly in sleep-deprived individuals or vegans.
effectsSummary: Increased muscular explosive power, enhanced resistance to mental and physical fatigue, faster cognitive processing under sleep deficit.
dosageRemark: Standard daily dose: 3-5 g taken consistently with water or carbohydrates. Loading phases (20 g/day for 5 days) are optional.
generalRisks: Benign intracellular water retention, mild stomach discomfort if taken without enough liquid.
longtermRisks: Extensive decades-long clinical safety record. Completely harmless to renal function in healthy individuals.
saferUse: Maintain adequate daily hydration (2-2.5L water) to support cellular hydration.
Take consistently every day; benefits stem from tissue saturation over 2-3 weeks.

name: Cyamemazine

tolerance.full: develops to acute sedation with daily use

addictionPotential: low-to-moderate psychological habit formation (documented sedative/downer misuse and co-ingestion with benzos/alcohol/opioids)
toxicities: QT interval prolongation and Torsades de Pointes arrhythmia
severe orthostatic hypotension, anticholinergic syndrome, and respiratory/CNS depression when mixed with downers
summary:
Cyamemazine (Tercian) is a phenothiazine neuroleptic with potent 5-HT2A/2C, H1, muscarinic, and alpha-1 antagonism, very widely prescribed in France for severe acute/chronic anxiety, agitation, depression/psychosis, and alcohol/drug withdrawal. Frequently encountered in sedative poly-drug misuse.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Extensively utilized in French emergency psychiatry, cyamemazine (Tercian) is a phenothiazine neuroleptic uniquely combining potent, fast-acting sedative and anxiolytic relief comparable to high-potency benzodiazepines with antipsychotic action, devoid of classical benzodiazepine withdrawal.
effectsSummary: Rapid mental and physical sedation, anxiety suppression, muscle heaviness, dry mouth, postural dizziness, and strong blunting of stimulants/psychedelics.
dosageRemark: THERAPEUTIC & DIVERTED RANGE: Anxiolytic doses typically range from 12.5-50 mg per intake (25-100 mg/day divided); antipsychotic/high sedative doses reach 100-200+ mg. Intakes >= 100-200 mg ('Strong'/'Heavy') cause profound sedation, orthostatic collapse, anticholinergic toxicity, and cardiac QT prolongation.
generalRisks: Heavy sedation, orthostatic fainting, dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention, tachycardia, QT prolongation, photosensitivity, extrapyramidal symptoms, and Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome.
longtermRisks: Weight gain, metabolic syndrome, tardive dyskinesia, and chronic anticholinergic cognitive impairment.
saferUse: NEVER mix with Alcohol, Opioids (Methadone, Buprenorphine, Morphine, Codeine, Tramadol), Benzodiazepines, or GHB (severe CNS/respiratory depression & QT cardiac arrest risk!).
Avoid combining with QT-prolonging drugs (Escitalopram, Citalopram, Hydroxyzine, Amisulpride, Haloperidol) or strong anticholinergics (Artane, Lepticur, TCAs).
Rise slowly from sitting or lying positions to avoid sudden orthostatic fainting.

name: Cyclazodone

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

summary:
Cyclazodone is a synthetic central nervous system stimulant of the 4-oxazolidinone class, structurally related to thozalinone and pemoline. Developed in the 1960s, it functions primarily as an alert-promoting cognitive enhancer with favorable wakefulness properties.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to modafinil and amphetamine, cyclazodone provides smooth mental drive with low peripheral cardiovascular jitter, but its structural kinship with pemoline mandates strict caution regarding potential cumulative hepatotoxicity.
effectsSummary: Clean cognitive focus, sustained alertness, working memory facilitation, and mild mood elevation without jitteriness.
dosageRemark: Typical oral dose: 5-15 mg. Begin with 5 mg. Avoid daily administration.
generalRisks: Insomnia, mild appetite suppression, headache, and potential liver enzyme elevation.
longtermRisks: Theoretical hepatotoxicity (akin to pemoline), tolerance, and psychological habituation.
saferUse: Avoid daily dosing; cycle use carefully.
Regularly monitor liver function panels if used long-term.

name: Cyclobenzaprine
addictionPotential: not habit-forming
toxicities: cardiac arrhythmia and serotonin syndrome with MAOIs/serotonergics
summary:
Cyclobenzaprine (Flexeril) is a centrally acting skeletal muscle relaxant structurally homologous to tricyclic antidepressants (amitriptyline), carrying both sedative, anticholinergic, and serotonergic interaction risks.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Structurally analogous to tricyclic antidepressants (amitriptyline), cyclobenzaprine (Flexeril) relieves acute musculoskeletal spasms via brainstem motor pathways, while causing significant sedative and anticholinergic side effects.
effectsSummary: Relieves acute skeletal muscle spasms while causing strong drowsiness, dry mouth, fatigue, and mild anticholinergic effects.
dosageRemark: STRICT INTERVAL: Space intakes by at least 8 hours (taken up to 3 times daily). The 'Heavy' threshold (10 mg) is the maximum single unit dose per intake. Maximum daily dose: 30 mg/24h for <= 2-3 weeks.
generalRisks: Strong sedation, dry mouth, blurred vision, tachycardia, urinary retention, dizziness, and QT/conduction disturbances.
longtermRisks: Anticholinergic cognitive burden; intended for short 2-3 week acute courses.
saferUse: NEVER combine with MAOIs (within 14 days) or Tramadol, and use caution with SSRIs/SNRIs (serotonin syndrome & seizure risk).
Avoid Alcohol, Benzodiazepines, Opioids, and other anticholinergics.

name: Datura

tolerance.full: with repeated use

addictionPotential: mildly addictive with a high potential for adverse side effects such as psychosis
summary:
A family of plants containing various Tropane alkaloids. Produces long-lasting deliriant effects including very realistic and often unpleasant hallucinations along with short-term amnesia. Datura plants are toxic to humans, and potency varies greatly from plant-to-plant, making the drug extremely difficult to dose safely. Not typically regarded as recreational.

⚖️ Comparative profile: A notoriously poisonous solanaceous botanical containing scopolamine and atropine, Datura induces absolute anticholinergic delirium where hallucinations are indistinguishable from reality. Possessing zero safety margin, it presents severe risks of fatal hyperthermia, cardiac arrest, and prolonged psychosis.
effectsSummary: Central muscarinic receptor antagonism causing true delirious hallucinations (inability to distinguish visions from reality), total amnesia, extreme xerostomia, hyperthermia, and pupil paralysis.
saferUse: EXTREME PHYSICAL AND PSYCHIATRIC HAZARD: Recreational use is strongly discouraged.
Mandatory presence of a sober, capable tripsitter to physically prevent wandering into traffic or self-harm.
High risk of severe anticholinergic toxicity requiring emergency medical hospitalization (physostigmine).
Never redose: erratic absorption kinetics frequently lead to fatal systemic poisoning.

name: Deschloroetizolam

tolerance.full: within a couple of days of continuous use

addictionPotential: extremely physically and psychologically addictive
toxicities: potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like alcohol or opioids
summary:
A Thienodiazepine which is close to its parent compound, Etizolam, whilst being significantly weaker and longer lasting.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to etizolam, deschloroetizolam is about half as potent by weight, but lasts slightly longer with milder sedation.
effectsSummary: Central nervous system sedation, marked anxiolysis, muscle relaxation, psychomotor slowing, and reduction of inhibitions.
saferUse: LETHAL DANGER: Never combine with alcohol, opioids, or other respiratory depressants.
Space out intake to prevent rapid tolerance and potentially life-threatening withdrawal.
Do not drive or operate heavy machinery while under the influence.
When discontinuing prolonged use, always taper gradually to avoid seizures.

name: Deschloroketamine

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary:
A novel analogue of Ketamine which is much more potent and has a longer duration.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to Ketamine, DCK is 3-5 times more potent by dose, with triple the duration (3-5 hours vs 1 hour) and a much heavier, numbing physical dissociation.
effectsSummary: Somatosensory and cognitive detachment, bodily anesthesia, proprioceptive distortions, double vision, floating sensations, and deep introspective immersion (hole states).
saferUse: LETHAL DANGER: Never combine with CNS depressants (alcohol, opioids, benzodiazepines).
Always consume while seated or lying down in a safe space to prevent falls and physical injuries.
Space uses out (at least 2-3 weeks apart) to prevent urinary bladder ulceration and cognitive blunting.
Ensure a sober tripsitter is present to prevent airway obstruction or aspirational risk.

name: Desomorphine
summary:
Desomorphine (Permonid) is a semi-synthetic opioid analogue of morphine first synthesized in 1932. While clinically approved in Switzerland historically, it gained worldwide notoriety as 'Krokodil', an illicit street preparation synthesized from codeine, iodine, and red phosphorus. Toxic unreacted solvents in street batches cause horrific tissue necrosis, phlebitis, and gangrene.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to pure morphine, pharmaceutical desomorphine is 8 to 10 times more potent by weight with high lipid solubility, delivering an instantaneous rush but a remarkably brief duration of action (1 to 2 hours), precipitating an extraordinarily rapid cycle of physical withdrawal and compulsive redosing.
effectsSummary: Rapid and profound analgesia, heavy stuporous sedation, intense fleeting euphoria, pinpoint miosis, and rapid respiratory depression.
dosageRemark: ⚠️ LETHAL POTENCY & TOXICITY: Active threshold is merely 1-3 mg. Clandestine street batches ('Krokodil') cause catastrophic systemic damage.
generalRisks: Fatal respiratory arrest, rapid overdose, profound sedation, hypotension, sepsis, and irreversible soft-tissue necrosis.
longtermRisks: Catastrophic physical and psychological opioid addiction, rapid venous destruction, gangrene requiring limb amputation, and early mortality.
saferUse: NEVER inject street-cooked desomorphine ('Krokodil'): chemical impurities cause immediate caustic necrosis.
Keep Naloxone within immediate reach.
Never use alone or mix with alcohol, benzodiazepines, or other depressants.

name: Desoxypipradrol

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary:
Desoxypipradrol (2-DPMP) is a synthetic stimulant developed in the 1950s as a pipradrol analogue. Acting as a potent NDRI, it is distinguished by an extraordinarily prolonged elimination half-life, yielding active central stimulation lasting 24 to 48 hours from a single dose.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to methylphenidate and amphetamines, 2-DPMP is infamous for its relentless duration. A single dose of 5-10 mg prevents sleep for up to two days, frequently precipitating acute paranoid psychosis and severe hallucinations when users redose during its deceptively slow onset.
effectsSummary: Unrelenting 24-48 hour wakefulness, continuous physical arousal, absolute suppression of fatigue, and severe sleep deprivation.
dosageRemark: ⚠️ EXTREME 24-48 HOUR DURATION: Active at micro-doses (1-5 mg). NEVER REDOSE. Extremely high risk of sleep-deprivation psychosis.
generalRisks: Prolonged insomnia, severe paranoid delirium, visual hallucinations, cardiovascular strain, and panic.
longtermRisks: Severe psychiatric breaks, physical exhaustion, and potential self-harm under paranoid delusions.
saferUse: Strongly advised to avoid this substance due to extreme duration.
If consumed, keep doses under 2 mg, never redose, and keep rescue benzodiazepines/antipsychotics accessible.

name: DET

tolerance.full: almost immediately after ingestion

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary:
A surprisingly uncommon analogue of DMT with similar effects and reported oral activity without the aid of an MAOI.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to DMT, DET has a significantly longer duration (2-4 hours vs 15 minutes) with progressive visual and emotional effects.
effectsSummary: Intense sensory and visual alterations, altered perception of space and time, emotional amplification, deep introspection, and potential ego dissolution.
saferUse: Strictly respect Set & Setting (positive mindset, calm and secure physical environment).
Always have a trusted, sober tripsitter present during the experience.
Never combine with lithium, tramadol, or MAOI/SSRI antidepressants.
Test substances with colorimetric reagents prior to use and start with a low test dose.

name: Dextroamphetamine
summary:
Dextroamphetamine (Dexedrine, Attentin) is the active dextrorotatory enantiomer of amphetamine, functioning as a potent dopamine and norepinephrine releasing agent and reuptake inhibitor. Prescribed for treatment-resistant ADHD and narcolepsy, it is also widely used recreationally and as a cognitive enhancer.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to mixed amphetamine salts (Adderall) which contain 25% levoamphetamine, pure dextroamphetamine is 3 to 4 times more potent centrally with significantly reduced peripheral adrenergic side effects (tachycardia, tremor, peripheral vasoconstriction), yielding cleaner focus but heightened euphoric potential.
effectsSummary: Intense dopaminergic focus, wakefulness, euphoria, increased motivation, talkativeness, complete appetite suppression, and accelerated thought processing.
dosageRemark: ⚠️ HIGH POTENCY: 5 mg dextroamphetamine is roughly bioequivalent to 15-20 mg methylphenidate. Start with 2.5-5 mg to assess cardiovascular reactivity.
generalRisks: Tachycardia, arterial hypertension, acute anxiety, bruxism, severe insomnia, and post-use depressive crash.
longtermRisks: Severe psychological addiction, rapid tolerance, amphetamine psychosis (paranoid delusions), and dopaminergic neurotoxicity at high unprescribed doses.
saferUse: Avoid redosing late in the session to preserve sleep architecture.
Take chelated magnesium to prevent jaw clenching and muscular tension.
Maintain hydration and consume calorie-dense liquid foods if solids are unpalatable.
Never combine with MAOIs, tramadol, or other stimulants.

name: Dextromethorphan

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: produces dependence with chronic use and has moderate abuse potential
summary:
Commonly found in certain over the counter cough medicines. Has dissociative effects similar to ketamine or MXE, though also shares properties with opioids and alcohol. Make sure DXM is the only active ingredient in the preparation.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to ketamine, dextromethorphan (DXM) is a morphinan antitussive converted via CYP2D6 into active dextrorphan (an NMDA antagonist) alongside potent serotonin reuptake inhibition. It produces tiered dissociative 'plateaus' (1 through 4), but carries a fatal serotonin syndrome hazard when combined with SSRIs, SNRIs, or empathogens.
effectsSummary: In high doses (120 mg or more) it has a hallucinogenic and euphoric effect. Perceptual disturbances up to confusion as well as states of agitation with epileptic episodes may occur. Side effects are reddening of the skin and severe itching. With regular use there is great potential for dependence with psychological and physical symptoms!
dosageRemark: DXM in freebase form (as found in Robocough RoboTablets) is around 27-37% more potent than its hydrobromide form due to a higher concentration of DXM by weight. One should take this into account when calculating their dose to avoid a potential overdose.
generalRisks: Caution: The simultaneous intake of MAO inhibitors delays the degradation of DXM and can lead to severe respiratory and circulatory disorders!
saferUse: LETHAL DANGER: Never combine with CNS depressants (alcohol, opioids, benzodiazepines).
Always consume while seated or lying down in a safe space to prevent falls and physical injuries.
Space uses out (at least 2-3 weeks apart) to prevent urinary bladder ulceration and cognitive blunting.
Ensure a sober tripsitter is present to prevent airway obstruction or aspirational risk.

name: Dextropropoxyphene

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
toxicities: potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like alcohol or benzodiazepines
known to cause potentially fatal heart arrhythmias
summary:
An opioid analgesic that is an optical isomer of levopropoxyphene. Used to treat mild pain and often used for its antitussive properties. It has been taken off the market in Europe and US due to concerns of health issues relating to the Kidney, Liver, Heart and Respiratory Disorders. Just a bit stronger than Tramadol.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to codeine and tramadol, dextropropoxyphene (Darvon) was a weak Step II opioid withdrawn globally due to narrow therapeutic index and fatal cardiac conduction toxicity in overdose (quinidine-like sodium channel blockade inducing refractory cardiac arrest).
effectsSummary: Potent analgesia, warm sedation, opioid euphoria, sense of deep contentment, pinpoint pupils, respiratory depression, and gastrointestinal slowing.
saferUse: LETHAL OVERDOSE RISK: Always keep naloxone (Narcan, Nyxoid) immediately accessible.
NEVER combine with benzodiazepines, alcohol, pregabalin, or any CNS depressants.
Never use alone, and test with fentanyl/nitazene test strips before use.
Space doses strictly to prevent severe physical dependence and debilitating withdrawal.

name: Diazepam

tolerance.full: within a couple of days of continuous use

addictionPotential: extremely physically and psychologically addictive
toxicities: potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like alcohol or opioids
summary:
A very common and widely prescribed benzodiazepine with hypnotic and sedative qualities. The metre by which other benzodiazepines are compared. May cause amnesia and lowered inhibitions in excess. Has a relatively long half-life in comparison with other benzodiazepines.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to alprazolam (Xanax) and lorazepam (Ativan), diazepam (Valium) boasts an exceptionally long elimination half-life (30 to 100 hours) via its active metabolite nordiazepam. Offering pronounced muscle relaxant and anticonvulsant properties with self-tapering pharmacokinetic decay, it serves as the international gold standard for alcohol and benzodiazepine withdrawal tapers.
effectsSummary:
Diazepam has a calming, relaxing, antispasmodic, anti-anxiety and sleep-inducing effect.
Taking benzodiazepines increases the effectiveness of the neurotransmitter gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) at the GABA-A receptor. This triggers sedative (calming), hypnotic, anxiolytic (anxiety-relieving), anticonvulsant (anticonvulsant) and muscle-relaxing effects in the body. Benzodiazepines have a depressant effect on the central nervous system. The flow of information in the brain between the brain cells (neurons) is thereby reduced / disturbed and feelings and perceptions are dampened.
The breakdown of the individual active ingredients of benzodiazepines in the body is age-dependent and therefore varies from person to person.
generalRisks:
There is little information available on risks, toxicity, side effects and long-term consequences. Therefore, the general information on benzodiazepines applies:
When mixing with other downers (alcohol, GHB/GBL, heroin) there is a risk of respiratory paralysis!
Taking benzodiazepines can cause numerous undesirable side effects. In addition, regular and long-term use carries a very high risk of physical and psychological dependence. Benzodiazepines should only be taken as prescribed by a doctor and only for a short period of time (max. 4-6 weeks). Longer-term use should be discussed with the treating specialist. The dosages and duration of action of the individual benzodiazepines differ considerably.
Side effects of benzodiazepines may be as follows: Prolonged fatigue, gastrointestinal problems, impaired reactions, hypersensitivity reactions, headaches, dizziness, motor difficulties, visual disturbances, slowed breathing, muscle weakness, confusion, sexual dysfunction, aggression, outbursts of anger, restlessness, random movements, allergies, skin problems/rashes and speech and movement disorders. Some benzodiazepines can cause seizures in epileptics.
longtermRisks:
Regular and long-term use can lead to psychological and physical dependence (very high dependence potential). Immediate discontinuation of the drug after prolonged use can lead to negative withdrawal symptoms (including dizziness, physical weakness, inner restlessness, tremors, sleep disturbances, headaches, sweating, nausea, hallucinations and depression).
In addition, seizures and memory disorders/loss and listlessness (hangover effects) can occur. In case of possible dependence, withdrawal should be discussed with a doctor beforehand and the withdrawal should be medically accompanied. It is extremely important that the dose is reduced gradually.
saferUse: If medicines are obtained on the black market or on the internet and not from a pharmacy/medical facility, the contents are unclear. Have the medicine tested for the exact ingredients in a drug check!
Do not rely on dosage information from colleagues who regularly use benzodiazepines. Due to habituation or dependence, their doses can be much higher and fatal for new users.
Blisters of counterfeits may look identical to the original packaging.

The simultaneous consumption of depressant substances such as alcohol, ketamine, GHB/GBL, nitrous oxide, opioids and/or other benzodiazepines is dangerous as there is an increased risk of vomiting and unconsciousness. The risk of suffocation is high!

name: Dichloropane

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary:
Dichloropane (RTI-111, O-401) is a synthetic phenyltropane stimulant derived as a potent structural analogue of cocaine. It acts as a potent monoamine reuptake inhibitor with dominant affinity for dopamine and norepinephrine transporters.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to cocaine, dichloropane offers a significantly extended duration of action (4-6 hours versus 45-60 minutes for cocaine), substantially reducing the compulsive urge for immediate redosing while carrying a more persistent peripheral adrenergic strain.
effectsSummary: Sharp dopaminergic focus, physical energy, social disinhibition, elevated confidence, and appetite suppression.
dosageRemark: Typical doses: 20-40 mg oral, 15-30 mg insufflated. Duration: 4-6 hours.
generalRisks: Tachycardia, elevated blood pressure, pupil dilation, restlessness, and insomnia.
longtermRisks: Stimulant psychological addiction, tolerance, and cardiovascular stress.
saferUse: Weigh using a 0.001g digital balance.
Do not redose frequently.
Avoid combining with alcohol or other cardiovascular stimulants.

name: Diclazepam

tolerance.full: within 3-4 days of continuous use

addictionPotential: extremely physically and psychologically addictive
toxicities: potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like alcohol or opioids
summary:
A benzodiazepine drug and analogue of diazepam first synthesised by Leo Sternbach at Hoffman-LaRoche in 1960, it has become prominent as an RC benzodiazepine on the grey market in recent years, particularly with the decline in etizolam availability. A sedative and hypnotic it is of intermediate to long half life with similar effects to diazepam, though 10x more potent.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to Diazepam (Valium), diclazepam is roughly 10 times more potent per milligram (1 mg = 10 mg diazepam) and metabolizes into delorazepam and lorazepam, making it an effective benzo taper tool.
effectsSummary: Central nervous system sedation, marked anxiolysis, muscle relaxation, psychomotor slowing, and reduction of inhibitions.
saferUse: LETHAL DANGER: Never combine with alcohol, opioids, or other respiratory depressants.
Space out intake to prevent rapid tolerance and potentially life-threatening withdrawal.
Do not drive or operate heavy machinery while under the influence.
When discontinuing prolonged use, always taper gradually to avoid seizures.

name: Diclofenac
addictionPotential: not habit-forming (no recreational or diversion potential)
toxicities: acute kidney injury and renal toxicity
increased cardiovascular thrombotic risk with high doses or prolonged use
summary:
Diclofenac is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID / AINS) used to treat pain, fever, and inflammation. Potent phenylacetic acid NSAID (Voltarène, Flector) prescribed for rheumatic, orthopedic, renal colic, and inflammatory pain. Contraindicated in established cardiovascular disease. Strict dosing intervals must be respected, and two different NSAIDs must never be combined.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to ibuprofen, diclofenac (Voltaren) is roughly 8 times more potent by weight with high synovial fluid penetration, but carries the highest thrombotic cardiovascular risk profile among traditional non-selective NSAIDs.
effectsSummary: Analgesic (pain relief), antipyretic (fever reduction), and anti-inflammatory effects via COX-1/COX-2 prostaglandin inhibition. No psychoactive or euphoric effect.
dosageRemark: STRICT INTERVAL: Wait at least 6 to 8 hours between two intakes. The 'Heavy' threshold (50 mg) represents the maximum single unit dose per intake. Maximum cumulative daily dose: 150 mg/24h divided into 2 or 3 intakes. Always take with food or a full glass of water to protect the stomach.
generalRisks: Stomach pain, heartburn, nausea, peptic ulcers, gastrointestinal bleeding, fluid retention, elevated blood pressure, and acute renal impairment (especially when dehydrated). Can trigger severe bronchospasm in aspirin-sensitive asthma. Must NOT be used during pregnancy (especially from the 6th month onward) or during bacterial infections like varicella/streptococcal infections without medical advice.
longtermRisks: Chronic or repeated high-dose use causes gastric/duodenal ulcers, gastrointestinal perforation, chronic kidney disease (analgesic nephropathy), hypertension, and elevated risk of myocardial infarction or stroke.
saferUse: Strictly wait at least 6 to 8 hours between two doses and never exceed 150 mg/24h divided into 2 or 3 intakes in 24 hours.
Never exceed 50 mg in a single intake.
NEVER combine with another NSAID (e.g., Ibuprofen, Ketoprofen, Naproxen, Diclofenac, Aspirin at anti-inflammatory doses, Celecoxib).
Take during a meal with a large glass of water and stay well hydrated to protect your kidneys and stomach.
Avoid combining with Lithium (causes severe Lithium poisoning), oral corticosteroids, anticoagulants, or heavy alcohol use.

name: Dihydrocodeine

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
toxicities: potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like alcohol or benzodiazepines
summary:
A weak semi-synthetic opioid analgesic and antitussive (anti-cough) drug. Often sold as a syrup in combination with aspirin or paracetamol. Not to be confused with the slightly less potent codeine.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to Codeine, dihydrocodeine is twice as potent per milligram, does not rely on CYP2D6 metabolism to work, and produces more consistent analgesia.
dosageRemark: ⚖️ RELATIVE POTENCY (~0.2x Oral Morphine, ~1.3-1.5x Codeine): For 12h extended-release tablets (Dicodin LP), wait 12 hours between doses.
effectsSummary: Potent analgesia, warm sedation, opioid euphoria, sense of deep contentment, pinpoint pupils, respiratory depression, and gastrointestinal slowing.
saferUse: LETHAL OVERDOSE RISK: Always keep naloxone (Narcan, Nyxoid) immediately accessible.
NEVER combine with benzodiazepines, alcohol, pregabalin, or any CNS depressants.
Never use alone, and test with fentanyl/nitazene test strips before use.
Space doses strictly to prevent severe physical dependence and debilitating withdrawal.

name: Dipentylone

tolerance.full: Develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: High potential for abuse and residual stimulation
summary:
Dipentylone (dimethylpentylone or bk-DMBDP) is a substituted cathinone that surfaced to replace eutylone and ephylone following their international scheduling. It acts as a dopaminergic and noradrenergic stimulant with a long duration and modest empathogenic qualities.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to eutylone, dipentylone (bk-DMBDP) displays a similar prolonged stimulant profile (4 to 7 hours) with minimal empathogenic warmth, leading to stubborn insomnia and anxiety when redosed consecutively.
effectsSummary: Physical stimulation, elevated heart rate, appetite suppression, prolonged wakefulness, insomnia, anxiety.
dosageRemark: Long-acting compound: redosing reliably leads to severe insomnia and cardiovascular strain.
generalRisks: Tachycardia, hypertension, dehydration, prolonged insomnia, hyperthermia.
longtermRisks: Physical exhaustion, anxiety disorders, rapid tolerance, psychological dependence.
saferUse: Avoid late ingestion due to lengthy duration
Do not redose during the session
Stay hydrated and ensure adequate nutrition

name: Diphenhydramine

tolerance.full: with repeated use

addictionPotential: produces dependence with chronic use
toxicities: fatal at amounts close to or exceeding 2 grams
summary:
An antihistamine which, when taken in smaller doses relieves allergies and insomnia. In larger doses works as a deliriant and can actually keep the user awake. Generally the 'high' of this drug is reported as dysphoric, potentially causing hallucinations indistinguishable from reality.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Diphenhydramine (Benadryl) is a classic first-generation H1 antihistamine and anticholinergic used for allergies and motion sickness; high-dose recreational misuse precipitates dangerous, dysphoric anticholinergic delirium.
effectsSummary: Central muscarinic receptor antagonism causing true delirious hallucinations (inability to distinguish visions from reality), total amnesia, extreme xerostomia, hyperthermia, and pupil paralysis.
saferUse: EXTREME PHYSICAL AND PSYCHIATRIC HAZARD: Recreational use is strongly discouraged.
Mandatory presence of a sober, capable tripsitter to physically prevent wandering into traffic or self-harm.
High risk of severe anticholinergic toxicity requiring emergency medical hospitalization (physostigmine).
Never redose: erratic absorption kinetics frequently lead to fatal systemic poisoning.

name: Diphenidine

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary:
A dissociative anaesthetic related to ephenidine with similar qualities to PCP and ketamine. Has seen some popularity as a recreational RC. Dosage curve has been reported as particularly steep, so care should be taken.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to Ketamine, diphenidine is a diarylethylamine dissociative causing abrupt anterograde amnesia and 'robotic' detachment without warm euphoria.
effectsSummary: Somatosensory and cognitive detachment, bodily anesthesia, proprioceptive distortions, double vision, floating sensations, and deep introspective immersion (hole states).
saferUse: LETHAL DANGER: Never combine with CNS depressants (alcohol, opioids, benzodiazepines).
Always consume while seated or lying down in a safe space to prevent falls and physical injuries.
Space uses out (at least 2-3 weeks apart) to prevent urinary bladder ulceration and cognitive blunting.
Ensure a sober tripsitter is present to prevent airway obstruction or aspirational risk.

name: DiPT

tolerance.full: almost immediately after ingestion

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary:
A rare tryptamine psychedelic closely related to DMT, with the interesting property of having little visual hallucinations, but strong auditory effects.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to all other tryptamines, DiPT is unique in that it leaves vision largely intact while dramatically lowering perceived auditory pitch by several tones.
effectsSummary: Intense sensory and visual alterations, altered perception of space and time, emotional amplification, deep introspection, and potential ego dissolution.
saferUse: Strictly respect Set & Setting (positive mindset, calm and secure physical environment).
Always have a trusted, sober tripsitter present during the experience.
Never combine with lithium, tramadol, or MAOI/SSRI antidepressants.
Test substances with colorimetric reagents prior to use and start with a low test dose.

name: Disulfiram

tolerance.full: irreversible ALDH inhibition
tolerance.zero: persists up to 14 days after stopping Disulfiram!

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
toxicities: SEVERE / POTENTIALLY FATAL DISULFIRAM-ALCOHOL ('ANTABUSE') REACTION with even trace amounts of alcohol (up to 14 days after last dose!)
drug-induced hepatitis (rare fulminant liver failure) and optic/peripheral neuropathy
inhibits dopamine-beta-hydroxylase (worsens Cocaine cardiovascular toxicity & psychosis!)
summary:
Disulfiram (Espéral, Antabuse) is an irreversible aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH) inhibitor used as an aversive deterrent in alcohol abstinence. Ingesting ANY alcohol causes immediate toxic acetaldehyde accumulation (flushing, throbbing headache, violent vomiting, chest pain, hypotension, collapse).

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to acamprosate and naltrexone which target central craving mechanisms, disulfiram (Antabuse) irreversibly blocks aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH). Any alcohol consumption triggers immediate accumulation of toxic acetaldehyde ('disulfiram-ethanol reaction': violent flushing, projectile vomiting, hypotension, arrhythmia), acting as a purely psychological deterrent.
effectsSummary: Minimal subjective effects alone (occasional metallic/garlic aftertaste or fatigue), but triggers an acute, violent acetaldehyde poisoning reaction within 5-15 minutes of any ethanol exposure.
dosageRemark: 24h MORNING SCHEDULE: Maintenance dose is typically 125-250 mg once every 24 hours (initial loading never >500 mg). The 'Heavy' threshold (500 mg = one full 500 mg tablet) is the strict maximum single/daily dose. Must wait >=24 hours after last alcoholic drink before starting!
generalRisks: With ANY alcohol (including vinegar/sauces, mouthwash, cough syrups, aftershave/perfumes!): intense facial flushing, throbbing headache, dyspnea, nausea/vomiting, tachycardia, severe hypotension, arrhythmias, seizures, and cardiovascular collapse.
longtermRisks: Hepatotoxicity (requires periodic liver transaminase tests!), peripheral neuropathy, optic neuritis, and rare psychosis exacerbation (via dopamine-beta-hydroxylase blockade).
saferUse: STRICT ZERO ALCOHOL — including hidden alcohol in liquid medicines, mouthwashes, kombucha, sauces, or alcohol-based skin sprays — during treatment AND for a full 14 days after your last tablet!
NEVER combine with Cocaine or Amphetamines (Disulfiram blocks dopamine breakdown and cocaine clearance, multiplying cardiovascular & psychotic toxicity!).
Monitor liver enzymes regularly and stop immediately if jaundice, dark urine, or fatigue occurs.

name: DMT

tolerance.full: does not appear to occur

addictionPotential: non-addictive with a low abuse potential
summary:
A popular and powerful psychedelic, typically used in two ways; either it is vapourised for a short 'breakthrough' experience, or it is taken in combination with an enzyme inhibitor for a long, intense trip (this is also known as ayahuasca or pharmahuasca).

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to LSD and psilocybin, vaporized N,N-DMT triggers the most explosive psychedelic transition known: onset occurs in 10-15 seconds, catapulting the user into complete sensory 'breakthrough' and autonomous hyper-dimensional entities, with baseline consciousness fully restored in 15-20 minutes and negligible receptor tolerance.
effectsSummary:
The effect depends very much on the set and the setting. Blood pressure and pulse increase, pupils dilate. Detachment of the body from the mind and ego dissolution are common, near-death experiences also occur relatively often, especially when high doses are consumed. The perception of time changes greatly during intoxication. A few minutes can be perceived as very long and intense. In addition, different feelings such as fear, euphoria, etc. can be experienced within a short period of time. Consumers report immersion in very "bizarre" worlds in which connections between being, environment and matter arise. With DMT, this phenomenon is also visually pronounced, i.e., images are linked with oneself, matter and being in one's own society. Physical perception can also be influenced, in that one feels weightless or thinks one is falling.
When swallowed, DMT is only effective in combination with MAO inhibitors. MAO inhibitors (e.g. harmine) are substances and drugs that prevent the enzyme MAO from breaking down the body's own messenger substances such as adrenaline, dopamine, serotonin etc. as well as foreign alkaloids such as caffeine, cocaine, morphine. The psychoactive potion ayahuasca and changa are such a combination. After the consumption of MAO inhibitors, the consumption of certain everyday foods such as cheese is life-threatening.
dosageRemark:
Ayahuasca is a shamanic herbal potion made from DMT-containing chacruna leaves (Psychotria viridis) and the harmaline-containing ayahuasca liana Banisteriopsis caapi. Harmaline is an MAO inhibitor. MAO inhibitors are substances and drugs that prevent the enzyme MAO from breaking down the body's own messenger substances such as adrenalin, dopamine, serotonin, etc. as well as foreign alkaloids such as caffeine, cocaine, etc.. MAO normally also degrades the active substance DMT even before it can enter the central nervous system via the blood-brain barrier.
Changa is a mixture for smoking of DMT-containing plants (but usually mostly crystalline DMT) and herbs that act as MAO inhibitors.
generalRisks: The risk associated with the use of DMT is mainly psychological and depends on the personality structure of the user. The perceptual changes during a trip can be so intense that especially inexperienced users feel overwhelmed by the flood of impressions. The perception of sudden emotional outbursts can also be perceived as rather disturbing and overwhelming. At high doses, such psychological side effects can be felt for days to weeks. If the rules of the set and setting are not followed, there can be false reactions, loss of orientation, panic, paranoia and horror trips. Physical side effects include nausea, vomiting, increase in heart rate, slightly accelerated breathing, increased blood pressure, pupil dilation, increased salivation, tremors, restlessness, headaches and movement disorders.
longtermRisks: Permanent disturbances in self- and reality recognition are possible. The view of the world can be permanently called into question, which can make it difficult to cope with everyday life. Latent (hidden) psychoses can be triggered.
saferUse: Only consume when you feel good. If you are afraid of the strong effects, do not use. Do not use if you are afraid of the substance.
Do not use DMT alone! Take it in a safe atmosphere and together with experienced people you trust.
Take DMT while sitting or lying down, as physical perception and ability to move are impaired during intoxication.
Dose carefully at first. If there is no effect, increase the dose the next time. Do not add more on the same day.
The consumption of MAO-inhibiting foods such as matured cheese, smoked fish or meat, sauerkraut, tofu, chocolate etc. should be avoided before and after consumption.
People with high blood pressure should not consume DMT.
A trip with DMT should remain an exceptional experience. Make sure you take long breaks from using DMT and talk to others about your experience so that it can be processed.

name: DOB

tolerance.full: almost immediately after ingestion

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary:
DOB is a relatively uncommon synthetic psychedelic. It is best known for its very low doses and long duration. Historically it has rarely been taken deliberately, but in place of LSD, however it has recently found its own place in the research chemical scene.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to 2C-B and LSD, DOB has a massive marathon duration (18-30h) and strong cardiovascular stimulation with serious risk of peripheral vascular spasms.
effectsSummary: At the beginning, typical effects of amphetamine unfold, such as increased alertness, accelerated pulse, slight euphoria, increased self-confidence and urge to talk. Afterwards, the effect changes: one often feels a strong urge to move, sensory perception, feelings and empathy are heightened, colours are perceived more distinctly. With DOB and DOI, coloured, superimposed, pulsating patterns are perceived. This effect is weaker with DOM.
generalRisks: Since the effect of DOB comes on late, the danger of overdosing by refilling is particularly great. The long duration of action poses a psychological burden. Confusion or anxiety is common, especially at high doses. Some DOB users report a burning or pressure sensation in the bladder. At high doses, temporary paralysis, inability to communicate or insensitivity to pain (caution: risk of injury and accidents) may occur. Teeth grinding and strain on the cardiovascular system are also possible.
longtermRisks: Due to the long and intense effects, use - especially frequent use - carries the risk of a loss of reality, which can manifest itself in schizophrenic traits and anxiety states. The consumption of DOB can trigger latent (hidden) psychoses.
saferUse: DOB are not suitable as party drugs and should only be used by experienced users.
Plan your trip ahead because of the long duration of action.
Never consume DOB alone and only when you feel very well mentally and physically and are well rested!

Pay attention to set and setting: only take DOB in a place where you feel safe and avoid unwanted disturbances from outside! Prepare yourself well for the trip and prepare yourself internally for the long duration of the effect.
Drink enough water during the trip.
Mixed use of these potent substances should be avoided at all costs.

As amphetamine derivatives, DOB can be particularly draining because of their long duration of action. Light vitamin-rich food, fruits, vegetable juices, vitamins and minerals promote a soft landing after the trip has subsided and can weaken a hangover.
Plan enough time for recovery after the trip (at least 1 day)!
A trip with DOB should remain an exceptional experience. Make sure to take long breaks from consumption so that the experience can be processed.
