name: Doxepin

tolerance.full: 2 - 4 weeks for antidepressant action (immediate sedation)

addictionPotential: not habit-forming (no recreational potential), causes cholinergic rebound withdrawal if stopped suddenly
toxicities: HIGHLY CARDIOTOXIC in overdose (sodium-channel blockade, QRS widening, fatal ventricular arrhythmias, seizures, coma)
serotonin syndrome with MAOIs/Tramadol/SSRIs and severe anticholinergic toxicity
summary:
Doxepin is a tricyclic antidepressant (TCA) acting as a serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor alongside strong antihistaminic, anticholinergic, and alpha-1 blocking properties. Tricyclic antidepressant and extremely potent H1 histamine antagonist (Quitaxon, Silenor); used at 3-10 mg for sleep-maintenance insomnia and 25-100+ mg for depression and anxiety.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Doxepin (Silenor) is a tricyclic compound possessing the highest known binding affinity for the histamine H1 receptor. At micro-doses (3-6 mg), it acts as a selective non-scheduled hypnotic specifically indicated for sleep maintenance insomnia.
effectsSummary: Antidepressant, neuropathic pain relief, and strong sedation/sleep induction; causes dry mouth, constipation, orthostatic dizziness, and blurred vision.
dosageRemark: NARROW THERAPEUTIC MARGIN: The 'Heavy' threshold (100 mg) represents the maximum single outpatient unit dose per intake (higher daily totals up to 150-200 mg/24h are divided or strictly supervised). Often taken in the evening due to sedation.
generalRisks: Sedation, dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention, blurred vision, tachycardia, orthostatic hypotension, QT/QRS prolongation, lowered seizure threshold, and severe cardiotoxicity in overdose.
longtermRisks: Weight gain, dental caries (from chronic dry mouth), anticholinergic cognitive burden, and withdrawal symptoms if stopped abruptly.
saferUse: Never exceed 100 mg in a single outpatient intake — tricyclic overdose is rapidly cardiotoxic.
NEVER combine with MAOIs, Tramadol, MDMA, or Clonidine.
Avoid combining with LSD/psychedelics (markedly intensifies trips and lowers seizure threshold!), Alcohol, Benzodiazepines, Opioids, or anticholinergics.

name: Doxylamine

tolerance.full: develops rapidly within 3 - 5 days

addictionPotential: moderately habit-forming for sleep; dysphoric deliriant misuse documented at high doses
toxicities: RHABDOMYOLYSIS (muscle breakdown and acute kidney failure in high-dose misuse/overdose!)
severe anticholinergic delirium, seizures, tachycardia, and hyperthermia
summary:
Doxylamine succinate (Donormyl 15 mg, Unisom) is an over-the-counter ethanolamine H1 antihistamine hypnotic closely related to diphenhydramine. At 7.5-15 mg (max 30 mg medically) it treats occasional insomnia; at high diverted doses (150-300+ mg) it acts as a dysphoric anticholinergic deliriant with a uniquely high risk of rhabdomyolysis!

⚖️ Comparative profile: Doxylamine (Unisom) is an over-the-counter first-generation H1 antihistamine for short-term insomnia. Devoid of benzodiazepine physical dependence, it reliably shortens sleep onset for acute 2-5 day episodes before rapid antihistamine tolerance develops.
effectsSummary: Drowsiness and sleep promotion at 7.5-30 mg; heavy physical load, restless legs, severe dry mouth, confusion, auditory/visual deliriant hallucinations, and amnesia at high misused doses.
dosageRemark: DIVERSION-ADAPTED DOSAGES: Therapeutic sleep dose is 7.5 to 15 mg (half to one Donormyl tablet; maximum medical dose 30 mg, for max 5 days). Doses >= 100-300 mg ('Strong'/'Heavy') cause dangerous anticholinergic delirium, tachycardia, seizures, and skeletal muscle breakdown (rhabdomyolysis)!
generalRisks: Morning grogginess, dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention, blurred vision, acute glaucoma, restless legs, tachycardia, and in overdose rhabdomyolysis (dark brown urine + muscle pain -> urgent ER!).
longtermRisks: Cognitive/memory decline (strong anticholinergic load), rapid tolerance to sleep effects, and kidney damage after high-dose episodes.
saferUse: For sleep, stick strictly to 7.5-15 mg (30 mg absolute medical max) for no more than 2-5 consecutive nights.
Strongly avoid deliriant high doses: Doxylamine carries a notably higher rate of rhabdomyolysis and acute renal failure than even Diphenhydramine.
NEVER mix with Alcohol, Opioids, Benzodiazepines, Dextromethorphan (DXM), or other anticholinergics/TCAs.

name: DPT
addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary:
N,N-Dipropyltryptamine, a psychedelic tryptamine compound and lesser-known analogue of DMT, with similar psychedelic effects. Like DMT it is a partial serotonin receptor agonist.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to DMT, DPT ('The Light') lasts 2-3 times longer when vaporized (1-2h) and carries a considerably heavier, vibrating physical body load.
effectsSummary: Intense sensory and visual alterations, altered perception of space and time, emotional amplification, deep introspection, and potential ego dissolution.
saferUse: Strictly respect Set & Setting (positive mindset, calm and secure physical environment).
Always have a trusted, sober tripsitter present during the experience.
Never combine with lithium, tramadol, or MAOI/SSRI antidepressants.
Test substances with colorimetric reagents prior to use and start with a low test dose.

name: Duloxetine

tolerance.full: 2 - 4 weeks

addictionPotential: not addictive; abrupt cessation causes SNRI withdrawal syndrome
toxicities: hepatotoxicity (contraindicated in liver disease or heavy alcohol use)
summary:
Duloxetine (Cymbalta) is a balanced serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (SNRI) prescribed for major depression, generalized anxiety disorder, diabetic neuropathic pain, and fibromyalgia.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to venlafaxine (Effexor), duloxetine (Cymbalta) is a balanced dual SNRI that simultaneously inhibits both serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake across its full therapeutic dose range (60-120 mg), providing superior efficacy for diabetic neuropathic pain and chronic fibromyalgia.
effectsSummary: Improves depressive/anxious symptoms and central neuropathic pain inhibition; swallow gastro-resistant capsules whole without crushing or opening.
dosageRemark: DAILY SCHEDULE: Standard dose is 60 mg once every 24 hours (sometimes 60 mg twice daily). The 'Heavy' threshold (120 mg) is the absolute maximum single and daily dose.
generalRisks: Nausea, dry mouth, constipation, sweating, fatigue or insomnia, blood pressure elevation, urinary hesitation, and liver enzyme elevation.
longtermRisks: Hepatotoxicity (especially with alcohol), hypertension, and withdrawal syndrome ('brain zaps', dizziness) if stopped abruptly.
saferUse: Swallow capsules whole (do not crush or chew — acid degrades duloxetine!) and never exceed 120 mg/day.
NEVER combine with MAOIs, Fluvoxamine (potent CYP1A2 inhibitor spikes duloxetine levels 5-fold!), Tramadol, or DXM.
Avoid heavy alcohol consumption (additive liver toxicity) and NSAIDs (bleeding risk).

name: Efavirenz
addictionPotential: not known to be habit-forming
toxicities: may cause liver toxicity at high doses or after chronic use
summary:
Efavirenz (Sustiva) is a non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI) core antiretroviral medication for HIV management. Owing to off-target affinity at 5-HT2A serotonin and CB1 cannabinoid receptors, it frequently induces potent neuropsychiatric phenomena including ultra-vivid dreaming, perceptual softening, and nocturnal hallucinations.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to classic serotonergic psychedelics, efavirenz is not an intended euphoriant, but has seen documented recreational diversion in South Africa (smoked in street mixtures termed 'Whoonga' or 'Nyaope' alongside cannabis), producing disorientation, vivid oneiric visions, and severe ataxia.
effectsSummary: Vivid dreams, night terrors, depersonalization, dizziness, morning hangover, and confused sedation.
dosageRemark: Standard medical HIV dose: 600 mg once daily at bedtime on an empty stomach.
generalRisks: Severe dizziness, impaired concentration, depression, rash, and nocturnal hallucinations.
longtermRisks: Hepatotoxicity, hypercholesterolemia, and rapid emergence of viral resistance if treatment is interrupted.
saferUse: Take strictly at bedtime on an empty stomach to sleep through peak CNS side effects.
Never divert, crush, or smoke antiretroviral pharmacotherapies.

name: Ephedrine
summary:
Ephedrine is a sympathomimetic amine commonly used as a stimulant, concentration aid, decongestant, appetite suppressant, and to treat hypotension associated with anaesthesia. A methamphetamine analogue and commonly used in the production of methamphetamine.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to amphetamine, ephedrine acts predominantly on the body (bronchodilation, elevated heart rate, thermogenesis) rather than central dopamine, offering physical drive without true mental euphoria.
effectsSummary: Stimulates circulation, increases drive and performance, and suppresses appetite.
generalRisks:
Even at low doses: Palpitations, restlessness, sleep problems, urinary urgency or retention and dry mouth. Also possible are feelings of anxiety, increased blood pressure (vasoconstriction), loss of appetite, dizziness, cardiac arrhythmias and even heart attacks.
In case of overdose: confusion and paranoia. The tannins of ephedra herb can cause stomach complaints in larger quantities.
longtermRisks: Continuous use: Impaired memory and concentration, irritability, nervousness, aggressive behaviour, cardiac arrhythmia, chronic high blood pressure, bad teeth, liver/kidney damage and psychological disorders. Regular ephedrine use can lead to the development of tolerance and dependence, especially with psychological symptoms.
saferUse: Take a low dose of ephedrine, as the active ingredient content can vary greatly, especially in herbs!
Drink enough water (3 - 5 dl per hour) and no alcohol!
People with circulatory problems/diseases, thyroid disorders and liver or kidney damage should not consume ephedrine!
Ephedrine is not an effective means of losing weight without medical supervision.

name: Ephenidine

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary:
A dissociative drug which is less potent and less confusing than MXE but with otherwise similar properties. Reported as causing light stimulant effects at lower doses.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to Ketamine, ephenidine lasts much longer (5-8 hours), has a slow oral onset, and produces marked philosophical clarity.
effectsSummary: Somatosensory and cognitive detachment, bodily anesthesia, proprioceptive distortions, double vision, floating sensations, and deep introspective immersion (hole states).
saferUse: LETHAL DANGER: Never combine with CNS depressants (alcohol, opioids, benzodiazepines).
Always consume while seated or lying down in a safe space to prevent falls and physical injuries.
Space uses out (at least 2-3 weeks apart) to prevent urinary bladder ulceration and cognitive blunting.
Ensure a sober tripsitter is present to prevent airway obstruction or aspirational risk.

name: Ephylone

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary: ⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to ethylone and MDMA, ephylone has a much longer duration of action (6 to 10 hours), with the initial empathogenic euphoria quickly giving way to persistent adrenergic stimulation and severe insomnia.
effectsSummary: Massive release of serotonin and dopamine, heightened empathy, deep feelings of interpersonal connection, tactile euphoria, and moderate physical stimulation.
saferUse: Respect the 6 to 12 weeks spacing rule between sessions to allow complete serotonin replenishment.
Stay hydrated reasonably (~250-500 ml water/electrolytes per hour during exertion to avoid hyponatremia).
Never combine with antidepressants (SSRIs, SNRIs, MAOIs) due to lethal serotonin syndrome risk.
Monitor body temperature closely and take frequent breaks in cool, ventilated areas.

name: EPT

tolerance.full: almost immediately after ingestion

addictionPotential: does not produce dependence and has low abuse potential
summary:
Ethylpropyltryptamine a novel tryptamine, that is the structural homologue of DMT.

⚖️ Comparative profile: A synthetic base tryptamine analogue of DMT and DPT, EPT features a prompt onset and short 1-2 hour duration with gentle visual alterations and light somatic load.
effectsSummary: Intense sensory and visual alterations, altered perception of space and time, emotional amplification, deep introspection, and potential ego dissolution.
saferUse: Strictly respect Set & Setting (positive mindset, calm and secure physical environment).
Always have a trusted, sober tripsitter present during the experience.
Never combine with lithium, tramadol, or MAOI/SSRI antidepressants.
Test substances with colorimetric reagents prior to use and start with a low test dose.

name: Escaline

tolerance.full: almost immediately after ingestion

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary:
First synthesised in the 50s, this uncommon drug was reexamined by David Nichols in the 1990s. It is an analogue of mescaline which is roughly six times more potent, and is thus a powerful psychedelic phenethylamine. Subjective effects may include stimulation and hallucinations.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to Mescaline, escaline is about 10 times more potent per milligram and produces more noticeable physical stimulation.
effectsSummary: Intense sensory and visual alterations, altered perception of space and time, emotional amplification, deep introspection, and potential ego dissolution.
saferUse: Strictly respect Set & Setting (positive mindset, calm and secure physical environment).
Always have a trusted, sober tripsitter present during the experience.
Never combine with lithium, tramadol, or MAOI/SSRI antidepressants.
Test substances with colorimetric reagents prior to use and start with a low test dose.

name: Escitalopram

tolerance.full: steady-state therapeutic effect after 2 - 4 weeks
tolerance.zero: requires gradual taper over weeks to avoid withdrawal

addictionPotential: not addictive (no recreational/diversion potential), but abrupt discontinuation causes SSRI withdrawal syndrome
toxicities: serotonin syndrome when combined with MAOIs, Tramadol, DXM, MDMA, or other serotonergics
increased gastrointestinal bleeding risk when combined with NSAIDs or Aspirin
summary:
Escitalopram is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) antidepressant prescribed for major depressive disorder, generalized/social anxiety, panic disorder, OCD, and PTSD. Highly selective S-enantiomer of citalopram (Seroplex, Lexapro). Subject to a strict regulatory 20 mg maximum dose cap due to dose-dependent QT interval prolongation.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to racemic citalopram (Celexa), escitalopram (Lexapro) is the pure active (S)-enantiomer. It is twice as potent, demonstrates the highest molecular selectivity for the serotonin transporter (SERT) of any clinical antidepressant, and halves the risk of cardiac QTc prolongation.
effectsSummary: Gradually stabilizes mood and reduces anxiety/obsessive symptoms over 2-4 weeks; markedly blunts the subjective effects of classic psychedelics and MDMA while raising serotonin toxicity risk with serotonergic releasers/MAOIs.
dosageRemark: DAILY SCHEDULE: Usually taken once every 24 hours at a consistent time. The 'Heavy' threshold (20 mg) represents the maximum single unit dose per intake. STRICT 20 mg CAP (10 mg in patients >65 years) due to cardiac QT prolongation risk! Never double a dose if missed, and never stop abruptly without a medical tapering plan.
generalRisks: Initial nausea, diarrhea, headache, transient anxiety/insomnia or somnolence, sweating, sexual dysfunction (anorgasmia/low libido), bruxism, hyponatremia, and suicidal ideation monitoring during the first weeks in young adults.
longtermRisks: Discontinuation syndrome upon abrupt cessation ('brain zaps' / electric shock sensations, dizziness, rebound anxiety, flu-like symptoms), emotional blunting, weight changes, and persistent sexual side effects.
saferUse: Take at a fixed 24-hour interval and never exceed 20 mg in a single intake.
NEVER combine with MAOIs (wait at least 14 days after stopping SSRIs, or 5 weeks after Fluoxetine, before starting an MAOI), Tramadol, or Dextromethorphan (high Serotonin Syndrome risk!).
Avoid combining with NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Ketoprofen, Aspirin, etc.) without gastric protection due to elevated GI bleeding risk.
Do not take higher doses of MDMA or psychedelics to 'overcome' SSRI blunting — doing so risks fatal serotonin toxicity without restoring euphoria.
Taper gradually with your doctor when stopping treatment.

name: Estazolam

tolerance.full: develops rapidly within days to 2 weeks of daily use

addictionPotential: extremely physically and psychologically addictive (severe/fatal withdrawal seizures if stopped abruptly!)
toxicities: low organ toxicity alone, but HIGHLY LETHAL respiratory depression when mixed with Alcohol, Opioids, GHB/GBL, or Barbiturates
summary:
Estazolam is a prescription benzodiazepine acting as a positive allosteric modulator of GABA-A receptors. Intermediate-acting triazolobenzodiazepine hypnotic (Nuctalon 2 mg) prescribed for sleep-onset and sleep-maintenance insomnia; metabolized via CYP3A4. Approximate potency equivalence: ~1.5 mg Estazolam ≈ 10 mg Diazepam. Do not combine with other CNS depressants.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Estazolam (Prosom) is an intermediate-acting triazolobenzodiazepine (10-18 hour half-life), clinically optimized for nocturnal sleep maintenance and reducing frequent nighttime awakenings.
effectsSummary: Anxiolysis (anxiety relief), sedation, hypnosis (sleep induction), muscle relaxation, anticonvulsant action; at higher/diverted doses causes disinhibition, motor ataxia, slurred speech, and anterograde amnesia ('blackouts').
dosageRemark: DIVERSION-ADAPTED DOSAGES: Dosages reflect both therapeutic and diverted/recreational usage (~1.5 mg ≈ 10 mg Diazepam). Doses in the 'Strong'/'Heavy' range (>=3-5 mg) frequently cause amnesia, compulsive redosing, delusion of sobriety, and behavioral disinhibition.
generalRisks: Drowsiness, impaired driving/coordination, memory blackouts, paradoxical aggression or disinhibition, falls, and fatal respiratory arrest if combined with opioids, alcohol, GHB, or other sedatives.
longtermRisks: Severe physical and psychological dependence (medical prescriptions should normally not exceed 4-12 weeks for anxiety or 4 weeks for insomnia). NEVER stop abruptly after daily use: benzodiazepine withdrawal can cause rebound panic, insomnia, tremors, delirium, and potentially fatal generalized seizures — always taper slowly under medical supervision!
saferUse: NEVER mix with Alcohol, Opioids (Codeine, Tramadol, Morphine, Oxycodone, Heroin, Methadone, Opium), GHB/GBL, Barbiturates, or Pregabalin (life-threatening respiratory arrest!).
Beware of 'delusion of sobriety' and memory blackouts that lead to accidental compulsive redosing — log every intake immediately.
Limit continuous daily use to prevent severe physical dependence, and NEVER stop cold-turkey after prolonged use (gradual medical taper mandatory).

name: Eszopiclone

tolerance.full: within a couple of weeks of daily use

addictionPotential: extremely physically and psychologically addictive
toxicities: potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like benzodiazepines, alcohol or opioids
summary:
The d-isomer of Zopiclone, this drug is a potent hypnotic 'Z' drug often used to treat insomnia. High doses may cause amnesia, delirium and lowered inhibitions. Should not be combined with any depressants. Limited recreational value.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to racemic zopiclone, eszopiclone (Lunesta) is the isolated active (S)-enantiomer. This allows for a 50% dose reduction (1 to 3 mg versus 3.75 to 7.5 mg) while providing sustained sleep maintenance with slightly reduced severity of dysgeusia (bitter metallic taste).
effectsSummary: Intense sensory and visual alterations, altered perception of space and time, emotional amplification, deep introspection, and potential ego dissolution.
saferUse: Strictly respect Set & Setting (positive mindset, calm and secure physical environment).
Always have a trusted, sober tripsitter present during the experience.
Never combine with lithium, tramadol, or MAOI/SSRI antidepressants.
Test substances with colorimetric reagents prior to use and start with a low test dose.

name: ETH-CAT

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: mildly addictive with a comparatively low potential for abuse
summary: ⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to mephedrone and methcathinone, ethcathinone is a significantly milder and less euphoric stimulant, producing predominantly wakefulness and appetite suppression similar to high-dose caffeine or bupropion.
effectsSummary: Heightened alertness and concentration, dopaminergic euphoria, physical and mental energy surge, increased heart rate, and appetite suppression.
saferUse: Stay hydrated regularly (water or electrolyte drinks, ~500 ml/h during exertion).
Avoid compulsive redosing which sharply escalates cardiotoxicity and hyperthermia.
Never combine with other stimulants, MAOIs, or decongestants.
Monitor blood pressure and body temperature, and ensure adequate recovery intervals.

name: ETH-LAD

tolerance.full: almost immediately after ingestion

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary:
A psychedelic drug and slightly more potent analogue of LSD, first synthesised by Alexander Shulgin - sometimes described as being less 'abrasive' than LSD. Less common than the associated AL-LAD, though has seen some popularity since its release on the Internet research chemical scene in 2015.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to LSD, ETH-LAD is significantly more potent per microgram (active from 50-75 µg), with distinct auditory shifts and unique visuals, though with more pronounced nausea and body load.
effectsSummary: Intense sensory and visual alterations, altered perception of space and time, emotional amplification, deep introspection, and potential ego dissolution.
saferUse: Strictly respect Set & Setting (positive mindset, calm and secure physical environment).
Always have a trusted, sober tripsitter present during the experience.
Never combine with lithium, tramadol, or MAOI/SSRI antidepressants.
Test substances with colorimetric reagents prior to use and start with a low test dose.

name: Ethylmorphine

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: very addictive with a high potential for abuse
toxicities: potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like alcohol or benzodiazepines
summary:
A medium-strength opioid analgesic and analogue of morphine. Considered less potent than morphine but more potent than codeine, and has been used in Germany for this reason. Said to have a 'ceiling' effect where no more euphoria occurs with increased dosage. Under investigation as a maintainance drug in opioid dependence therapy.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to Codeine, ethylmorphine provides equivalent cough suppression with slightly heavier sedating qualities.
effectsSummary: Potent analgesia, warm sedation, opioid euphoria, sense of deep contentment, pinpoint pupils, respiratory depression, and gastrointestinal slowing.
saferUse: LETHAL OVERDOSE RISK: Always keep naloxone (Narcan, Nyxoid) immediately accessible.
NEVER combine with benzodiazepines, alcohol, pregabalin, or any CNS depressants.
Never use alone, and test with fentanyl/nitazene test strips before use.
Space doses strictly to prevent severe physical dependence and debilitating withdrawal.

name: Ethylone

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary:
A euphoric stimulant often sold in place of MDMA since methylone was banned. Slightly less potent and empathogenic than methylone, it is often described as more of a 'straight stimulant.'

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to MDMA, ethylone provides a subtler, milder emotional warmth and modest physical stimulation lasting 3-4 hours.
effectsSummary: Heightened alertness and concentration, dopaminergic euphoria, physical and mental energy surge, increased heart rate, and appetite suppression.
saferUse: Stay hydrated regularly (water or electrolyte drinks, ~500 ml/h during exertion).
Avoid compulsive redosing which sharply escalates cardiotoxicity and hyperthermia.
Never combine with other stimulants, MAOIs, or decongestants.
Monitor blood pressure and body temperature, and ensure adequate recovery intervals.

name: Ethylphenidate

summary:
Potent psychostimulant, similar to Methylphenidate. Note: Ethylphenidate should NOT be insufflated as it is known to be highly caustic and will cause serious harm to your nasal septum, even with light usage.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to methylphenidate, ethylphenidate has a faster onset with a stronger euphoric rush, but a shorter duration and higher cardiac strain (tachycardia).
effectsSummary: Heightened alertness and concentration, dopaminergic euphoria, physical and mental energy surge, increased heart rate, and appetite suppression.

Avoid compulsive redosing which sharply escalates cardiotoxicity and hyperthermia.

Monitor blood pressure and body temperature, and ensure adequate recovery intervals.

name: Etifoxine
addictionPotential: not habit-forming (no rebound anxiety or physical withdrawal)
toxicities: rare but severe hepatotoxicity (cytolytic/cholestatic hepatitis) and severe cutaneous reactions (DRESS)
summary:
Etifoxine (Stresam) is a non-benzodiazepine benzoxazine anxiolytic acting on GABA-A beta-2/beta-3 subunits and mitochondrial TSPO (stimulating endogenous neurosteroid synthesis) without causing amnesia or physical dependence.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to benzodiazepines, etifoxine (Stresam) enhances GABAergic tone through dual action: direct GABA-A modulation and stimulation of endogenous anxiolytic neurosteroidogenesis (allopregnanolone) via mitochondrial TSPO proteins, avoiding muscle weakness and dependence.
effectsSummary: Reduces psychosomatic anxiety manifestations (palpitations, chest tightness, tension) with much milder drowsiness than benzodiazepines.
dosageRemark: STRICT 8-12h SCHEDULE: Taken as 50 mg three times daily or 100 mg morning and evening with a glass of water (maximum 200 mg/24h). The 'Heavy' threshold (100 mg) is the maximum single unit intake.
generalRisks: Mild initial drowsiness, skin rash/urticaria, metrorrhagia (intermenstrual bleeding on oral contraceptives), lymphocytic colitis (watery diarrhea), and rare severe hepatitis.
longtermRisks: Treatment duration generally limited to a few weeks up to 12 weeks; stop permanently if liver enzyme elevation or skin rash occurs.
saferUse: Never exceed 100 mg per intake or 200 mg/24h.
STOP IMMEDIATELY and consult a doctor if jaundice/dark urine, severe skin rash, or persistent watery diarrhea appears.
Avoid Alcohol and CNS depressants (potentiates sedation).

name: Etizolam

tolerance.full: within a couple of days of continuous use

addictionPotential: highly addictive with a high potential for abuse
toxicities: potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like alcohol or opioids
summary:
A thienodiazepine anxiolytic. Similar in action to benzodiazepine drugs. Relieves anxiety, causes sedation and mild euphoria. High doses can lead to losing memory of what happened while on the drug. Users often compulsively re-dose frequently leading to accidental blackouts. Can be found in pressed pharmaceutical pills from various countries, clandestine pill presses, or as a powder

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to Diazepam (Valium), etizolam is about 10 times more potent per milligram (1 mg equals 10 mg diazepam), has a much faster onset (15-30 min), and stronger anxiolytic/euphoric properties, but its shorter duration (4-6h) speeds up tolerance.
effectsSummary:
Etizolam is a research chemical with anti-anxiety, anticonvulsant, sedative and sleep-inducing properties.
As it is a little-researched substance, only vague information is available regarding its effect.
Taking benzodiazepines increases the effectiveness of the neurotransmitter gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) at the GABA-A receptor. This triggers sedative (calming), hypnotic, anxiolytic (anxiety-relieving), anticonvulsant (anticonvulsant) and muscle-relaxing effects in the body. Benzodiazepines have a depressant effect on the central nervous system. The flow of information in the brain between the brain cells (neurons) is thereby reduced / disturbed and feelings and perceptions are dampened.
The breakdown of the individual active ingredients of benzodiazepines in the body is age-dependent and therefore varies from person to person.
dosageRemark: 0.75 mg etizolam corresponds to 10 mg diazepam
generalRisks:
There is little information available on risks, toxicity, side effects and long-term consequences. Therefore, the general information on benzodiazepines applies:
When mixing with other downers (alcohol, GHB/GBL, heroin) there is a risk of respiratory paralysis!
Taking benzodiazepines can cause numerous undesirable side effects. In addition, regular and long-term use carries a very high risk of physical and psychological dependence. Benzodiazepines should only be taken as prescribed by a doctor and only for a short period of time (max. 4-6 weeks). Longer-term use should be discussed with the treating specialist. The dosages and duration of action of the individual benzodiazepines differ considerably.
Side effects of benzodiazepines may be as follows: Prolonged fatigue, gastrointestinal problems, impaired reactions, hypersensitivity reactions, headaches, dizziness, motor difficulties, visual disturbances, slowed breathing, muscle weakness, confusion, sexual dysfunction, aggression, outbursts of anger, restlessness, random movements, allergies, skin problems/rashes and speech and movement disorders. Some benzodiazepines can cause seizures in epileptics.
longtermRisks:
Regular and long-term use can lead to psychological and physical dependence (very high dependence potential). Immediate discontinuation of the drug after prolonged use can lead to negative withdrawal symptoms (including dizziness, physical weakness, inner restlessness, tremors, sleep disturbances, headaches, sweating, nausea, hallucinations and depression).
In addition, seizures and memory disorders/loss and listlessness (hangover effects) can occur. In case of possible dependence, withdrawal should be discussed with a doctor beforehand and the withdrawal should be medically accompanied. It is extremely important that the dose is reduced gradually.
saferUse: If medicines are obtained on the black market or on the internet and not from a pharmacy/medical facility, the contents are unclear. Have the medicine tested for the exact ingredients in a drug check!
Do not rely on dosage information from colleagues who regularly use benzodiazepines. Due to habituation or dependence, their doses can be much higher and fatal for new users.
Blisters of counterfeits may look identical to the original packaging.

The simultaneous consumption of depressant substances such as alcohol, ketamine, GHB/GBL, nitrous oxide, opioids and/or other benzodiazepines is dangerous as there is an increased risk of vomiting and unconsciousness. The risk of suffocation is high!

name: Etomidate
summary:
Etomidate (Amidate) is an ultra-short-acting intravenous non-barbiturate anaesthetic derived from imidazole. Employed exclusively in emergency medicine and operating suites for rapid sequence induction (RSI), it acts as a selective positive allosteric modulator of GABA-A receptors.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to propofol and thiopental, etomidate boasts unparalleled hemodynamic stability with minimal myocardial depression or blood pressure drops, making it the premier induction agent for critically ill or trauma patients. However, even a single dose blocks the enzyme 11-beta-hydroxylase, causing transient adrenal cortical suppression.
effectsSummary: Rapid onset of complete hypnosis within 30-45 seconds, lack of intrinsic analgesia, transient myoclonic twitches, and prompt emergence.
dosageRemark: ⚠️ STRICT HOSPITAL USE ONLY: 0.2-0.3 mg/kg administered via secure IV access with mechanical airway support immediately available.
generalRisks: Apnea, severe transient myoclonus, post-operative nausea/vomiting, and local venous irritation.
longtermRisks: Adrenal insufficiency via suppression of cortisol and aldosterone synthesis (fatal if used as a continuous ICU infusion).
saferUse: Administer only with immediate capabilities for endotracheal intubation.
Contraindicated for prolonged sedation or maintenance infusions.

name: Etoricoxib
addictionPotential: not habit-forming (no recreational or diversion potential)
toxicities: acute kidney injury and renal toxicity
increased cardiovascular thrombotic risk with high doses or prolonged use
summary:
Etoricoxib is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID / AINS) used to treat pain, fever, and inflammation. Long-acting selective COX-2 inhibitor NSAID (Arcoxia) taken strictly once every 24 hours. Contraindicated in uncontrolled hypertension. Strict dosing intervals must be respected, and two different NSAIDs must never be combined.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to celecoxib, etoricoxib (Arcoxia) exhibits even higher COX-2 selectivity (>100-fold over COX-1), offering maximal anti-inflammatory relief in once-daily dosing with minimal GI distress, while requiring close blood pressure monitoring.
effectsSummary: Analgesic (pain relief), antipyretic (fever reduction), and anti-inflammatory effects via COX-1/COX-2 prostaglandin inhibition. No psychoactive or euphoric effect.
dosageRemark: STRICT INTERVAL: Wait 24 hours (strictly once daily) between two intakes. The 'Heavy' threshold (120 mg) represents the maximum single unit dose per intake. Maximum cumulative daily dose: 90 mg/24h (120 mg/24h strictly limited to acute gouty arthritis for max 8 days). Always take with food or a full glass of water to protect the stomach.
generalRisks: Stomach pain, heartburn, nausea, peptic ulcers, gastrointestinal bleeding, fluid retention, elevated blood pressure, and acute renal impairment (especially when dehydrated). Can trigger severe bronchospasm in aspirin-sensitive asthma. Must NOT be used during pregnancy (especially from the 6th month onward) or during bacterial infections like varicella/streptococcal infections without medical advice.
longtermRisks: Chronic or repeated high-dose use causes gastric/duodenal ulcers, gastrointestinal perforation, chronic kidney disease (analgesic nephropathy), hypertension, and elevated risk of myocardial infarction or stroke.
saferUse: Strictly wait 24 hours (strictly once daily) between two doses and never exceed 90 mg/24h (120 mg/24h strictly limited to acute gouty arthritis for max 8 days) in 24 hours.
Never exceed 120 mg in a single intake.
NEVER combine with another NSAID (e.g., Ibuprofen, Ketoprofen, Naproxen, Diclofenac, Aspirin at anti-inflammatory doses, Celecoxib).
Take during a meal with a large glass of water and stay well hydrated to protect your kidneys and stomach.
Avoid combining with Lithium (causes severe Lithium poisoning), oral corticosteroids, anticoagulants, or heavy alcohol use.

name: Eutylone

tolerance.full: Develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: High potential for abuse and persistent compulsive stimulation
summary:
Eutylone (bk-EBDB) is a substituted methylenedioxyphenethylamine-type cathinone related to ethylone and butylone. Highly prevalent in global seizures between 2019 and 2023, it was frequently sold adulterated as counterfeit MDMA. It produces lasting stimulation with a relatively short euphoric peak followed by lingering adrenergic activity up to 8 hours.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to MDMA and methylone, eutylone (bk-EBDB) features a substantially longer residual stimulation (5 to 8 hours), a brief euphoric peak that fades quickly, and heavy cardiovascular strain (persistent tachycardia).
effectsSummary: Moderate euphoria, pronounced physical stimulation, marked tachycardia, stubborn insomnia, bruxism, and anxiety during comedown.
dosageRemark: Significantly longer duration of action than typical cathinones. Redosing leads to drug accumulation and severe insomnia.
generalRisks: Prolonged tachycardia, hypertension, hyperthermia, dehydration, paranoia, serotonin syndrome in combinations.
longtermRisks: Cardiovascular strain, chronic insomnia, anxiety disorders, psychological addiction.
saferUse: Test pills with reagent kits (frequent adulterant in counterfeit ecstasy)
Avoid redosing due to long elimination half-life
Never combine with other stimulants or antidepressants
Plan ample rest time following use

name: F-Phenibut

tolerance.full: within a couple of days of continuous use

addictionPotential: moderately physically and psychologically addictive
toxicities: potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like alcohol, benzodiazepines or opioids
summary:
F-Phenibut (Fluorophenibut, 4-fluorophenibut) is a fluorinated analogue of phenibut. While classic phenibut is primarily an alpha-2-delta voltage-dependent calcium channel blocker with weak GABA-B affinity, F-phenibut acts as a substantially more potent GABA-B receptor agonist, pharmacologically mirroring baclofen.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to classic phenibut, F-phenibut is 5 to 10 times more potent by weight (typical doses 100-250 mg versus 1000-2000 mg), takes effect much faster (30-45 minutes versus 2-4 hours), and has a shorter duration (6-8 hours versus 18-24 hours), yet carries identical risks of rapid physical dependency and brutal withdrawal syndrome.
effectsSummary: Potent anxiolysis, profound skeletal muscle relaxation, calming sedation, social disinhibition, bodily euphoria, and sleep promotion.
dosageRemark: ⚠️ MUCH MORE POTENT THAN PHENIBUT: Active threshold 50-100 mg. Doses above 300 mg cause heavy incapacitation. Always weigh on a 0.001g digital scale.
generalRisks: Motor ataxia, profound somnolence, vertigo, nausea, respiratory depression at elevated doses.
longtermRisks: Rapid development of severe physical dependence within consecutive days of use, accompanied by life-threatening autonomic withdrawal (delirium, convulsions).
saferUse: Limit consumption to a maximum of 1-2 non-consecutive days per week.
STRICTLY FORBIDDEN to combine with alcohol, benzodiazepines, GHB, or opioids.
Taper slowly if used consecutively for more than a few days.

name: Fenethylline
summary:
Fenethylline (Captagon) is a synthetic co-drug linking amphetamine covalently to theophylline via an alkyl bridge. Originally developed in 1961 for ADHD and narcolepsy, it is widely trafficked in the Middle East. Hepatic metabolism cleaves the molecule into active amphetamine and theophylline (a bronchodilator and adenosine antagonist).

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to pure amphetamine, fenethylline produces a smoother onset and less acute peripheral vasoconstriction due to the bronchodilating properties of theophylline. However, it carries identical risks of severe amphetamine addiction, sleep deprivation, and paranoid psychosis.
effectsSummary: Extreme physical stamina, total abolition of hunger and sleepiness, rapid speech, heightened vigilance, and aggressive confidence.
dosageRemark: ⚠️ ILLICIT COUNTERFEIT WARNING: Street 'Captagon' pills rarely contain authentic fenethylline, typically consisting of adulterated amphetamine, caffeine, and diphenhydramine mixtures.

summary:
Fentanyl is a synthetic opiate analgesic with a rapid onset and short duration of action. It is a strong agonist at the μ-opioid receptors and is historically used to treat breakthrough pain. Fentanyl is approximately 100 times more potent than Morphine, and is commonly used as a patch. Sometimes used as an adulterant for heroin, which has led to many overdose deaths.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to morphine, fentanyl is an ultra-lipophilic synthetic opioid roughly 50 to 100 times more potent by weight. It crosses the blood-brain barrier within seconds, inducing rapid respiratory arrest and chest wall rigidity ('wooden chest') upon rapid administration. Its razor-thin therapeutic index accounts for the overwhelming majority of modern accidental fatal overdoses.
effectsSummary: Fentanyl has a strong analgesic and sedative effect and is effective in the smallest doses. However, its euphoric effect is less pronounced than that of other opioids. It is used in emergency medicine for surgical procedures and anesthesia, and for breakthrough pain in cancer patients. For chronic pain, fentanyl patches are used, which release the active ingredient slowly. Due to its opioid properties, fentanyl rapidly leads to dependence when taken over a long period of time and should not be discontinued abruptly and only under medical supervision.
dosageRemark: ⚠️ EXTREME POTENCY (~100x IV Morphine): Dosages harmonized by route bioavailability (IV 100%: Heavy ~120 µg; Insufflated ~80%: Heavy ~140 µg; Sublingual ~50-65%: Heavy ~175 µg; Transdermal patch in µg/h every 72h).

The side effects are strongly dose-dependent. As the dose increases, the side effects also become more pronounced. At the beginning there is often drowsiness, dizziness, dizziness, pupil constriction, slowed heartbeat, drop in blood pressure, nausea and vomiting.
Excessive sweating, rashes, itching, central dullness, confusion, visual disturbances, cardiac arrhythmias, respiratory reflex depression and urinary retention may also occur.
Overdoses with fentanyl are life-threatening because the substance, like all opioids, slows down breathing, even to the point of respiratory arrest and coma.
longtermRisks: Regular, abusive use of fentanyl can lead to dependence with severe withdrawal symptoms such as seizures, sleep disorders and depression. Withdrawal, as with all opioids, should not be abrupt and should only take place under medical supervision.
saferUse: Opioids are highly effective drugs that should only be used for a limited time and at best under medical supervision.
Start with a low dose and wait for the effect and tolerance before adding more. Do not exceed the maximum daily dose.

If you inject opioids, dose even more carefully, as the range between desired effect (rush) and dangerous overdose is even more difficult to assess. Avoid injecting fentanyl; the risk of overdose is particularly high. Always use new (clean and sterile) injection material! Never exchange syringes, filters, water, disinfection swabs to avoid transmission of hepatitis and HIV.

Take longer breaks (at least several days) between consumption.
After a period of abstinence, take a much lower dose! The usual dose before the abstinence phase can otherwise quickly have life-threatening consequences.

The simultaneous consumption of depressant substances such as alcohol, ketamine, GHB/GBL, nitrous oxide, benzodiazepines and/or other opioids is dangerous as there is an increased risk of vomiting and unconsciousness. The risk of suffocation is high!

Taking benzodiazepines increases the effectiveness of the neurotransmitter gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) at the GABA-A receptor. This triggers sedative (calming), hypnotic, anxiolytic (anxiety-relieving), anticonvulsant (anticonvulsant) and muscle-relaxing effects in the body. Benzodiazepines have a depressant effect on the central nervous system. The flow of information in the brain between the brain cells (neurons) is thereby reduced / disturbed and feelings and perceptions are dampened.
The breakdown of the individual active ingredients of benzodiazepines in the body is age-dependent and therefore varies from person to person.

There is little information available on risks, toxicity, side effects and long-term consequences. Therefore, the general information on benzodiazepines applies:
When mixing with other downers (alcohol, GHB/GBL, heroin) there is a risk of respiratory paralysis!
Taking benzodiazepines can cause numerous undesirable side effects. In addition, regular and long-term use carries a very high risk of physical and psychological dependence. Benzodiazepines should only be taken as prescribed by a doctor and only for a short period of time (max. 4-6 weeks). Longer-term use should be discussed with the treating specialist. The dosages and duration of action of the individual benzodiazepines differ considerably.

Some benzodiazepines can cause seizures in epileptics.
longtermRisks:
Regular and long-term use can lead to psychological and physical dependence (very high dependence potential). Immediate discontinuation of the drug after prolonged use can lead to negative withdrawal symptoms (including dizziness, physical weakness, inner restlessness, tremors, sleep disturbances, headaches, sweating, nausea, hallucinations and depression).

Do not rely on dosage information from colleagues who regularly use benzodiazepines. Due to habituation or dependence, their doses can be much higher and fatal for new users.
Blisters of counterfeits may look identical to the original packaging.

summary:
Fluoxetine is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) antidepressant prescribed for major depressive disorder, generalized/social anxiety, panic disorder, OCD, and PTSD. Possesses a uniquely long elimination half-life (4-6 days for fluoxetine, 9-16 days for active metabolite norfluoxetine) and is a potent CYP2D6 inhibitor.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to other SSRIs (paroxetine, sertraline), fluoxetine (Prozac) features an exceptionally long elimination half-life (several days, and up to 2 weeks for active norfluoxetine). This built-in taper virtually eliminates acute discontinuation syndrome upon missed doses, but requires a strict 5-week washout before initiating MAO inhibitors.
effectsSummary: Gradually stabilizes mood and reduces anxiety/obsessive symptoms over 2-4 weeks; markedly blunts the subjective effects of classic psychedelics and MDMA while raising serotonin toxicity risk with serotonergic releasers/MAOIs.
dosageRemark: DAILY SCHEDULE: Usually taken once every 24 hours at a consistent time. The 'Heavy' threshold (60 mg) represents the maximum single unit dose per intake. (Up to 80 mg/day only in specialist OCD protocols). Interactions persist for up to 5 weeks after stopping Fluoxetine! Never double a dose if missed, and never stop abruptly without a medical tapering plan.
generalRisks: Initial nausea, diarrhea, headache, transient anxiety/insomnia or somnolence, sweating, sexual dysfunction (anorgasmia/low libido), bruxism, hyponatremia, and suicidal ideation monitoring during the first weeks in young adults.
longtermRisks: Discontinuation syndrome upon abrupt cessation ('brain zaps' / electric shock sensations, dizziness, rebound anxiety, flu-like symptoms), emotional blunting, weight changes, and persistent sexual side effects.
saferUse: Take at a fixed 24-hour interval and never exceed 60 mg in a single intake.
NEVER combine with MAOIs (wait at least 14 days after stopping SSRIs, or 5 weeks after Fluoxetine, before starting an MAOI), Tramadol, or Dextromethorphan (high Serotonin Syndrome risk!).
Avoid combining with NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Ketoprofen, Aspirin, etc.) without gastric protection due to elevated GI bleeding risk.
Do not take higher doses of MDMA or psychedelics to 'overcome' SSRI blunting — doing so risks fatal serotonin toxicity without restoring euphoria.
Taper gradually with your doctor when stopping treatment.

name: Flurbiprofen
addictionPotential: not habit-forming (no recreational or diversion potential)

summary:
Flurbiprofen is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID / AINS) used to treat pain, fever, and inflammation. Propionic acid NSAID (Antadys, Cebutid) very frequently prescribed for primary dysmenorrhea (menstrual cramps), dental pain, and rheumatology. Strict dosing intervals must be respected, and two different NSAIDs must never be combined.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Flurbiprofen (Ansaid) is a potent NSAID displaying high selectivity for suppressing uterine prostaglandin synthesis, making it frontline clinical pharmacotherapy for severe primary dysmenorrhea.
effectsSummary: Analgesic (pain relief), antipyretic (fever reduction), and anti-inflammatory effects via COX-1/COX-2 prostaglandin inhibition. No psychoactive or euphoric effect.
dosageRemark: STRICT INTERVAL: Wait at least 6 to 8 hours between two intakes. The 'Heavy' threshold (100 mg) represents the maximum single unit dose per intake. Maximum cumulative daily dose: 300 mg/24h (maximum 3 tablets of 100 mg per day). Always take with food or a full glass of water to protect the stomach.
generalRisks: Stomach pain, heartburn, nausea, peptic ulcers, gastrointestinal bleeding, fluid retention, elevated blood pressure, and acute renal impairment (especially when dehydrated). Can trigger severe bronchospasm in aspirin-sensitive asthma. Must NOT be used during pregnancy (especially from the 6th month onward) or during bacterial infections like varicella/streptococcal infections without medical advice.
longtermRisks: Chronic or repeated high-dose use causes gastric/duodenal ulcers, gastrointestinal perforation, chronic kidney disease (analgesic nephropathy), hypertension, and elevated risk of myocardial infarction or stroke.
saferUse: Strictly wait at least 6 to 8 hours between two doses and never exceed 300 mg/24h (maximum 3 tablets of 100 mg per day) in 24 hours.
Never exceed 100 mg in a single intake.
NEVER combine with another NSAID (e.g., Ibuprofen, Ketoprofen, Naproxen, Diclofenac, Aspirin at anti-inflammatory doses, Celecoxib).
Take during a meal with a large glass of water and stay well hydrated to protect your kidneys and stomach.
Avoid combining with Lithium (causes severe Lithium poisoning), oral corticosteroids, anticoagulants, or heavy alcohol use.

name: Gaboxadol
summary:
Gaboxadol (THIP) is a synthetic derivative of the Amanita muscaria alkaloid muscimol. It operates as a direct and selective agonist at extrasynaptic GABA-A receptors containing alpha-4, beta-3, and delta subunits, uniquely enhancing slow-wave non-REM deep sleep.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to zolpidem and benzodiazepines which modulate classical synaptic GABA-A sites, gaboxadol preserves natural sleep architecture without classical tolerance, but at higher doses evokes distinctive muscimol-like sensory distortions and dissociative dream states.

summary:

It acts as a selective, competitive acetylcholinesterase inhibitor (AChEI) and an allosteric potentiating ligand at nicotinic acetylcholine receptors. Prescribed for mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease, it is world-renowned as the premier pharmacological oneirogen for lucid dream induction.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to donepezil and rivastigmine, galantamine uniquely sensitizes presynaptic nicotinic receptors, dramatically multiplying REM sleep density, dream recall, and metacognitive awareness within dreams (lucid dreaming), while carrying typical peripheral cholinergic side effects (nausea, gastrointestinal cramps).
effectsSummary: Profound intensification of dream vividness, spontaneous dream lucidity, enhanced memory consolidation, and sharp cognitive focus.
dosageRemark: Lucid dreaming protocol: 4-8 mg taken after 4-5 hours of natural sleep (Wake-Back-To-Bed / WBTB protocol). Do NOT take at bedtime due to severe sleep onset disruption.

longtermRisks: Rapid receptor desensitization if used frequently (limit to once or twice weekly maximum), and cardiac rhythm abnormalities in predisposed patients.

Space sessions by at least 3-4 days to prevent rapid tolerance.

name: GBL

addictionPotential: highly physically and moderately to highly psychologically addictive
summary:
A pro-drug to GHB whose rapid absorption leads it to have a faster onset and shorter duration. Used in a similar manner to GHB, as a less-toxic alternative to alcohol. Consume slowly instead of as a "shot" to hugely improve safety and reduce overdose risk.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to GHB, GBL is roughly twice as potent by volume, hits much faster (10-15 min) with a steeper intoxicating peak, and is corrosive to mucous membranes if not heavily diluted.

The spectrum of effects ranges from euphoria, relaxation, disinhibition, intensification of perception, urge to talk (babble flash), slight dizziness and drowsiness to deep (coma-like) sleep or unconsciousness.
dosageRemark: The dosage depends on the degree of dilution and is even more delicate with GBL than with GHB, as not every body converts GBL into GHB at the same rate and in the same amount. GBL is a strong acid that can corrode the mucous membranes and must be heavily diluted with a non-alcoholic drink before drinking! In case of doubt: less is more!
generalRisks:
The higher the dose, the more likely nausea, vomiting and dizziness will occur. Headaches, confusion, breathing difficulties, cardiac arrhythmias, impaired balance and memory can occur at very high doses, as can uncontrollable muscle twitching, which is easily mistaken for epilepsy but can also progress into epilepsy.
The danger of an unintentional overdose is very high with GBL - even if it is not mixed! Signs of a GBL overdose are severe drowsiness followed by several hours of deep sleep that cannot be disturbed or can only be disturbed with difficulty (sometimes interrupted by short periods of wakefulness = standing man symptom), mild to very severe nausea, nausea, dizziness, headache, muscle atrophy (barely able to stay on one's feet) up to complete immobility, unconsciousness, disappearance of reflexes and breathing difficulties. It is difficult to assess whether users are only in a deep sleep or already in a coma after GBL use - if in doubt, always seek medical help!
longtermRisks: Regular use of GBL can lead to sleep disorders, anxiety and tremors; there is a risk of dependence with psychological and physical symptoms. In the case of chronic high-dose consumption (several doses daily), severe physical withdrawal symptoms such as sweating, muscle cramps or epileptic seizures occur upon discontinuation.
saferUse: If you are offered GBL, ask about the origin of the substance and the dosage.
GBL should be dosed lower than GHB! To produce the same effect, you need about half as much GBL as GHB.

Dose carefully! If GBL does not (yet) work, it is best to wait 2 hours and not add more right away. Often, overdosing is caused by adding more. Use an insulin syringe or graduated pipettes so that you can measure your unit of consumption accurately. Make a note of when you took your last dose.
Refrain from using GBL when you are alone.
With GBL, refrain from mixed consumption of any kind, especially with alcohol! Dilute the liquid before consumption, e.g. with tea.
If you have sex on GBL, follow the safe sex rules. Have condoms etc. ready before consumption.
People with epilepsy, heart or kidney dysfunction should not consume GBL under any circumstances!
GBL withdrawal should only be carried out under medical supervision.
Never leave your drink unattended to avoid someone mixing GBL into your drink. If your drink tastes strange, pour it out for your own safety.
