Headaches, confusion, breathing difficulties, cardiac arrhythmias, impaired balance and memory can occur at very high doses, as can uncontrollable muscle twitching, which is easily mistaken for epilepsy but can also progress into epilepsy.
The danger of an unintentional overdose is very high with GHB - even if it is not mixed! Signs of a GHB overdose are severe drowsiness followed by several hours of deep sleep that cannot be disturbed or can only be disturbed with difficulty (sometimes interrupted by short periods of wakefulness = standing man symptom), mild to very severe nausea, nausea, dizziness, headache, muscle atrophy (barely able to stay on one's feet) up to complete immobility, unconsciousness, disappearance of reflexes and breathing difficulties. It is difficult to assess whether users are only in a deep sleep or already in a coma after GHB use - if in doubt, always seek medical help!
longtermRisks: Regular use of GHB/GBL can lead to sleep disorders, anxiety and tremors; there is a risk of dependence with psychological and physical symptoms. In the case of chronic high-dose consumption (several doses daily), severe physical withdrawal symptoms such as sweating, muscle cramps or epileptic seizures occur upon discontinuation.
saferUse: If you are offered GHB, ask about the origin of the substance and the dosage.

Dose carefully! If GHB does not (yet) work, it is best to wait 2 hours and not add more right away. Often, overdosing is caused by adding more. Use an insulin syringe or graduated pipettes so that you can measure your unit of consumption accurately. Make a note of when you took your last dose.
Refrain from using GHB when you are alone.
With GHB, refrain from mixed consumption of any kind, especially with alcohol! Dilute the liquid before consumption, e.g. with tea.
If you have sex on GHB, follow the safe sex rules. Have condoms etc. ready before consumption.
People with epilepsy, heart or kidney dysfunction should not consume GHB under any circumstances!
GHB withdrawal should only be carried out under medical supervision.
Never leave your drink unattended to avoid someone mixing GHB into your drink. If your drink tastes strange, pour it out for your own safety.

name: Guanfacine

tolerance.full: steady therapeutic action over 1 - 3 weeks
tolerance.zero: MUST taper gradually (max 1 mg every 3-7 days) to avoid rebound hypertension!

addictionPotential: not habit-forming (causes physiological rebound hypertension/tachycardia if stopped abruptly)
toxicities: hypotension, bradycardia, syncope, and rebound hypertensive spike on abrupt withdrawal
summary:
Guanfacine (Intuniv, Tenex) is a selective postsynaptic alpha-2A adrenergic receptor agonist in the prefrontal cortex prescribed for ADHD (monotherapy or adjunct to stimulants), tic disorders/Tourette's, and rejection sensitivity/hyperarousal.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to clonidine, guanfacine (Intuniv) is a 25-fold more selective alpha-2A adrenergic agonist, strengthening prefrontal cortex working memory in ADHD with less daytime sedation and lower hypotensive side effects.
effectsSummary: Calms prefrontal hyperarousal, impulsivity, tics, and sympathetic stress while lowering blood pressure and heart rate; causes early somnolence.
dosageRemark: 24h DAILY SCHEDULE: Taken consistently once daily (avoid high-fat meals with Intuniv ER tablets as fat sharply increases peak Cmax and sedation!). The 'Heavy' threshold (4 mg) represents the standard maximum single tablet dose (up to 4-7 mg only in specific weight-based specialist regimens).
generalRisks: Somnolence, fatigue, hypotension, orthostatic dizziness/fainting, bradycardia, dry mouth, and constipation.
longtermRisks: Rebound hypertension, nervousness, and tachycardia if discontinued abruptly — always taper by <=1 mg every 3-7 days!
saferUse: Swallow Intuniv tablets whole (never crush/split) and avoid taking with high-fat meals.
NEVER stop Guanfacine abruptly — taper slowly with your physician to prevent dangerous rebound high blood pressure.
Avoid Alcohol, Benzodiazepines, Clonidine, Tizanidine, and Grapefruit/strong CYP3A4 inhibitors.

name: Haloperidol
toxicities: can have serious side effects at higher dosages
risk of having severe extrapyramidal symptoms and muscle rigidity
summary:
Haloperidol (Haldol) is a first-generation butyrophenone antipsychotic functioning as a high-potency dopamine D2 receptor antagonist. Widely utilized in acute psychiatric emergencies, delirium, and schizophrenia for its rapid neuroleptic action.

⚖️ Comparative profile: As the classic first-generation butyrophenone antipsychotic, haloperidol (Haldol) exerts potent, selective dopamine D2 antagonism without 5-HT2A blockade. Highly effective for acute agitation and psychosis, it carries a much higher incidence of extrapyramidal symptoms (akathisia, parkinsonism, acute dystonias) than second-generation atypical agents.
effectsSummary: Modulation of central neurotransmitters (dopamine, serotonin, norepinephrine), reduction of psychotic agitation or depressive mood, emotional stabilization, and variable sedation.
saferUse: Strictly adhere to the prescribed clinical dosage and schedule established by the treating physician.
Never discontinue treatment abruptly due to the risk of severe discontinuation syndrome or symptom rebound.
Avoid alcohol and illicit psychoactive substances which compromise therapeutic outcomes and augment toxicity.
Immediately report any movement disorders (extrapyramidal symptoms) or cardiovascular alterations to a physician.

name: Heroin

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

summary:
A powerful opioid derived from Morphine, with 2-4x its potency. Infamous for a high addiction potential and fatal respiratory depression in overdose, C. R. Alder Wright first synthesised this compound in 1874 trying to find a less addictive alternative to Morphine. In recent years, it has often been sold cut with the extremely potent fentanyl, causing a spike in overdose deaths.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to morphine, heroin (diacetylmorphine) is a lipophilic prodrug whose dual acetyl groups allow it to cross the blood-brain barrier within seconds. Once inside the central nervous system, rapid deacetylation into active 6-MAM and morphine produces an unmatched rush of euphoria and an extraordinarily severe physical addiction profile.
effectsSummary: Pain-relieving, balancing, calming, anxiety-relieving and euphoric. The euphoric "flash" at the beginning is followed by a state of well-being and a feeling of indifference, serenity, light-heartedness and self-satisfaction.
dosageRemark: The dose depends on the individual tolerance to heroin. The lethal dose in non-tolerant people is about 60 mg.
generalRisks:
Slowing of breathing, nausea, vomiting, itching, drop in blood pressure, pulse slowing, pupil constriction and urinary retention may occur.
Other side effects of regular use of heroin: confusion, disorientation, memory lapses, slurred and garbled speech as well as coordination disorders, extreme constipation, reduction of sexual desire and a potentially life-threatening reduction of the breathing rate to 2 to 4 breaths per minute (due to the attenuation of the coughing and breathing centre).
High doses of heroin can be fatal if medical help is not sought immediately!
The drug methadone is a synthetic opioid and is used as a substitute for heroin addiction. For users who are not used to opiates, the consumption of methadone even in small quantities can be life-threatening (severe respiratory depression, danger of suffocation).
Sniffing: damage to nasal septums and mucous membranes. Risk of hepatitis C infection.
Smoking: damage to bronchial tubes and lungs (lungs become sticky with daily use).
Injections: Venous inflammation and risk of infectious diseases (hepatitis C, HIV/AIDS, fungi). Organ damage can occur due to the impurities in heroin.
longtermRisks: The risk of dependence with psychological and physical symptoms is great. As soon as a tolerance has developed and the body is not supplied with the necessary amount of substance, physical withdrawal symptoms occur 8 to 12 hours after the last heroin intake. Withdrawal symptoms are sweating and chills, running eyes and nose, vomiting, diarrhoea, restlessness, irritability, weakness, anxiety, depressive states, painful cramps, insomnia and, less frequently, hallucinations, psychotic phases and seizures.
saferUse: Always use your own clean and new spraying equipment (needles, filters, spoons).
Follow the safe sniffing rules when sniffing.

Avoid mixed use with other substances, otherwise the effect becomes incalculable and the risks increase! Note that the combination with other downers (e.g. benzodiazepines) can lead to respiratory arrest.
The risk of overdose is particularly high after longer periods of non-use and with extremely "pure substance".
Consume in a quiet environment and not alone.

name: Hexedrone

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary:
A rare mephedrone analogue also known as MACP, a cathinone stimulant with similar effects to pentedrone.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to cocaine, hexedrone (NEH / Hexen) induces a very potent intranasal rush with a slightly longer duration (2-3h) but noticeable anxious tension towards the comedown.
effectsSummary: Heightened alertness and concentration, dopaminergic euphoria, physical and mental energy surge, increased heart rate, and appetite suppression.
saferUse: Stay hydrated regularly (water or electrolyte drinks, ~500 ml/h during exertion).
Avoid compulsive redosing which sharply escalates cardiotoxicity and hyperthermia.
Never combine with other stimulants, MAOIs, or decongestants.
Monitor blood pressure and body temperature, and ensure adequate recovery intervals.

name: HXE

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary:
Hydroxetamine (HXE, 3-HO-2'-Oxo-PCE) is a synthetic arylcyclohexylamine dissociative developed as a structural hybrid between methoxetamine (MXE) and 3-HO-PCE. It acts as an NMDA receptor antagonist featuring pronounced warm, relaxing, and analgesic qualities.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to MXE and ketamine, HXE produces a much more sedating, somatic 'couch-lock' dissociation with lower manic agitation, offering comforting warmth at slightly higher required doses (30-60 mg versus 20-40 mg for MXE).
effectsSummary: Deep physical dissociation, heavy bodily relaxation, peaceful mental disconnection, gentle visual distortions, and analgesia.
dosageRemark: Typical doses: 20-40 mg oral or insufflated. Duration of active effects: 3-5 hours.
generalRisks: Motor ataxia, psychomotor slowing, dizziness, cognitive confusion, and fall hazards.
longtermRisks: Psychological dependence, dissociative cross-tolerance, and potential urinary tract damage from chronic binging.
saferUse: Consume only while reclined in a quiet, safe setting.
Strictly avoid combining with alcohol, GHB, opioids, or benzodiazepines.

name: Hydrocodone

tolerance.full: with prolonged use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive
summary:
A codeine-derived opioid generally unheard of outside the United States. Generally mild in effects, used as an analgesic and cough-supressant. Sometimes used recreationally.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to Codeine, hydrocodone (Vicodin) is roughly 6 times more potent, providing superior pain relief and a warmer euphoric body high.
effectsSummary: Potent analgesia, warm sedation, opioid euphoria, sense of deep contentment, pinpoint pupils, respiratory depression, and gastrointestinal slowing.
saferUse: LETHAL OVERDOSE RISK: Always keep naloxone (Narcan, Nyxoid) immediately accessible.
NEVER combine with benzodiazepines, alcohol, pregabalin, or any CNS depressants.
Never use alone, and test with fentanyl/nitazene test strips before use.
Space doses strictly to prevent severe physical dependence and debilitating withdrawal.

name: Hydromorphone
summary:
An opioid that is roughly 5x the potency of IV Morphine. Only comes in IR tablets in the US, and is given mostly as XR in other countries. It is frequently used in hospitals for short immediate pain relief during procedures, requiring the patient to be awake. Also frequently used as a recreational opiate.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to oral Morphine, hydromorphone (Dilaudid) is 5-7 times more potent by dose, with less histamine itching and intense sedation.
dosageRemark: ⚠️ MAJOR BIOAVAILABILITY GAP BETWEEN ORAL (~20-25%) AND IV (100%): Orally ~5x more potent than oral morphine (Oral Heavy = 12 mg). Intravenously ~7.5x more potent than IV morphine (IV Heavy = 2 mg).
effectsSummary: Potent analgesia, warm sedation, opioid euphoria, sense of deep contentment, pinpoint pupils, respiratory depression, and gastrointestinal slowing.
saferUse: LETHAL OVERDOSE RISK: Always keep naloxone (Narcan, Nyxoid) immediately accessible.
NEVER combine with benzodiazepines, alcohol, pregabalin, or any CNS depressants.
Never use alone, and test with fentanyl/nitazene test strips before use.
Space doses strictly to prevent severe physical dependence and debilitating withdrawal.

name: Hydroxyzine

tolerance.full: sedative effect partially attenuates over 3 - 7 days

addictionPotential: not habit-forming (non-addictive alternative to benzodiazepines)
toxicities: CARDIAC QT INTERVAL PROLONGATION / Torsades de Pointes (strictly capped at 100 mg/day max in adults!)
additive CNS sedation and anticholinergic effects
summary:
Hydroxyzine (Atarax, Vistaril) is a first-generation piperazine H1 antihistamine with mild 5-HT2A antagonism, very widely prescribed as a non-addictive anxiolytic, preoperative sedative, sleep aid, and antipruritic (anti-itch). Subject to a strict 100 mg/day regulatory cap due to QT prolongation.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to benzodiazepines, hydroxyzine (Vistaril, Atarax) is a first-generation H1 receptor inverse agonist delivering rapid central anxiolysis within 30-45 minutes. It possesses zero physical addiction liability or withdrawal syndrome, representing the premier non-habit-forming alternative for acute anxiety.
effectsSummary: Calms acute anxiety and somatic tension, relieves itching/nausea, and induces drowsiness without physical dependence or benzodiazepine withdrawal.
dosageRemark: STRICT REGULATORY CAP: Space intakes by 6 to 8 hours (or take at bedtime). The 'Heavy' threshold (100 mg) is the strict maximum single AND 24-hour adult dose (50 mg/24h maximum in elderly patients) due to cardiac QT prolongation risk!
generalRisks: Drowsiness, dry mouth, fatigue, headache, dizziness, anticholinergic urinary hesitation/constipation, and cardiac QT interval prolongation.
longtermRisks: Minimal dependence risk; anticholinergic cognitive burden in elderly patients.
saferUse: Never exceed 100 mg in a single intake or within 24 hours (50 mg max in older adults).
STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED with other QT-prolonging drugs: Escitalopram (Seroplex), Citalopram (Seropram), Amisulpride, Cyamemazine (Tercian), Haloperidol, Methadone!
Avoid Alcohol, Opioids, and Benzodiazepines (markedly potentiates sedation and opioid respiratory depression).

name: Ibogaine
addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary:
An alkaloid found in many African plants most famously Iboga, with psychedelic and hallucinogenic properties. May be unpleasant. Traditionally used in tribal environments for coming-of-age rituals, it has recently been used as an alternative treatment for drug addiction although this usage has not been backed by conclusive data in humans. Has killed in overdose.

⚖️ Comparative profile: A multi-target monoterpene indole alkaloid from Tabernanthe iboga, renowned in addiction medicine for acutely interrupting opioid withdrawal and extinguishing drug craving over 24-36 hours, mandating continuous ECG telemetry due to hERG-mediated QTc prolongation.
effectsSummary: Intense sensory and visual alterations, altered perception of space and time, emotional amplification, deep introspection, and potential ego dissolution.
saferUse: Strictly respect Set & Setting (positive mindset, calm and secure physical environment).
Always have a trusted, sober tripsitter present during the experience.
Never combine with lithium, tramadol, or MAOI/SSRI antidepressants.
Test substances with colorimetric reagents prior to use and start with a low test dose.

name: Ibuprofen
addictionPotential: not habit-forming (no recreational or diversion potential)
toxicities: acute kidney injury and renal toxicity
increased cardiovascular thrombotic risk with high doses or prolonged use
summary:
Ibuprofen is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID / AINS) used to treat pain, fever, and inflammation. Commonly sold as 200 mg and 400 mg tablets (Advil, Nurofen, Spedifen) for headache, dental pain, dysmenorrhea, fever, and musculoskeletal inflammation. Strict dosing intervals must be respected, and two different NSAIDs must never be combined.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to paracetamol, ibuprofen is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) inhibiting COX-1 and COX-2 enzymes. It is markedly superior for pain with active inflammatory pathology (dental, arthritic, musculoskeletal), but carries risks of gastrointestinal ulceration and renal impairment with repeated use.
effectsSummary: Analgesic (pain relief), antipyretic (fever reduction), and anti-inflammatory effects via COX-1/COX-2 prostaglandin inhibition. No psychoactive or euphoric effect.
dosageRemark: STRICT INTERVAL: Wait at least 6 hours between two intakes. The 'Heavy' threshold (400 mg) represents the maximum single unit dose per intake. Maximum cumulative daily dose: 1200 mg/24h in self-medication (up to 2400 mg/24h only on explicit medical prescription). Always take with food or a full glass of water to protect the stomach.
generalRisks: Stomach pain, heartburn, nausea, peptic ulcers, gastrointestinal bleeding, fluid retention, elevated blood pressure, and acute renal impairment (especially when dehydrated). Can trigger severe bronchospasm in aspirin-sensitive asthma. Must NOT be used during pregnancy (especially from the 6th month onward) or during bacterial infections like varicella/streptococcal infections without medical advice.
longtermRisks: Chronic or repeated high-dose use causes gastric/duodenal ulcers, gastrointestinal perforation, chronic kidney disease (analgesic nephropathy), hypertension, and elevated risk of myocardial infarction or stroke.
saferUse: Strictly wait at least 6 hours between two doses and never exceed 1200 mg/24h in self-medication (up to 2400 mg/24h only on explicit medical prescription) in 24 hours.
Never exceed 400 mg in a single intake.
NEVER combine with another NSAID (e.g., Ibuprofen, Ketoprofen, Naproxen, Diclofenac, Aspirin at anti-inflammatory doses, Celecoxib).
Take during a meal with a large glass of water and stay well hydrated to protect your kidneys and stomach.
Avoid combining with Lithium (causes severe Lithium poisoning), oral corticosteroids, anticoagulants, or heavy alcohol use.

name: Imipramine

tolerance.full: 2 - 4 weeks for antidepressant action (immediate sedation)

addictionPotential: not habit-forming (no recreational potential), causes cholinergic rebound withdrawal if stopped suddenly
toxicities: HIGHLY CARDIOTOXIC in overdose (sodium-channel blockade, QRS widening, fatal ventricular arrhythmias, seizures, coma)
serotonin syndrome with MAOIs/Tramadol/SSRIs and severe anticholinergic toxicity
summary:
Imipramine is a tricyclic antidepressant (TCA) acting as a serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor alongside strong antihistaminic, anticholinergic, and alpha-1 blocking properties. Prototypical tricyclic antidepressant (Tofranil) prescribed for major depression, panic disorder, neuropathic pain, and nocturnal enuresis.

⚖️ Comparative profile: The original prototype tricyclic antidepressant (Tofranil), imipramine serves as a clinical benchmark for severe melancholic depression and nocturnal enuresis, metabolized into desipramine.
effectsSummary: Antidepressant, neuropathic pain relief, and strong sedation/sleep induction; causes dry mouth, constipation, orthostatic dizziness, and blurred vision.
dosageRemark: NARROW THERAPEUTIC MARGIN: The 'Heavy' threshold (100 mg) represents the maximum single outpatient unit dose per intake (higher daily totals up to 150-200 mg/24h are divided or strictly supervised). Often taken in the evening due to sedation.
generalRisks: Sedation, dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention, blurred vision, tachycardia, orthostatic hypotension, QT/QRS prolongation, lowered seizure threshold, and severe cardiotoxicity in overdose.
longtermRisks: Weight gain, dental caries (from chronic dry mouth), anticholinergic cognitive burden, and withdrawal symptoms if stopped abruptly.
saferUse: Never exceed 100 mg in a single outpatient intake — tricyclic overdose is rapidly cardiotoxic.
NEVER combine with MAOIs, Tramadol, MDMA, or Clonidine.
Avoid combining with LSD/psychedelics (markedly intensifies trips and lowers seizure threshold!), Alcohol, Benzodiazepines, Opioids, or anticholinergics.

name: Isopropylphenidate

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary:
IPPH (or incorrectly IPH) is a novel piperidine based methylphenidate analogue and NDRI stimulant, but comes with much less physical side effects.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to methylphenidate, IPPH focuses almost exclusively on mental focus and wakefulness, eliminating physical jitteriness and jaw clenching.
effectsSummary: Heightened alertness and concentration, dopaminergic euphoria, physical and mental energy surge, increased heart rate, and appetite suppression.
saferUse: Stay hydrated regularly (water or electrolyte drinks, ~500 ml/h during exertion).
Avoid compulsive redosing which sharply escalates cardiotoxicity and hyperthermia.
Never combine with other stimulants, MAOIs, or decongestants.
Monitor blood pressure and body temperature, and ensure adequate recovery intervals.

name: JWH-018

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary:
JWH-018 is a synthetic cannabinoid of the naphthoylindole class, synthesized by chemist John W. Huffman. It emerged in the late 2000s as the primary active synthetic cannabinoid in early 'Spice' and 'K2' incense blends. It acts as an extremely potent full agonist at both CB1 and CB2 cannabinoid receptors with 4-fold higher affinity than THC.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to natural THC (which acts as a partial CB1 agonist with an intrinsic safety ceiling), JWH-018 is a high-efficacy full agonist. Receptor saturation triggers acute toxicities virtually unseen with herbal cannabis: malignant tachyarrhythmias, grand mal seizures, severe panic, and acute toxic psychosis.
effectsSummary: Explosive onset within seconds, intense sensory distortion, fleeting synthetic euphoria, marked paranoia, cognitive disconnection, and heavy sedation.
dosageRemark: ⚠️ EXTREME MILLIGRAM POTENCY: Active at 0.5 to 2 mg. Unregulated synthetic herbal blends frequently contain deadly localized 'hotspots'.
generalRisks: Severe tachycardia, panic attacks, visual/auditory hallucinations, seizures, hypothermia, acute vomiting, and syncope.
longtermRisks: Rapid, severe physical dependence with punishing withdrawal (intense sweating, total insomnia, nausea, tremors), extreme tolerance, and prolonged psychiatric impairment.
saferUse: Avoid pre-sprayed herbal blends ('Spice/K2') with unpredictable concentrations.
If handling pure powder, utilize accurate volumetric dilution.
Keep emergency benzodiazepines available to manage panic and seizure risks.

name: JWH-073

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary:
JWH-073 is a synthetic cannabinoid of the naphthoylindole class, functioning as the butyl homologue of JWH-018. Featured in early 'Spice' blends, it acts as a high-potency agonist at CB1 and CB2 cannabinoid receptors.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to JWH-018, JWH-073 exhibits lower binding affinity at the CB1 receptor, resulting in roughly half the potency and a more sedating, relaxing cannabis-like stone with reduced propensity for acute panic, though still carrying synthetic cannabinoid overdose hazards.
effectsSummary: Heavy bodily stone, sedation, mild sensory enhancement, appetite stimulation, and altered time perception.
dosageRemark: ⚠️ MILLIGRAM POWDER: Active at 2-5 mg vaporized. Never eyeball pure powder.
generalRisks: Tachycardia, acute sedation, panic, dizziness, and cognitive disorientation.
longtermRisks: Rapid tolerance, severe physical withdrawal upon cessation, and cognitive blunting.
saferUse: Avoid unregulated commercial spice incense blends.
Keep emergency benzodiazepines available for acute panic episodes.

name: Ketamine

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderate to high abuse potential and produces psychological dependence with chronic use
summary:
A short acting dissociative anaesthetic and hallucinogen commonly used in emergency medicine. It is the prototypical dissociative, and is widely used at sub-anesthetic doses recreationally. Small doses are comparable with alcohol, while larger doses are immobilising and lead to psychedelic experiences: the "K-Hole."

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to PCP and MXE, ketamine is a short-acting arylcyclohexylamine dissociative (45-60 minute duration) with a favorable airway safety profile. At peak doses, it induces the complete sensory detachment known as the 'K-hole'. However, chronic frequent abuse generates severe, irreversible ulcerative cystitis of the bladder and biliary dilation.
effectsSummary:
The effect of ketamine as an intoxicant is strongly dependent on the dosage: In lower doses, it has a disinhibiting and relaxing effect similar to alcohol, while higher doses can induce trance-like states up to out-of-body or near-death experiences (K-Hole). There can be a fragmentary dissolution of the environment and bodily sensation, thoughts can break off, feelings of weightlessness or floating can appear. Sensory perceptions and the sense of space-time change. At higher doses, detachment from one's own body and/or ego dissolution or merging with the environment may occur.
After the trip: drowsiness, memory of the experience is often only partially possible.
dosageRemark: The dosage of ketamine depends strongly on the desired effect.
generalRisks:
Movement and communication may be severely restricted. Partial or complete insensitivity to pain, coordination disorders, sensation of weakness, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, uncoordinated muscle movements, dizziness, slurred speech, increased pulse and blood pressure and cardiac arrhythmias. At high doses, muscle stiffness, paralysis and narcosis, at very high doses, epileptic seizures and coma.
Ketamine puts a strain on the cardiovascular system. A ketamine trip can be psychologically very stressful. Many ketamine users report near-death experiences, nightmare hallucinations, tunnel visions, blackouts and short periods of memory loss.
After repeated consumption within a short period of time, the effect diminishes considerably and a tolerance develops.
Ketamine taken intravenously quicker than 1.5 minute can cause breathing depression for up to a minute.
longtermRisks: Ketamine can cause dependence with psychological symptoms. Chronic use damages the liver and kidneys and can lead to depressive moods and anxiety. It is suspected that even in small doses, ketamine can trigger dysfunctions in areas of the brain responsible for memory, learning and perception. The more often it is consumed and the larger the individual doses, the more alarming these disturbances become.
saferUse: Ketamine is not a party drug! Do not take ketamine alone and make sure you are in a familiar and comfortable environment. Allow enough time to process the trip in peace afterwards.
Dose carefully. Small differences in dose can cause significant differences in effect, so dosing is difficult.
Take regular breaks from consumption.
You need a place to sit or lie down, because at high doses there is a great risk of collapsing or fainting.
Because of the insensitivity to pain, you can hurt yourself without noticing it.
Do not take ketamine on a full stomach.

Refrain from mixed consumption. When combined with alcohol, benzodiazepines or opiates, there is a risk of respiratory arrest! Mixing with uppers (e.g. cocaine) can lead to circulatory problems, increase in heart rate and shortness of breath.
People with cardiovascular problems, high blood pressure or glaucoma should absolutely refrain from consuming ketamine!

name: Ketoprofen
addictionPotential: not habit-forming (no recreational or diversion potential)
toxicities: acute kidney injury and renal toxicity
increased cardiovascular thrombotic risk with high doses or prolonged use
summary:
Ketoprofen is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID / AINS) used to treat pain, fever, and inflammation. Potent propionic acid NSAID (Profenid, Toprec) widely prescribed for acute inflammatory, dental, rheumatic, and traumatic pain. Carries higher gastric ulcer risk than ibuprofen. Strict dosing intervals must be respected, and two different NSAIDs must never be combined.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to ibuprofen, ketoprofen is roughly 4 times more potent by weight, delivering powerful, fast-acting analgesia for acute musculoskeletal flare-ups and renal colic, with heightened gastrointestinal sensitivity.
effectsSummary: Analgesic (pain relief), antipyretic (fever reduction), and anti-inflammatory effects via COX-1/COX-2 prostaglandin inhibition. No psychoactive or euphoric effect.
dosageRemark: STRICT INTERVAL: Wait at least 6 to 8 hours between two intakes. The 'Heavy' threshold (100 mg) represents the maximum single unit dose per intake. Maximum cumulative daily dose: 200 mg/24h (or 150 mg/24h in elderly/fragile patients). Always take with food or a full glass of water to protect the stomach.
generalRisks: Stomach pain, heartburn, nausea, peptic ulcers, gastrointestinal bleeding, fluid retention, elevated blood pressure, and acute renal impairment (especially when dehydrated). Can trigger severe bronchospasm in aspirin-sensitive asthma. Must NOT be used during pregnancy (especially from the 6th month onward) or during bacterial infections like varicella/streptococcal infections without medical advice.
longtermRisks: Chronic or repeated high-dose use causes gastric/duodenal ulcers, gastrointestinal perforation, chronic kidney disease (analgesic nephropathy), hypertension, and elevated risk of myocardial infarction or stroke.
saferUse: Strictly wait at least 6 to 8 hours between two doses and never exceed 200 mg/24h (or 150 mg/24h in elderly/fragile patients) in 24 hours.
Never exceed 100 mg in a single intake.
NEVER combine with another NSAID (e.g., Ibuprofen, Ketoprofen, Naproxen, Diclofenac, Aspirin at anti-inflammatory doses, Celecoxib).
Take during a meal with a large glass of water and stay well hydrated to protect your kidneys and stomach.
Avoid combining with Lithium (causes severe Lithium poisoning), oral corticosteroids, anticoagulants, or heavy alcohol use.

name: Kratom

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: produces dependence with chronic use and has a high abuse potential
summary:
A drug made out of the leaves of Mitragyna Speciosa, which is related to coffee. Stimulating at lower doses, with opioid effects at higher doses. Frequent heavy use can cause physical addiction and withdrawals.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to pharmaceutical opioids, kratom features a unique natural biphasic profile: stimulating at lower doses (<3g) and sedating/analgesic at higher doses (>5g), with significantly lower risk of fatal respiratory depression.
effectsSummary: Heightened alertness and concentration, dopaminergic euphoria, physical and mental energy surge, increased heart rate, and appetite suppression.
saferUse: Stay hydrated regularly (water or electrolyte drinks, ~500 ml/h during exertion).
Avoid compulsive redosing which sharply escalates cardiotoxicity and hyperthermia.
Never combine with other stimulants, MAOIs, or decongestants.
Monitor blood pressure and body temperature, and ensure adequate recovery intervals.

name: LAE-32
summary:
LAE-32 (D-lysergic acid ethylamide) is an ergot derivative synthesized by Albert Hofmann during early lysergamide investigations. Standing structurally between ergine (LSA) and LSD, it operates as a partial 5-HT2A agonist with distinct central sedative properties.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to LSD-25, LAE-32 is approximately 20-30 times less potent by weight (effective at 0.5-1.5 mg versus 50-100 µg for LSD), inducing far fewer visual geometric distortions and instead evoking a tranquil state of emotional indifference and introspective sedation.
effectsSummary: Sedating psychedelic relaxation, emotional detachement, abstract thoughts, mild perceptual softening, and physical calm.
dosageRemark: Active dose range: 500-1500 µg orally or sublingually. Active duration: 6-10 hours.
generalRisks: Lethargy, muscular heaviness, mild nausea, and peripheral vasoconstriction.
longtermRisks: Cross-tolerance to all serotonergic psychedelics.
saferUse: Consume in a peaceful setting with comfortable rest facilities.
Do not drive or operate machinery.

name: Lamotrigine
addictionPotential: not habit-forming
toxicities: LIFE-THREATENING SKIN RASH (Stevens-Johnson Syndrome / Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis) if titrated too fast, restarted at full dose after >5 days off, or combined with Valproate without halving the dose!
summary:
Lamotrigine (Lamictal) is a voltage-gated sodium-channel / glutamate-release modulating anticonvulsant and bipolar mood stabilizer (particularly effective for preventing bipolar depressive episodes).

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to lithium and valproate which primarily manage mania, lamotrigine (Lamictal) is uniquely effective for preventing recurring bipolar depressive episodes without weight gain or cognitive blunting. It mandates strict, slow dose titration to prevent life-threatening Stevens-Johnson skin necrosis.
effectsSummary: Stabilizes mood and seizure threshold without weight gain or heavy sedation; requires slow multi-week upward titration.
dosageRemark: STRICT TITRATION & SCHEDULE: Taken once every 24h or split every 12h. The 'Heavy' threshold (200 mg) is the standard maximum single unit intake (daily totals up to 200-400 mg/24h; MAX 100-200 mg/24h if co-prescribed Valproate/Dépakine!). CRITICAL: If you miss Lamotrigine for >= 5 consecutive days, DO NOT restart your full maintenance dose — consult your doctor to re-titrate from 25 mg!
generalRisks: Skin rash (seek urgent medical evaluation for ANY new rash, fever, or mouth/eye sores, especially during the first 8 weeks!), headache, dizziness, diplopia (double vision), insomnia, or nausea.
longtermRisks: Minimal metabolic or organ toxicity once safely past the initial titration window.
saferUse: Seek immediate medical care if ANY rash, blistering, fever, or swollen lymph nodes appear.
Valproate (Dépakine/Depakote) DOUBLES Lamotrigine blood levels — Lamotrigine doses MUST be halved under medical supervision to avoid fatal Stevens-Johnson syndrome!
Estrogen-containing hormonal birth control reduces Lamotrigine blood levels by ~50% (and levels spike during pill-free week) — inform your prescriber.
Never restart at full dose if you stopped taking Lamotrigine for more than 5 days.

name: Levetiracetam
addictionPotential: not habit-forming
toxicities: neuropsychiatric behavioral adverse effects (severe irritability, agitation, mood swings / 'Keppra rage', depression)
summary:
Levetiracetam (Keppra) is a widely prescribed SV2A-binding anticonvulsant requiring strict 12-hour twice-daily dosing. Minimal hepatic drug interactions, but well-known for potential psychiatric side effects (irritability, anxiety, mood lability).

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to classic anticonvulsants, levetiracetam (Keppra) binds presynaptic vesicle protein SV2A, completely avoiding CYP450 drug interactions. However, it triggers neuropsychiatric side effects (irritability, mood swings, agitation, 'Kepprage') in 10-15% of patients.
effectsSummary: Prevents focal and generalized seizures; may cause somnolence, fatigue, dizziness, or marked irritability/emotional lability.
dosageRemark: STRICT 12-HOUR INTERVAL: Must be taken twice daily every 12 hours (typically 500 mg to 1500 mg twice daily). The 'Heavy' threshold (1500 mg) is the maximum single unit intake (3000 mg/24h maximum).
generalRisks: Somnolence, asthenia, dizziness, irritability, aggression, anxiety, depressive mood shifts (report severe mood changes to your neurologist!), and withdrawal seizures if stopped abruptly.
longtermRisks: Minimal organ or hepatic toxicity; adjust dose in renal impairment.
saferUse: Strictly respect the 12-hour interval between morning and evening doses and never stop abruptly.
Avoid Alcohol and sedating drugs (worsens somnolence and lowers seizure control); monitor mood and irritability.

name: Levomepromazine

tolerance.full: antipsychotic stabilization over 1 - 4 weeks
tolerance.zero: taper gradually to prevent rebound symptoms

addictionPotential: not habit-forming (abrupt cessation causes rebound insomnia, nausea, or psychotic relapse)
toxicities: QT interval prolongation / cardiac arrhythmia risk
extrapyramidal motor symptoms (akathisia, dystonia, parkinsonism) and rare neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS)
summary:
Levomepromazine is a prescription antipsychotic (neuroleptic) medication used in schizophrenia, bipolar mania/maintenance, or severe agitation. Highly sedative aliphatic phenothiazine neuroleptic (Nozinan) with potent H1/alpha-1/5-HT2 blockade and intrinsic analgesic properties, used in severe psychosis, agitation, and palliative pain/nausea.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Levomepromazine (methotrimeprazine, Nozinan) is a potent first-generation phenothiazine neuroleptic widely utilized in palliative medicine and severe psychosis for profound sedation, anxiolysis, and adjuvant analgesia.
effectsSummary: Dopamine D2 / serotonin receptor antagonism (or partial agonism) reducing hallucinations, delusions, mania, agitation, and psychedelic 5-HT2A/dopaminergic effects.
dosageRemark: DIVIDED OR BEDTIME SCHEDULE: Low doses (6-25 mg) at bedtime for severe insomnia/pain; higher antipsychotic daily totals are divided across 2-3 intakes. The 'Heavy' threshold (100 mg) represents the maximum single unit oral intake. Never stop antipsychotic treatment abruptly without medical guidance.
generalRisks: Sedation or akathisia (inner restlessness), orthostatic hypotension, dizziness, weight gain, elevated prolactin, extrapyramidal stiffness/tremor, QT prolongation, and rare Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (high fever + muscle rigidity = medical emergency).
longtermRisks: Weight gain, insulin resistance/type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hyperprolactinemia, and tardive dyskinesia with chronic exposure.
saferUse: Respect your prescribed schedule and never exceed 100 mg in a single intake.
Avoid Alcohol, Opioids, and unprescribed sedatives (additive CNS depression and hypotension).
Avoid combining with other QT-prolonging medications (Escitalopram, Citalopram, Hydroxyzine, Methadone) without ECG monitoring.
Seek immediate emergency care if high fever, severe muscle stiffness, and confusion occur (Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome).

name: Lisdexamfetamine
summary:
Lisdexamfetamine (Vyvanse, Elvanse) is an inactive prodrug composed of dextroamphetamine coupled to L-lysine, approved for ADHD and binge eating disorder. It requires enzymatic hydrolysis by red blood cells to liberate active dextroamphetamine, providing a smooth, steady therapeutic duration of 10 to 14 hours with substantially diminished abuse potential via non-oral routes.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to methylphenidate (Ritalin) and instant-release amphetamine salts (Adderall), lisdexamfetamine provides a significantly smoother pharmacokinetic curve without sharp euphoric spikes or abrupt evening crashes, while remaining abuse-deterrent against crushing, snorting, or injection.
effectsSummary: Substantial enhancement of sustained focus, vigilance, decreased impulsivity, marked appetite suppression, smooth physical wakefulness, and daytime emotional consistency.
dosageRemark: ⚠️ MORNING DOSING ONLY: Begin at 20-30 mg daily in the morning. Taking past noon causes severe sleep latency. Maximum standard dose: 70 mg/day.
generalRisks: Insomnia, appetite loss, weight loss, tachycardia, hypertension, dry mouth, irritability, and anxiety.
longtermRisks: Psychological dependence, cardiovascular strain, chronic weight loss, and potential exacerbation of underlying psychiatric conditions.
saferUse: Take strictly in the morning with breakfast to prevent sleep disruption.
Stay hydrated and intentionally schedule balanced meals despite appetite blunting.
Regularly check blood pressure and resting heart rate.
Avoid combining with caffeine or other sympathomimetics.

name: Lithium
addictionPotential: not habit-forming
toxicities: VERY NARROW THERAPEUTIC INDEX: acute lithium toxicity (>1.2-1.5 mmol/L) causes coarse tremor, ataxia, vomiting, confusion, seizures, arrhythmias, renal failure, and coma
EXTREME SEIZURE & FUGUE RISK when combined with classic Psychedelics (LSD, Psilocybin, DMT, Mescaline, 2C-x)!
SEVERE LITHIUM POISONING when combined with NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Ketoprofen, Naproxen, Diclofenac, Coxibs) or dehydration!
summary:
Lithium carbonate (Téralithe) is the gold-standard mood stabilizer for bipolar disorder (mania prevention, bipolar depression, and suicide risk reduction). It has a very narrow therapeutic window monitored via serum lithemia (0.5-0.8 to 1.0 mmol/L) and TWO CRITICAL INTERACTIONS: NSAIDs cause acute lithium poisoning by blocking kidney excretion, and Psychedelics (LSD, mushrooms) provoke generalized seizures!

⚖️ Comparative profile: Lithium remains the gold standard mood stabilizer for bipolar disorder, exhibiting a unique, proven anti-suicidal efficacy not shared by anticonvulsants. However, its therapeutic window is razor-thin (target serum level 0.6-1.0 mEq/L), requiring regular lab monitoring to prevent toxic neurotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, and hypothyroidism.
effectsSummary: Stabilizes manic and depressive mood cycling; causes increased thirst/urination (polyuria/polydipsia) and fine hand tremor at therapeutic levels.
dosageRemark: STRICT SCHEDULE & LITHEMIA: Immediate-release Lithium carbonate (e.g. Téralithe 250 mg) is typically taken 2 to 3 times daily (every 8-12 hours). The 'Heavy' threshold (500 mg = two 250 mg IR tablets) represents the upper standard single immediate-release intake (daily totals of 500-1250 mg are divided and strictly guided by 12-hour trough serum blood tests!).
generalRisks: Fine postural hand tremor, increased thirst and urination, nausea/diarrhea, weight gain, acne/psoriasis flare. Warning signs of Lithium toxicity (go to ER / check lithemia immediately!): coarse shaking, slurred speech, unsteady gait, persistent vomiting/diarrhea, confusion, or muscle twitching.
longtermRisks: Hypothyroidism, hyperparathyroidism, nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, and progressive chronic kidney function decline (requires regular TSH, creatinine, calcium, and serum lithium checks).
saferUse: NEVER take NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Advil, Nurofen, Profenid, Ketoprofen, Voltarène, Apranax, Celebrex) while on Lithium — use Paracetamol for pain instead!
NEVER combine Lithium with classic Psychedelics (LSD, Psilocybin mushrooms, DMT, 2C-B, Mescaline, NBOMe) — notoriously high incidence of grand mal seizures and dissociative fugue emergencies!
Stay consistently hydrated and keep salt (sodium) and caffeine intake steady — dehydration, heavy sweating, vomiting/diarrhea, or low-salt diets rapidly trigger Lithium poisoning!

name: Loprazolam

tolerance.full: develops rapidly within days to 2 weeks of daily use

addictionPotential: extremely physically and psychologically addictive (severe/fatal withdrawal seizures if stopped abruptly!)
toxicities: low organ toxicity alone, but HIGHLY LETHAL respiratory depression when mixed with Alcohol, Opioids, GHB/GBL, or Barbiturates
summary:
Loprazolam is a prescription benzodiazepine acting as a positive allosteric modulator of GABA-A receptors. Potent intermediate-acting imidazobenzodiazepine hypnotic (Havlane 1 mg) prescribed for severe short-term insomnia. Approximate potency equivalence: ~1 mg Loprazolam ≈ 10 mg Diazepam. Do not combine with other CNS depressants.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to standard hypnotics, loprazolam is a potent imidazobenzodiazepine with intermediate duration (6-10 hours), promoting continuous slow-wave sleep architecture with minimal morning residual grogginess.
effectsSummary: Anxiolysis (anxiety relief), sedation, hypnosis (sleep induction), muscle relaxation, anticonvulsant action; at higher/diverted doses causes disinhibition, motor ataxia, slurred speech, and anterograde amnesia ('blackouts').
dosageRemark: DIVERSION-ADAPTED DOSAGES: Dosages reflect both therapeutic and diverted/recreational usage (~1 mg ≈ 10 mg Diazepam). Doses in the 'Strong'/'Heavy' range (>=2-3 mg) frequently cause amnesia, compulsive redosing, delusion of sobriety, and behavioral disinhibition.
generalRisks: Drowsiness, impaired driving/coordination, memory blackouts, paradoxical aggression or disinhibition, falls, and fatal respiratory arrest if combined with opioids, alcohol, GHB, or other sedatives.
longtermRisks: Severe physical and psychological dependence (medical prescriptions should normally not exceed 4-12 weeks for anxiety or 4 weeks for insomnia). NEVER stop abruptly after daily use: benzodiazepine withdrawal can cause rebound panic, insomnia, tremors, delirium, and potentially fatal generalized seizures — always taper slowly under medical supervision!
saferUse: NEVER mix with Alcohol, Opioids (Codeine, Tramadol, Morphine, Oxycodone, Heroin, Methadone, Opium), GHB/GBL, Barbiturates, or Pregabalin (life-threatening respiratory arrest!).
Beware of 'delusion of sobriety' and memory blackouts that lead to accidental compulsive redosing — log every intake immediately.
Limit continuous daily use to prevent severe physical dependence, and NEVER stop cold-turkey after prolonged use (gradual medical taper mandatory).

name: Lorazepam

tolerance.full: within a couple of days of continuous use

addictionPotential: extremely physically and psychologically addictive
toxicities: potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like alcohol or opioids
summary:
An intermediate acting benzodiazepine commonly known as Ativan, commonly prescribed as an alternative to Xanax. Sedating, hypnotic and anxiolytic. Potential to induce amnesia and lowered inhibitions in overdose. Do not combine with other depressants.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to alprazolam (Xanax) and diazepam, lorazepam (Ativan) is a high-potency anxiolytic and sedative cleared via direct hepatic glucuronidation without CYP450 pathways. It serves as the frontline clinical antidote for status epilepticus seizures, though carrying a pronounced tendency to induce anterograde memory amnesia.
effectsSummary:
Lorazepam has a calming, relaxing, antispasmodic, anti-anxiety and sleep-inducing effect.
Taking benzodiazepines increases the effectiveness of the neurotransmitter gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) at the GABA-A receptor. This triggers sedative (calming), hypnotic, anxiolytic (anxiety-relieving), anticonvulsant (anticonvulsant) and muscle-relaxing effects in the body. Benzodiazepines have a depressant effect on the central nervous system. The flow of information in the brain between the brain cells (neurons) is thereby reduced / disturbed and feelings and perceptions are dampened.
The breakdown of the individual active ingredients of benzodiazepines in the body is age-dependent and therefore varies from person to person.
generalRisks:
There is little information available on risks, toxicity, side effects and long-term consequences. Therefore, the general information on benzodiazepines applies:
When mixing with other downers (alcohol, GHB/GBL, heroin) there is a risk of respiratory paralysis!
Taking benzodiazepines can cause numerous undesirable side effects. In addition, regular and long-term use carries a very high risk of physical and psychological dependence. Benzodiazepines should only be taken as prescribed by a doctor and only for a short period of time (max. 4-6 weeks). Longer-term use should be discussed with the treating specialist. The dosages and duration of action of the individual benzodiazepines differ considerably.
Side effects of benzodiazepines may be as follows: Prolonged fatigue, gastrointestinal problems, impaired reactions, hypersensitivity reactions, headaches, dizziness, motor difficulties, visual disturbances, slowed breathing, muscle weakness, confusion, sexual dysfunction, aggression, outbursts of anger, restlessness, random movements, allergies, skin problems/rashes and speech and movement disorders. Some benzodiazepines can cause seizures in epileptics.
longtermRisks:
Regular and long-term use can lead to psychological and physical dependence (very high dependence potential). Immediate discontinuation of the drug after prolonged use can lead to negative withdrawal symptoms (including dizziness, physical weakness, inner restlessness, tremors, sleep disturbances, headaches, sweating, nausea, hallucinations and depression).
In addition, seizures and memory disorders/loss and listlessness (hangover effects) can occur. In case of possible dependence, withdrawal should be discussed with a doctor beforehand and the withdrawal should be medically accompanied. It is extremely important that the dose is reduced gradually.
saferUse: If medicines are obtained on the black market or on the internet and not from a pharmacy/medical facility, the contents are unclear. Have the medicine tested for the exact ingredients in a drug check!
Do not rely on dosage information from colleagues who regularly use benzodiazepines. Due to habituation or dependence, their doses can be much higher and fatal for new users.
Blisters of counterfeits may look identical to the original packaging.

The simultaneous consumption of depressant substances such as alcohol, ketamine, GHB/GBL, nitrous oxide, opioids and/or other benzodiazepines is dangerous as there is an increased risk of vomiting and unconsciousness. The risk of suffocation is high!

name: LSA

tolerance.full: almost immediately after ingestion

addictionPotential: non-addictive with a low abuse potential
summary:
A chemical found in Morning Glory and Hawaiian Baby Woodrose seeds, which are often legally available. Has mental effects similar to LSD, although with almost no visual effects. It is famous for being very nauseating, and for causing excessive time dilation at higher doses.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to LSD, natural LSA (Morning Glory / HBWR) is much more physically sedating and heavy, with frequent initial nausea and less sharp geometric visuals.
effectsSummary: Intense sensory and visual alterations, altered perception of space and time, emotional amplification, deep introspection, and potential ego dissolution.
saferUse: Strictly respect Set & Setting (positive mindset, calm and secure physical environment).
Always have a trusted, sober tripsitter present during the experience.
Never combine with lithium, tramadol, or MAOI/SSRI antidepressants.
Test substances with colorimetric reagents prior to use and start with a low test dose.

name: LSD

tolerance.full: almost immediately after ingestion

addictionPotential: non-addictive with a low abuse potential
toxicities: extremely low toxicity relative to dose
summary:
LSD is a popular psychedelic with a relatively long history of use and research, and as such is known to be relatively safe despite its extremely high potency. It is the archetypical psychedelic to which all others are compared, and remains in popular usage.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to psilocybin (magic mushrooms), LSD is roughly 100 to 200 times more potent by weight (active at 20-50 µg), lasts twice as long (10-14 hours), and features dopamine D2 affinity that produces a crisper, more electric and analytical headspace compared to psilocybin's grounded, emotional, and somatic experience.
effectsSummary: The effect is very much dependent on dose, set and setting. As a hallucinogen, LSD intensifies and alienates sensory perceptions and the sense of space-time. Mood and feelings can change abruptly. At higher doses, feelings of detachment from one's own body can occur. Especially in the initial phase of the trip, slight breathing difficulties, palpitations, sweating, altered blood pressure and nausea may occur.
generalRisks:
The risks of LSD use are psychological and depend on the personality structure of the user. The perceptual changes during a trip can be so intense that inexperienced users in particular feel overwhelmed by the flood of impressions. This can lead to erroneous reactions, loss of orientation, panic, paranoia and badtrips/horror trips.
There is a risk - even with single use - that latent (hidden) mental disorders can be triggered. LSD does not lead to organ damage or genetic mutations and is not physically addictive.
saferUse: Take LSD only if you are well prepared, in an environment where you feel comfortable, and only with experienced friends (favourable setting).
Only take LSD when you feel good mentally and physically (cheap set).
You should not be afraid, but have enough respect for the LSD effect.
Do not consume LSD on a full stomach, but eat something light before or during the high.
Dose low. Don't throw it if it doesn't work right away!
Let yourself go during the trip, don't try to fight the LSD effect.
Dextrose can help against circulatory problems.
Avoid roads and other "dangerous" places, your orientation may be disturbed.
At least the day after the trip, allow yourself plenty of rest and recovery to be able to process the experience.
LSD trips should remain exceptional experiences and should in no case be experienced more than once a month.
People with mental problems or illnesses, people taking neuroleptics and people with circulatory and heart problems should refrain from consuming LSD.

Blotters: Orally administering (swallowing) substances whose identity is uncertain is a potential way to eliminate most of the effects from dangerous mimics like 25x-NBx (25x-NBOMe like 25I-NBOMe, and 25x-NBOH like 25I-NBOH, etc). 25I-NBOMe is widely rumored to be orally inactive; however, oral efficacy has not been disproven and apparent overdoses have occurred via oral administration. 25I-NBOMe (and other NB's like 25x-NBOMe, 25x-NBOH) have much lower oral bioavailability than sublingual, buccal, and sublabial administration. 25I-NBOMe, to which several deaths have been attributed may commonly be mistaken for LSD by sellers and users.

Wait two hours for the effect to take effect before adding more.
With MDA, topping up is pointless, as it is effective for a long time even in small doses.
Refrain from mixed consumption.
Avoid alcohol, drink enough non-alcoholic beverages (0.3-0.5 L per hour).
Take breaks from dancing at parties and get some fresh air in between.
Take regular breaks from consumption. The body needs time to recover.
People taking medication are advised to inform themselves about interactions.

effectsSummary: MDEA is closely related to MDMA. It differs mainly in how well one's own feelings are perceived (entactogenic effect), how strong empathic understanding (empathic effect) and hallucinogenic effects occur.
dosageRemark: 1.3 mg per kg body weight (1.3 mg x 80 kg = 100 mg)
generalRisks: Nausea to nausea, dry mouth, cramping of the jaw muscles, sweating, coordination disorders, sleep disorders and trembling.
longtermRisks: MDA is both neurotoxic (damaging to the nerves) and hepatotoxic (damaging to the liver); regular use can lead to schizophrenia-like symptoms.
saferUse: First test a third or half a pill.
Wait two hours for the effect to take effect before adding more.
Refrain from mixed consumption.
Avoid alcohol, drink enough non-alcoholic beverages (0.3-0.5 L per hour).
Take breaks from dancing at parties and get some fresh air in between.
Take regular breaks from consumption. The body needs time to recover.
People taking medication are advised to inform themselves about interactions.

name: MDMA

tolerance.full: with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary:
The world's most popular empathogen with powerful pro-social effects. Has been strongly linked to cognitive decline in excess. Popular at parties, it is often sold in powder or in pills, and may be adulterated with other similar chemicals.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to pure dopaminergic stimulants (amphetamine, cocaine), MDMA forces massive presynaptic serotonin and oxytocin efflux. It generates profound emotional empathy, fearless introspective vulnerability, and prosocial warmth, but temporarily depletes vesicular serotonin stores, mandating a strict 6-to-12 week spacing rule to prevent neurotoxicity.
effectsSummary: MDMA mainly causes an increased release of the body's own messenger substance serotonin. At the recommended dosage, about 80% of the available serotonin at that time is released. This release triggers a feeling of euphoria, lightness and light-heartedness. Sight and hearing change, touch and music are felt more intensely, inhibitions are reduced and the need for contact is increased. The effect is described as empathogenic (triggering a feeling of closeness and connection to other people) and entactogenic (touching the inner self, intensifying emotional perception). The simultaneous release of the neurotransmitters noradrenalin and dopamine has a stimulating effect. This reduces the feeling of hunger and thirst as well as tiredness and increases alertness. Body temperature and blood pressure also rise.
dosageRemark: Swallowed max. 1.5 mg MDMA per kg body weight for men, max. 1.3 mg per kg body weight for women. Lower doses are recommended for rectal and nasal use.
generalRisks: Side effects are jaw spasms, muscle tremors, urinary retention, headache, nausea/vomiting, increased pulse and blood pressure. The heart, liver and kidneys are particularly stressed. There is also a risk of life-threatening overheating as body temperature rises and the body becomes dehydrated. In the case of an overdose, hallucinations are possible. When the effect wears off or on the days afterwards, depressive moods may occur.
longtermRisks: After a consumption experience, the body needs at least 4 weeks to regenerate the serotonin balance. If one does not allow oneself this break in the long term and consumes repeatedly after short breaks, the probability of a permanent restriction of spatial awareness increases. This risk also exists after repeated high doses. Intense and prolonged use of ecstasy can also lead to a change in the serotonin system. A form of dependence with psychological symptoms can develop, especially if ecstasy use is linked to a certain activity, for example if it is always used at parties and partying without ecstasy afterwards is no longer possible. In the case of snorting, the nasal mucous membranes and the nasal wall are damaged. Rectal use can cause irritation in the rectum.
saferUse: If you want to be sure that your pill really contains MDMA and know the dose, use drug checking. If this is not possible, first consume only one third of the pill.
Do not add more right away, but wait two hours for the full effect and then decide.
Avoid mixed use with other substances.
Avoid alcohol and drink enough non-alcoholic beverages. Approx. 3 dl per hour is enough. Isotonic drinks are best to avoid hyponatremia ("water intoxication").
Take breaks from dancing at parties and get some fresh air.
Do not wear headgear, except in strong sun (danger of overheating!).
Do not take ecstasy immediately after a meal, but also not on an empty stomach. It is advisable to have a light, healthy meal a few hours before.
Accept when the effect runs out. "Re-spiking" increases the toxicity (poisonousness) of MDMA.
Give yourself time to recover and take regular breaks (at least 4-6 weeks) to restore serotonin levels.
If you use MDMA nasally, follow the safe-sniffing rules. If consuming rectally, use lubricant to minimise the risk of rectal irritation.
If you are taking medication, ask your doctor about possible interactions. If you are taking psychotropic drugs, the use of MDMA is strongly discouraged (risk of serotonin syndrome)!
Ecstasy can cause asthma attacks in asthmatics and epileptic seizures in epileptics.
People with high blood pressure, heart problems, hyperthyroidism, liver and kidney diseases or circulatory problems should refrain from using MDMA.

There is a small percentage of people, who due to their race and family history, have a lower level of the liver enzyme P450 2D6. This can cause them to be more sensitive to MDMA, requiring lower doses and extra caution should be taken.

name: MDPV
summary:
MDPV (3,4-methylenedioxypyrovalerone) is a synthetic pyrrolidinophenone stimulant widely regarded as having the most devastating psychological addiction liability in the history of research chemicals. Functioning as an ultra-potent dopamine and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (~50x more potent than cocaine and 2-3x more potent than α-PVP), its high lipophilicity leads to long-lasting brain retention, driving obsessive multi-day craving ('MDPV fiending'), protracted insomnia, and profound paranoid psychosis.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to alpha-PVP (which has a shorter 30-45 min peak and a precipitous crash), MDPV is 2-3 times more potent by dose, with much longer-lasting residual stimulation (6-12h+). Its comedown generates profound dysphoric paranoia and hyper-vigilance, triggering relentless compulsive fiending and multi-day binges.
effectsSummary: Intense dopaminergic euphoria, explosive physical and mental stimulation, racing thoughts, compulsive loquacity, marked tachycardia, severe vasoconstriction, multi-day insomnia, and extreme obsessive craving.
dosageRemark: Extreme potency: active at 1-3 mg. An analytical laboratory milligram scale (0.001 g) is strictly required. An inadvertent escalation of just a few milligrams can induce 24+ hour panic and paranoid delirium.
generalRisks: Prolonged toxic paranoid psychosis (threatening hallucinations, persecutory delusions), supraventricular tachycardia, hypertensive crisis, malignant hyperthermia, critical dehydration, and seizures.
longtermRisks: Extreme psychological addiction with rapid dopamine pathway depletion, severe refractory depressive states, lingering psychosis, and chronic cardiovascular pathology.
saferUse: Never redose to prolong the peak (residual stimulation dangerously stacks)
Mandatory precision weighing on a 0.001g scale
Never use alone due to risks of paranoid delirium and cardiovascular collapse
Have emergency sedatives (benzodiazepines) available to mitigate acute crisis
Stay regularly hydrated and strictly pre-determine the end of the session

name: Meclofenoxate
summary:
Meclofenoxate (Centrophenoxine, Lucidril) is a synthetic nootropic combining 4-chlorophenoxyacetic acid (pCPA) with dimethylaminoethanol (DMAE). Developed as a neuroprotective cognition enhancer, it promotes cellular lipofuscin clearance (anti-aging pigment removal) and elevates central acetylcholine levels.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to piracetam and basic choline salts, meclofenoxate crosses neuronal membranes with superior efficiency, demonstrating unique cellular anti-senescence benefits and sharper wakefulness, while occasionally prompting cholinergic jaw tension at higher doses.
effectsSummary: Cognitive clarity, enhanced memory recall, mental alertness, and neuroprotective cell cleanup.
dosageRemark: Standard supplemental dose: 250-500 mg 1-2 times daily in the morning/afternoon.
generalRisks: Jaw tension, headache, restlessness, and insomnia if taken in the evening.
longtermRisks: High long-term safety profile; caution in major seizure disorders.
saferUse: Take with morning meals to optimize absorption.
Cycle use in 8-12 week regimens.

name: Mefenamic acid
addictionPotential: not habit-forming (no recreational or diversion potential)
toxicities: acute kidney injury and renal toxicity
increased cardiovascular thrombotic risk with high doses or prolonged use
summary:
Mefenamic acid is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID / AINS) used to treat pain, fever, and inflammation. Fenamate NSAID (Ponstyl) commonly prescribed for dysmenorrhea, pelvic pain, and moderate inflammatory pain. Strict dosing intervals must be respected, and two different NSAIDs must never be combined.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Mefenamic acid (Ponstel) is an anthranilic acid NSAID that simultaneously inhibits prostaglandin synthesis and antagonizes peripheral prostaglandin receptors, favored for severe pelvic pain and menorrhagia.
effectsSummary: Analgesic (pain relief), antipyretic (fever reduction), and anti-inflammatory effects via COX-1/COX-2 prostaglandin inhibition. No psychoactive or euphoric effect.
dosageRemark: STRICT INTERVAL: Wait at least 6 to 8 hours between two intakes. The 'Heavy' threshold (500 mg) represents the maximum single unit dose per intake. Maximum cumulative daily dose: 1500 mg/24h (maximum 500 mg three times daily for <= 5-7 days). Always take with food or a full glass of water to protect the stomach.
generalRisks: Stomach pain, heartburn, nausea, peptic ulcers, gastrointestinal bleeding, fluid retention, elevated blood pressure, and acute renal impairment (especially when dehydrated). Can trigger severe bronchospasm in aspirin-sensitive asthma. Must NOT be used during pregnancy (especially from the 6th month onward) or during bacterial infections like varicella/streptococcal infections without medical advice.
longtermRisks: Chronic or repeated high-dose use causes gastric/duodenal ulcers, gastrointestinal perforation, chronic kidney disease (analgesic nephropathy), hypertension, and elevated risk of myocardial infarction or stroke.
saferUse: Strictly wait at least 6 to 8 hours between two doses and never exceed 1500 mg/24h (maximum 500 mg three times daily for <= 5-7 days) in 24 hours.
Never exceed 500 mg in a single intake.
NEVER combine with another NSAID (e.g., Ibuprofen, Ketoprofen, Naproxen, Diclofenac, Aspirin at anti-inflammatory doses, Celecoxib).
Take during a meal with a large glass of water and stay well hydrated to protect your kidneys and stomach.
Avoid combining with Lithium (causes severe Lithium poisoning), oral corticosteroids, anticoagulants, or heavy alcohol use.

name: Melatonin

tolerance.full: after prolonged and repeated usage

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary:
A naturally occurring hormone produced in the body, which promotes sleep at certain times in the day based on the circadian rhythm. It is also commonly available as a drug to treat insomnia and promote a proper sleep cycle. It can be used to promote sleepfulness at the tail-end of drug experiences, though it is not particularly hypnotic.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to benzodiazepines and Z-drugs, melatonin is an endogenous circadian neurohormone rather than a central depressant. It acts chronobiotically to entrain circadian phase without causing motor impairment, tolerance, physical addiction, or anterograde amnesia, exhibiting a very mild intrinsic potency profile (0.01x).
effectsSummary: Intense sensory and visual alterations, altered perception of space and time, emotional amplification, deep introspection, and potential ego dissolution.
saferUse: Strictly respect Set & Setting (positive mindset, calm and secure physical environment).
Always have a trusted, sober tripsitter present during the experience.
Never combine with lithium, tramadol, or MAOI/SSRI antidepressants.
Test substances with colorimetric reagents prior to use and start with a low test dose.

name: Meloxicam
addictionPotential: not habit-forming (no recreational or diversion potential)
toxicities: acute kidney injury and renal toxicity
increased cardiovascular thrombotic risk with high doses or prolonged use
summary:
Meloxicam is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID / AINS) used to treat pain, fever, and inflammation. Preferential COX-2 oxicam NSAID (Mobic) with a ~20-hour half-life, taken strictly once every 24 hours. Strict dosing intervals must be respected, and two different NSAIDs must never be combined.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to piroxicam, meloxicam (Mobic) is an oxicam-class NSAID featuring a 20-hour half-life and preferential COX-2 selectivity, enabling convenient once-daily therapy for osteoarthritis with improved gastric tolerability.
effectsSummary: Analgesic (pain relief), antipyretic (fever reduction), and anti-inflammatory effects via COX-1/COX-2 prostaglandin inhibition. No psychoactive or euphoric effect.
dosageRemark: STRICT INTERVAL: Wait 24 hours (strictly once daily) between two intakes. The 'Heavy' threshold (15 mg) represents the maximum single unit dose per intake. Maximum cumulative daily dose: 15 mg/24h (never exceed 15 mg per day). Always take with food or a full glass of water to protect the stomach.
generalRisks: Stomach pain, heartburn, nausea, peptic ulcers, gastrointestinal bleeding, fluid retention, elevated blood pressure, and acute renal impairment (especially when dehydrated). Can trigger severe bronchospasm in aspirin-sensitive asthma. Must NOT be used during pregnancy (especially from the 6th month onward) or during bacterial infections like varicella/streptococcal infections without medical advice.
longtermRisks: Chronic or repeated high-dose use causes gastric/duodenal ulcers, gastrointestinal perforation, chronic kidney disease (analgesic nephropathy), hypertension, and elevated risk of myocardial infarction or stroke.
saferUse: Strictly wait 24 hours (strictly once daily) between two doses and never exceed 15 mg/24h (never exceed 15 mg per day) in 24 hours.
Never exceed 15 mg in a single intake.
NEVER combine with another NSAID (e.g., Ibuprofen, Ketoprofen, Naproxen, Diclofenac, Aspirin at anti-inflammatory doses, Celecoxib).
Take during a meal with a large glass of water and stay well hydrated to protect your kidneys and stomach.
Avoid combining with Lithium (causes severe Lithium poisoning), oral corticosteroids, anticoagulants, or heavy alcohol use.

name: Memantine
addictionPotential: unknown
summary:
An NMDA-antagonist that if used recreationally can cause to a very prolonged "hole" lasting up to 16+ hours.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to ketamine, memantine (Namenda) is a low-to-moderate affinity, uncompetitive NMDA receptor antagonist with rapid off-rate kinetics. Prescribed for Alzheimer's dementia, it selectively blocks pathological glutamate excitotoxicity while preserving normal neurotransmission, producing zero dissociative anesthesia at clinical doses (10-20 mg).
effectsSummary: Somatosensory and cognitive detachment, bodily anesthesia, proprioceptive distortions, double vision, floating sensations, and deep introspective immersion (hole states).
saferUse: LETHAL DANGER: Never combine with CNS depressants (alcohol, opioids, benzodiazepines).
Always consume while seated or lying down in a safe space to prevent falls and physical injuries.
Space uses out (at least 2-3 weeks apart) to prevent urinary bladder ulceration and cognitive blunting.
Ensure a sober tripsitter is present to prevent airway obstruction or aspirational risk.

name: Mephenaqualone

tolerance.full: within a few days of repeated administration

addictionPotential: highly addictive
summary:
Mephenaqualone is a synthetic quinazolinone sedative-hypnotic analogue of methaqualone (Quaalude). It functions as a positive allosteric modulator of GABA-A receptors, inducing profound somatic sedation, muscle relaxation, and euphoric disinhibition.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to classic methaqualone and benzodiazepines, mephenaqualone carries higher potency and shares the dangerous quinazolinone pro-convulsant liability: high doses precipitate muscle twitching, severe ataxia, and paradoxical grand mal seizures.
effectsSummary: Heavy somatic relaxation, warm euphoric disinhibition, profound muscle softening, and sleep induction.
dosageRemark: ⚠️ SEIZURE RISK AT ELEVATED DOSES: Active at 15-30 mg. Do not escalate doses due to paradoxical seizure hazards.
generalRisks: Motor ataxia, falls, myoclonic jerks, paradoxical convulsions, amnesia, and coma.
longtermRisks: Severe physical dependence, rapid tolerance, and life-threatening GABAergic withdrawal.
saferUse: STRICTLY PROHIBITED to combine with alcohol, opioids, or benzodiazepines.
Never dose without a milligram scale.

name: Mescaline

tolerance.full: almost immediately after ingestion

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary:
A psychedelic of the phenethylamine family. Found in psychedelic cacti that have long been used by peoples native to the Southwestern US and Mexico, including Peyote and San Pedro cacti, among others. Can be found as cactus pulp, as an extract from cacti, or as a synthetic substance created in a lab.

⚖️ Comparative profile: The prototype natural phenethylamine psychedelic found in Peyote and San Pedro cacti, mescaline delivers an expansive 10-14 hour visual, empathetic, and philosophical journey accompanied by initial gastrointestinal purging.
effectsSummary: Before the effect sets in, nausea and/or vomiting can often occur. Hot and cold flushes as well as sweating and dizziness may also occur. These side effects usually subside after a while. The trip begins with hyperactivity and inner restlessness, followed by altered, sharpened perception and intensified colour vision. In a second phase, a more meditative concentration occurs. Users report visions and a euphoria of religious depth, the feeling of a visionary experience and the change of ego sensation as well as feelings of ego dissolution.
dosageRemark: The mescaline content can vary greatly from plant to plant.
generalRisks: The pharmacological effect of mescaline and the bitter taste usually lead to nausea and vomiting in the initial phase of the trip. Mescaline is toxic in high doses (from approx. 2 g) and can lead to liver damage and respiratory paralysis. Other side effects may include an increase in pulse and blood pressure, initially dry mouth, then increased salivation, pupil enlargement, increase in body temperature and a reduced feeling of hunger during the period of effect. During vomiting, users may choke on the vomit (danger of choking!).
longtermRisks: The use of mescaline can trigger latent (hidden) mental disorders even with single use.
saferUse: Mescaline is not suitable as a party drug and should only be used by experienced users.

Use mescaline only if you are well prepared and in an environment where you feel comfortable. Use mescaline only in the presence of friends who are experienced users (good setting) and/or a sober person (tripsitter).
Only use mescaline when you feel good mentally and physically (good set).
You should have respect but not fear for the mescaline effect.
Mescaline should be taken on an empty stomach. Fasting before the trip may help to reduce the likelihood of nausea and vomiting.
For nausea, it helps if you take mescaline in small doses at a time.
Don't add to it if it doesn't work right away.
Let yourself go during the trip, don't try to fight the effects of mescaline. A trip sitter can help you with this.
Dextrose can help against circulatory problems.
Avoid roads and other "dangerous" places. Your orientation may be disturbed.
Drink enough water during the trip.
Mixed use of this potent substance should be avoided at all costs, as the effect can then no longer be assessed.
Plan enough time for recovery after the trip (at least 1 day)!
Mescaline trips should remain exceptional experiences and should in no case be experienced more than once a month.
People with mental problems or illnesses, people taking neuroleptics and people with circulatory and heart problems should refrain from using mescaline.

name: MET
addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary:
A rare psychedelic tryptamine, related to DMT and DET. Little information exists about the effects or pharmacology of this drug.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to DMT, MET provides a much smoother, gentler transition with aesthetic geometric visuals and far less launch panic.
effectsSummary: Intense sensory and visual alterations, altered perception of space and time, emotional amplification, deep introspection, and potential ego dissolution.
saferUse: Strictly respect Set & Setting (positive mindset, calm and secure physical environment).
Always have a trusted, sober tripsitter present during the experience.
Never combine with lithium, tramadol, or MAOI/SSRI antidepressants.
Test substances with colorimetric reagents prior to use and start with a low test dose.

name: Metamizole
addictionPotential: not habit-forming (no recreational or diversion potential)
toxicities: rare but potentially fatal agranulocytosis (severe white blood cell drop)
summary:
Metamizole (dipyrone / Novalgine) is a potent non-opioid pyrazolone analgesic, antipyretic, and spasmolytic used for severe acute pain, colic, and refractory high fever.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Metamizole (dipyrone, Novalgin) is a potent non-opioid, non-NSAID analgesic and antipyretic exceptionally effective for acute visceral spasmic pain, banned in multiple countries due to a rare, unpredictable risk of fatal agranulocytosis.
effectsSummary: Strong pain relief, smooth muscle spasm relief, and fever reduction without opioid sedation or gastric ulceration typical of classic NSAIDs.
dosageRemark: STRICT INTERVAL: Wait at least 6 hours between two intakes. The 'Heavy' threshold (1000 mg) is the maximum single unit dose per intake. Maximum daily dose: 4000 mg/24h.
generalRisks: Rare but life-threatening agranulocytosis (seek immediate medical attention if fever, sore throat, or mouth ulcers appear), anaphylactic reactions, and hypotension.
longtermRisks: Increased cumulative risk of agranulocytosis with prolonged courses; blood count monitoring is required for extended use.
saferUse: Wait at least 6 hours between doses and never exceed 1000 mg in a single intake.
Stop immediately and get an urgent blood count (CBC) if fever, chills, sore throat, or mucosal lesions occur.
Do not combine with Clozapine or Carbamazepine (additive bone marrow/agranulocytosis risk).

name: Methadone

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: extremely addictive with a high potential for abuse
toxicities: potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like alcohol or benzodiazepines
summary:
A synthetic opioid drug used as an analgesic and is often used in detoxification off of other opioids. As it has a much longer half-life.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to buprenorphine, methadone is a long-acting full mu-opioid agonist featuring NMDA receptor antagonism and monoamine reuptake inhibition.
