Its prolonged, variable half-life (24 to 60 hours) effectively suppresses craving without peaks and valleys, but poses risks of cumulative toxicity and cardiac QTc interval prolongation.
effectsSummary: Potent analgesia, warm sedation, opioid euphoria, sense of deep contentment, pinpoint pupils, respiratory depression, and gastrointestinal slowing.
saferUse: LETHAL OVERDOSE RISK: Always keep naloxone (Narcan, Nyxoid) immediately accessible.
NEVER combine with benzodiazepines, alcohol, pregabalin, or any CNS depressants.
Never use alone, and test with fentanyl/nitazene test strips before use.
Space doses strictly to prevent severe physical dependence and debilitating withdrawal.

name: Methallylescaline

tolerance.full: almost immediately after ingestion

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary:
Mescaline analogue first synthesised by Alexander Shulgin, derived from and less potent than allylescaline. A psychedelic phenethylamine which causes stimulation, euphoria and hallucinatory experiences.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to Mescaline, MAL faithfully reproduces the warm visual and contemplative character of mescaline at a fraction of the dose (40-65 mg).
effectsSummary: Intense sensory and visual alterations, altered perception of space and time, emotional amplification, deep introspection, and potential ego dissolution.
saferUse: Strictly respect Set & Setting (positive mindset, calm and secure physical environment).
Always have a trusted, sober tripsitter present during the experience.
Never combine with lithium, tramadol, or MAOI/SSRI antidepressants.
Test substances with colorimetric reagents prior to use and start with a low test dose.

name: Methamphetamine

tolerance.full: rapidly develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: extremely addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary:
A fairly common and very strong CNS stimulant. It is sometimes prescribed in the form of desoxyn for ADHD and severe obesity. In low doses, methamphetamine can elevate mood, increase alertness, concentration, energy and reduces appetite. At higher doses, it can induce mania, psychosis and muscle degeneration among other issues. Tolerant users may report much higher doses than new users.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to regular amphetamine, methamphetamine's methyl group renders it exceptionally lipophilic, allowing instantaneous, massive penetration into the brain. It elicits up to 5 times greater dopamine release with a 10-to-20 hour active duration, producing profound dopamine axon terminal neurotoxicity and catastrophic psychological addiction.
effectsSummary: The body's own performance drug noradrenaline is released, the simultaneous release of dopamine increases self-esteem. Since methamphetamine reaches the brain more quickly than amphetamine and the stimulating effect is stronger, it causes a stronger high and has a higher addiction potential than amphetamine. The body temperature rises, pulse and breathing are accelerated, blood pressure is increased. Hunger and the need for sleep are suppressed. The willingness to take risks is increased, the sensation of pain is suppressed, and euphoria, extreme nervousness, and an increased urge to talk ("babble flash") can occur. Methamphetamine has a pleasure-increasing and disinhibiting effect, which is why it is also used as a sex drug.
generalRisks: Methamphetamine can sometimes hardly be distinguished from amphetamine, but has a much stronger effect. Short-term side effects are: tense jaw muscles, dry mouth, temperature increase, great loss of fluid, increased heart rate as well as increased blood pressure and trembling all over the body. Irritability and aggressive behaviour can also occur (especially in combination with alcohol).
longtermRisks: Methamphetamine is a highly depleting substance with a very high dependence potential with psychological and physical symptoms. Aggression, depression, mental coldness and the desire for more characterise the period of regular use. Constant restlessness, sleep and circulatory disorders, paranoia and even amphetamine psychosis can occur. Weight loss, skin inflammations ("speed pimples"), tooth loss, stomach problems and cramps are also possible. In menstruating persons, the menstrual cycle may be disturbed. Snorting damages the nasal mucous membranes and nasal septum, swallowing damages the stomach mucous membranes. Chronic consumption favours brain haemorrhages and strokes with sudden paralysis. It is suspected that the use of methamphetamine (especially mixed use with MDMA) can lead to irreversible changes or damage in the brain!
saferUse: Dose low, methamphetamine is a highly potent substance!
Take vitamin C and D and minerals (iron, calcium and magnesium) with frequent use.
Eat enough after consumption to prevent weight loss.
Drink a lot (soft drinks).
Follow the safer-sniffing and safer-sex rules.
Refrain from mixed consumption. Make sure to take breaks from consumption.
Mentally ill persons, persons with high blood pressure, liver and kidney diseases, diabetics and pregnant women should not use methamphetamine.
It is better not to wear headgear (danger of overheating!).
Have your substance analysed in a drug check.

name: Methaqualone

tolerance.full: within a couple of days of repeated administration

addictionPotential: extremely addictive
toxicities: doses of over 300mg can be dangerous for first time users
summary:
A pharmaceutical depressant and sedative phased out due to the better safety profile of benzodiazepines, part of the Qualone group of substances. Now very rare, except in South Africa.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Methaqualone (Quaalude, Mandrax) is an iconic quinazolinone sedative-hypnotic modulating GABA-A receptors. Renowned historically for somatic warmth, sensual tingling, and social disinhibition, it carries a unique pro-convulsant toxicity at elevated doses, causing paradoxical motor spasms and grand mal seizures.
effectsSummary: Central nervous system sedation, marked anxiolysis, muscle relaxation, psychomotor slowing, and reduction of inhibitions.
saferUse: LETHAL DANGER: Never combine with alcohol, opioids, or other respiratory depressants.
Space out intake to prevent rapid tolerance and potentially life-threatening withdrawal.
Do not drive or operate heavy machinery while under the influence.
When discontinuing prolonged use, always taper gradually to avoid seizures.

name: Methcathinone
effectsSummary: The effect of methcathinone is in no way directly comparable to that of the khat plant, which is traditionally consumed in Yemen, Ethiopia and Kenya. It is much more similar to the effect of other uppers such as speed. Methcathinone suppresses fatigue and hunger. It causes an increase in drive and performance, euphoria, an increased urge to talk, disinhibition, extroversion, inner restlessness and hyperactivity.
dosageRemark: Snorted: 50 - 70 mg (never more than 300 mg per night!)
generalRisks:
Methcathinone puts considerable strain on the heart and circulation. Since the effect of methcathinone seems rather subtle at first, there is a risk of overdose by refilling. Overdoses can cause fluttering of the heart, stomach problems, restlessness and sleep disturbances. According to reports from users, there is an increased urge to urinate, but urination can be difficult.
Some users report depressive states when coming down.
Methcathinone, like speed, can have increased impurities and high levels of extenders as it is often produced in illegal home labs.
longtermRisks: There is a risk of dependence with psychological symptoms. In the case of long-term, high-dose consumption, the psychological and physical risks are similar to those of speed, cocaine or methamphetamine. In the laboratory, a so-called "craving" (urge to consume even more) could also be observed in experimental animals.
saferUse: Dose methcathinone carefully and do not add more right away.
Refrain from mixed use whenever possible. Above all, do not mix methcathinone with other drugs such as speed or cocaine.
Do not mix methcathinone with alcohol, this only increases the side effects.
Methcathinone has a very draining effect - so take breaks from using it and give yourself enough rest.
Drink water or fruit juices regularly, but not too much, as urination on methcathinone can be tedious.
Make sure you eat a balanced, healthy diet with enough vitamins and minerals.
Follow the safer sniffing rules!
summary: ⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to amphetamine, methcathinone ('ephedrone') has a faster onset with a warm, chatty euphoria, but a shorter duration prompting frequent redosing.

name: Methiopropamine

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary:
Methiopropamine (MPA) is a synthetic thiophene-based stimulant structurally analogous to methamphetamine, featuring a thiophene ring in place of the benzene core. It acts primarily as a selective norepinephrine and dopamine reuptake inhibitor with negligible serotonin activity.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to methamphetamine, MPA produces a cleaner, less euphoric functional stimulation with lower central rush, but causes disproportionate peripheral adrenergic side effects including pronounced vasoconstriction and heart palpitations at higher doses.
effectsSummary: Alertness, mental energy, moderate physical stimulation, reduced appetite, and elevated heart rate.
dosageRemark: Typical doses: 20-50 mg orally, 15-30 mg insufflated. Active duration: 4-6 hours.
generalRisks: Tachycardia, peripheral vasoconstriction, cold clammy hands, jaw tension, and insomnia.
longtermRisks: Cardiovascular strain, tolerance, and psychological habituation.
saferUse: Avoid redosing to chase diminished mental effects.
Stay hydrated and avoid strenuous physical exertion.

name: Methocarbamol
addictionPotential: low / not habit-forming at therapeutic doses
toxicities: additive CNS depression with alcohol, opioids, or sedatives
summary:
Methocarbamol (Lumirelax / Robaxin) is a centrally acting carbamate muscle relaxant prescribed for painful acute muscle spasms and lumbago.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Methocarbamol (Robaxin) is a centrally acting skeletal muscle relaxant operating via general CNS depression without direct neuromuscular blockade, relieving acute musculoskeletal spasms without the high addiction liability of carisoprodol.
effectsSummary: Relieves skeletal muscle spasms via central polysynaptic reflex inhibition; causes mild drowsiness, dizziness, or lightheadedness.
dosageRemark: STRICT INTERVAL: Wait 4 to 6 hours between intakes (taken 3 to 4 times daily). The 'Heavy' threshold (1500 mg = three 500 mg tablets) is the maximum single unit dose per intake. Maximum daily dose: 4500-6000 mg/24h for max 8 days.
generalRisks: Drowsiness, impaired driving alertness, dizziness, nausea, blurred vision, and additive sedation with CNS depressants.
longtermRisks: Intended strictly for short-term acute treatment (<= 8 days).
saferUse: Wait at least 4 to 6 hours between intakes and never exceed 1500 mg in a single intake.
Do not drive or combine with Alcohol, Benzodiazepines, or Opioids due to marked drowsiness.

name: Methoxetamine

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary:
Methoxetamine (MXE, 3-MeO-2'-Oxo-PCE) is a synthetic arylcyclohexylamine dissociative designed as a structurally optimized, longer-lasting ketamine derivative. It functions as a potent non-competitive NMDA receptor antagonist paired with modest serotonin reuptake inhibition and weak mu-opioid affinity.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to ketamine, methoxetamine is approximately 3 to 4 times more potent by weight with a substantially longer duration of action (3 to 5 hours versus 1 hour for ketamine), producing a warmer, more colorful somatic hole experience ('M-hole') but carrying a considerably higher risk of prolonged manic agitation and accidental injury upon redosing.
effectsSummary: Comprehensive mind-body dissociation, warm somatic numbness, internal hallucinatory landscapes ('M-hole'), temporal distortion, and mood elevation.
dosageRemark: ⚠️ HIGH POTENCY VS KETAMINE: 15-30 mg insufflated/sublingual yields potent dissociation. 50-70 mg produces complete sensory disconnection. Always use a 0.001g digital scale.
generalRisks: Severe ataxia, acute delirium, catatonic postures, tachycardia, hypertension, and sensory-anaesthetic physical accidents.
longtermRisks: Strong psychological habituation, cross-tolerance to dissociatives, potential bladder toxicity (ketamine-like ulcerative cystitis), and psychiatric mania.
saferUse: Consume only while lying down in a quiet, physically secure environment.
Wait at least 2 full hours before considering redosing due to delayed oral/nasal onset.
Never combine with serotonergic agents (SSRIs, MDMA, tramadol) due to serotonin toxicity risks.
Strictly avoid alcohol and depressants.

name: Methoxphenidine

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary:
A dissociative from the diarylethylamine class, a more potent analogue of diphenidine. Known to be unpredictable, and can cause blackouts.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to MXE, MXP has a slower onset (up to 1.5h), a longer duration, and a more diffuse, less euphoric dissociation.
effectsSummary: Somatosensory and cognitive detachment, bodily anesthesia, proprioceptive distortions, double vision, floating sensations, and deep introspective immersion (hole states).
saferUse: LETHAL DANGER: Never combine with CNS depressants (alcohol, opioids, benzodiazepines).
Always consume while seated or lying down in a safe space to prevent falls and physical injuries.
Space uses out (at least 2-3 weeks apart) to prevent urinary bladder ulceration and cognitive blunting.
Ensure a sober tripsitter is present to prevent airway obstruction or aspirational risk.

name: Methylnaphthidate
summary:
Methylnaphthidate (HDMP-28) is a synthetic stimulant analogue of methylphenidate incorporating a naphthyl moiety. It functions as a potent triple monoamine reuptake inhibitor (SNDRI), blocking dopamine, norepinephrine, and serotonin reuptake.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to standard methylphenidate (Ritalin), HDMP-28 features significant serotonergic activity, imparting entactogenic warmth, mood elevation, and sensory enhancement absent in pure NDRIs, alongside heightened potency and serotonin toxicity hazards.
effectsSummary: Mood lift, entactogenic warmth, conversational disinhibition, physical stimulation, and appetite suppression.
dosageRemark: ⚠️ HIGH POTENCY: Active at 5-15 mg. Typical duration: 3-5 hours. Use a 0.001g digital scale.
generalRisks: Tachycardia, hypertension, jaw clenching, hyperthermia, and post-session comedown.
longtermRisks: Psychological dependence and serotonin depletion with repeated use.
saferUse: Never combine with serotonergic agents (SSRIs, MAOIs, MDMA, DXM).
Allow several weeks between sessions to recover monoamine stores.

name: Methylone

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary:
βk-MDMA is a cathinone stimulant and empathogen, similar in structure to MDMA, though more stimulating and less empathogenic in comparison. Was very commonly mis-sold as MDMA on the street until it was banned in 2013. The Marquis reagent can differentiate βk-MDMA from MDMA. Less potent than MDMA with a slightly shorter duration.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to MDMA, methylone (bk-MDMA) provides very similar openness and sociability, but with half the duration (2-3h), a faster onset, and a physically gentler comedown.
effectsSummary: Compared to MDMA, methylone has a stronger stimulating and less empathogenic effect. The effect is more constant, the "hangover" less than with MDMA.
generalRisks: Short-term side effects are increased body temperature and heartbeat, dilated pupils and tightening of the jaw. The side effects and the (long-term) risks of methylone have hardly been researched yet.
saferUse: Refrain from re-throwing: This does not intensify or prolong the flash with methylone.
Be sure to drink enough water during the effect.
Do not combine methylone with alcohol and other drugs, especially MAO inhibitors.
Do not use methylone if you have heart or circulatory problems, high blood pressure, diabetes, asthma, epilepsy or mental health problems.

name: Methylphenidate
addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary:
A psychostimulant commonly used in the treatment of ADHD, narcolepsy and obesity, particularly in the EU instead of Adderall. Methylphenidate is also a 5HT1A receptor agonist. Sometimes prescribed off-label to help the withdrawals from cocaine and other stimulants.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to amphetamines (Adderall), methylphenidate (Ritalin, Concerta) acts strictly as a reuptake blocker of dopamine and norepinephrine (NDRI) rather than a presynaptic substrate releaser. It provides predictable ADHD executive enhancement with lower initial euphoria and abuse potential, though instant-release formulations frequently induce late-afternoon irritability rebounds.
effectsSummary:
Taking methylphenidate increases the concentration of the nerve messengers dopamine, noradrenaline and serotonin in the brain. When prescribed for ADHD, the drug is supposed to act as a filter for incoming stimuli and alleviate symptoms such as distractibility, attention deficit disorder, disorganisation and impulsivity.
However, due to its stimulating, energising and drive-enhancing properties, methylphenidate is also used as a party drug or to increase performance. Due to the increased release of dopamine, similar effects occur as with the use of cocaine.
generalRisks:
If prescribed by a doctor or used as directed, sleep disturbances and irritability can often occur. Eating disorders, stomach complaints, nausea and vomiting are also known side effects.
Abusive use and higher doses can lead to seizures, cardiac arrhythmias as well as headaches and confusion.
Tolerance develops relatively quickly, which is why higher and higher doses have to be consumed. In overdose, Ritalin can trigger hallucinations.
longtermRisks: It is assumed that no dependence develops with therapeutic use of Ritalin. When abusing higher doses over a longer period of time, psychological dependence may develop. With abrupt discontinuation, withdrawal symptoms such as lethargy, apathy, depression and paranoia may occur.
saferUse: If possible, do not consume methylphenidate intravenously. Due to the substances contained in the tablets, embolism (blockage of lung or brain vessels) can occur.

name: Metizolam

tolerance.full: within a couple of days of repeated administration

addictionPotential: extremely addictive
toxicities: large therapeutic index and margin of safety
summary:
Also known as desmethyletizolam, a thienodiazepine similar in effects and structure to etizolam, but around half as potent and with around a 60% longer half-life. A sedative, and hypnotic, it may cause amnesia and lowered inhibitions in excess.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to etizolam, metizolam is slightly less potent but has a 50% longer duration of action, providing smoother day-long anxiolysis.
effectsSummary: Central nervous system sedation, marked anxiolysis, muscle relaxation, psychomotor slowing, and reduction of inhibitions.
saferUse: LETHAL DANGER: Never combine with alcohol, opioids, or other respiratory depressants.
Space out intake to prevent rapid tolerance and potentially life-threatening withdrawal.
Do not drive or operate heavy machinery while under the influence.
When discontinuing prolonged use, always taper gradually to avoid seizures.

name: Mexedrone

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary:
Mexedrone is a stimulant drug of the cathinone class. It alters the reuptake of serotonin, dopamine, and norepinephrine to cause euphoria,  and is similar in effects to mephedrone. It is considered a designer drug and is in a legally grey area globally.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to mephedrone, mexedrone is about one-third as potent by weight and produces significantly attenuated stimulation.
effectsSummary: Heightened alertness and concentration, dopaminergic euphoria, physical and mental energy surge, increased heart rate, and appetite suppression.
saferUse: Stay hydrated regularly (water or electrolyte drinks, ~500 ml/h during exertion).
Avoid compulsive redosing which sharply escalates cardiotoxicity and hyperthermia.
Never combine with other stimulants, MAOIs, or decongestants.
Monitor blood pressure and body temperature, and ensure adequate recovery intervals.

name: Mianserin

tolerance.full: sedation partially attenuates over 1 - 2 weeks

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary:
Mianserin (Athymil) is a tetracyclic noradrenergic/serotonergic (5-HT2/alpha-2/H1 antagonist) antidepressant structurally related to mirtazapine, widely prescribed in Europe for depression accompanied by insomnia and anxiety.

⚖️ Comparative profile: A tetracyclic antidepressant related to mirtazapine, mianserin (Tolvon) acts via alpha-2 and H1 antagonism, widely favored for depression complicated by anxiety and insomnia without sexual side effects.
effectsSummary: Marked nighttime sedation, sleep restoration, appetite stimulation, and gradual antidepressant/anxiolytic effect without anticholinergic cardiotoxicity.
dosageRemark: BEDTIME DOSING: Usually taken in a single evening intake at bedtime (30-60 mg usual; up to 90 mg). The 'Heavy' threshold (90 mg) represents the maximum single outpatient bedtime intake.
generalRisks: Pronounced drowsiness, increased appetite and weight gain, orthostatic dizziness, liver enzyme elevation, and rare agranulocytosis (check blood count if fever, sore throat, or stomatitis occurs).
longtermRisks: Weight gain and metabolic changes; rare hematological toxicity during the first months.
saferUse: Take in the evening before sleep and avoid driving if morning drowsiness persists.
Avoid Alcohol, Benzodiazepines, Opioids, and MAOIs; consult a doctor promptly if unexplained fever or sore throat appears.

name: Midazolam
summary:
A common hypnotic, sedative and anxiolytic benzodiazepine. High doses may cause amnesia and loss of inhibitions. Unusually, it is water soluble, and commonly used as a premedication for sedation as the solubility makes it better for IV use than other benzodiazepines.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to classic oral benzodiazepines, midazolam (Versed) is a water-soluble, ultra-short-acting agent (half-life 1.5-2.5 hours). Frontline in procedural sedation, palliative care, and anesthesia, it produces instantaneous heavy sedation and dense anterograde amnesia via IV or mucosal delivery.
effectsSummary:
Midazolam has a calming, relaxing, antispasmodic, anti-anxiety and sleep-inducing effect.
Taking benzodiazepines increases the effectiveness of the neurotransmitter gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) at the GABA-A receptor. This triggers sedative (calming), hypnotic, anxiolytic (anxiety-relieving), anticonvulsant (anticonvulsant) and muscle-relaxing effects in the body. Benzodiazepines have a depressant effect on the central nervous system. The flow of information in the brain between the brain cells (neurons) is thereby reduced / disturbed and feelings and perceptions are dampened.
The breakdown of the individual active ingredients of benzodiazepines in the body is age-dependent and therefore varies from person to person.
generalRisks:
There is little information available on risks, toxicity, side effects and long-term consequences. Therefore, the general information on benzodiazepines applies:
When mixing with other downers (alcohol, GHB/GBL, heroin) there is a risk of respiratory paralysis!
Taking benzodiazepines can cause numerous undesirable side effects. In addition, regular and long-term use carries a very high risk of physical and psychological dependence. Benzodiazepines should only be taken as prescribed by a doctor and only for a short period of time (max. 4-6 weeks). Longer-term use should be discussed with the treating specialist. The dosages and duration of action of the individual benzodiazepines differ considerably.
Side effects of benzodiazepines may be as follows: Prolonged fatigue, gastrointestinal problems, impaired reactions, hypersensitivity reactions, headaches, dizziness, motor difficulties, visual disturbances, slowed breathing, muscle weakness, confusion, sexual dysfunction, aggression, outbursts of anger, restlessness, random movements, allergies, skin problems/rashes and speech and movement disorders. Some benzodiazepines can cause seizures in epileptics.
longtermRisks:
Regular and long-term use can lead to psychological and physical dependence (very high dependence potential). Immediate discontinuation of the drug after prolonged use can lead to negative withdrawal symptoms (including dizziness, physical weakness, inner restlessness, tremors, sleep disturbances, headaches, sweating, nausea, hallucinations and depression).
In addition, seizures and memory disorders/loss and listlessness (hangover effects) can occur. In case of possible dependence, withdrawal should be discussed with a doctor beforehand and the withdrawal should be medically accompanied. It is extremely important that the dose is reduced gradually.
saferUse: If medicines are obtained on the black market or on the internet and not from a pharmacy/medical facility, the contents are unclear. Have the medicine tested for the exact ingredients in a drug check!
Do not rely on dosage information from colleagues who regularly use benzodiazepines. Due to habituation or dependence, their doses can be much higher and fatal for new users.
Blisters of counterfeits may look identical to the original packaging.

The simultaneous consumption of depressant substances such as alcohol, ketamine, GHB/GBL, nitrous oxide, opioids and/or other benzodiazepines is dangerous as there is an increased risk of vomiting and unconsciousness. The risk of suffocation is high!

name: Milnacipran

tolerance.full: 2 - 4 weeks

addictionPotential: not addictive; abrupt cessation causes withdrawal symptoms
summary:
Milnacipran (Ixel, Savella) is a norepinephrine-preferring SNRI used for major depression and fibromyalgia, requiring strict twice-daily (12-hour) administration due to its 8-hour half-life.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Milnacipran (Savella) is an equipotent dual SNRI (1:1 ratio for serotonin to norepinephrine inhibition), delivering energizing, non-sedating relief approved for fibromyalgia and pain-related fatigue.
effectsSummary: Energizing antidepressant and central pain-modulating effect with minimal CYP450 drug metabolism interactions, but marked noradrenergic effects (heart rate, blood pressure, dysuria).
dosageRemark: STRICT 12-HOUR INTERVAL: Taken twice daily (morning and evening, 50 mg + 50 mg = 100 mg/day) during meals. The 'Heavy' threshold (100 mg) represents the maximum single unit intake (max 200 mg/24h in severe hospital/fibromyalgia regimens).
generalRisks: Nausea, palpitations, tachycardia, hypertension, sweating, hot flashes, headache, and dysuria/urinary hesitation.
longtermRisks: Sustained blood pressure/heart rate elevation; withdrawal upon abrupt discontinuation.
saferUse: Space the two daily intakes by ~12 hours and take with meals to minimize nausea.
NEVER combine with MAOIs, Tramadol, Dextromethorphan, or strong sympathomimetics/stimulants.

name: MiPLA

tolerance.full: almost immediately after ingestion

addictionPotential: low potential for abuse and dependence
summary:
MiPLA (methylisopropyllysergamide) is a novel synthetic lysergamide bearing a methyl-isopropyl substitution on the amide nitrogen. Designed to study lysergamide receptor topology, it acts as a selective 5-HT2A receptor agonist.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to LSD, MiPLA is roughly half as potent (active at 150-250 µg) with a pleasantly abbreviated duration of 4 to 6 hours (versus 10-12 hours for LSD). It delivers mood enhancement and tactile lightness with remarkably low cognitive confusion and minimal sensory distortion.
effectsSummary: Crisp sensory enhancement, mood lift, cheerful sociability, enhanced music appreciation, and short duration.
dosageRemark: Standard blotter dose: 100-200 µg sublingual. Duration: 4-6 hours.
generalRisks: Pupillary dilation, mild elevation in blood pressure, and jaw tension.
longtermRisks: Cross-tolerance with other 5-HT2A psychedelics.
saferUse: Store blotters in a cool, dark, airtight environment.
Follow classic harm reduction Set and Setting practices.

name: MiPT

tolerance.full: almost immediately after ingestion

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary:
N-Methyl-N-isopropyltryptamine, a tryptamine analogue of DMT, a very uncommon drug with very few reports of human use. Described as 'more psychedelic than hallucinogenic' users report only mild visuals with some stimulation and cognitive effects. One of the more stable tryptamines.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to DMT, MiPT favors auditory enhancement and bodily warmth with modest alterations to the visual field.
effectsSummary: Intense sensory and visual alterations, altered perception of space and time, emotional amplification, deep introspection, and potential ego dissolution.
saferUse: Strictly respect Set & Setting (positive mindset, calm and secure physical environment).
Always have a trusted, sober tripsitter present during the experience.
Never combine with lithium, tramadol, or MAOI/SSRI antidepressants.
Test substances with colorimetric reagents prior to use and start with a low test dose.

name: Mirtazapine

tolerance.full: almost immediately after ingestion

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
dosageRemark: 24h BEDTIME SCHEDULE: Taken once daily in the evening before sleep (15-45 mg). Paradoxically MORE sedating at lower doses (7.5-15 mg) than at 30-45 mg due to noradrenergic activation. The 'Heavy' threshold (45 mg) is the maximum single and daily therapeutic dose (supratherapeutic overdoses >90-150 mg cause dysphoric confusion/delirium).
summary:
Mirtazapine (Remeron, Norset) is a noradrenergic and specific serotonergic antidepressant (NaSSA) acting as a potent central alpha-2 adrenergic and 5-HT2/5-HT3 antagonist, along with marked H1 antihistamine blockade yielding pronounced sedation and appetite enhancement.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to classic SSRIs, mirtazapine (Remeron) is a noradrenergic and specific serotonergic antidepressant (NaSSA) acting via alpha-2 auto-receptor antagonism and 5-HT2/5-HT3 blockade. It causes zero sexual dysfunction or nausea, but triggers profound bedtime sedation and robust appetite stimulation via high-affinity H1 blockade.
effectsSummary: Central muscarinic receptor antagonism causing true delirious hallucinations (inability to distinguish visions from reality), total amnesia, extreme xerostomia, hyperthermia, and pupil paralysis.
saferUse: EXTREME PHYSICAL AND PSYCHIATRIC HAZARD: Recreational use is strongly discouraged.
Mandatory presence of a sober, capable tripsitter to physically prevent wandering into traffic or self-harm.
High risk of severe anticholinergic toxicity requiring emergency medical hospitalization (physostigmine).
Never redose: erratic absorption kinetics frequently lead to fatal systemic poisoning.

name: Moclobemide

tolerance.full: 1 - 3 weeks

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
toxicities: FATAL serotonin syndrome when combined with SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs, MDMA, Tramadol, or DXM
hypertensive crisis with sympathomimetics or large amounts of tyramine
summary:
Moclobemide (Moclamine, Aurorix) is a reversible inhibitor of monoamine oxidase A (RIMA) prescribed for major depression and social phobia. Must be taken after meals and NEVER combined with serotonergics or stimulants.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Moclobemide (Manerix) is a reversible inhibitor of monoamine oxidase A (RIMA). Unlike irreversible MAOIs, displaced by tyramine, it does not mandate strict dietary tyramine/cheese restrictions at therapeutic doses.
effectsSummary: Increases synaptic serotonin, norepinephrine, and dopamine without sedation or anticholinergic effects; dramatically potentiates tryptamines (oral DMT / psilocybin 'pharmahuasca') and causes lethal toxicity with MDMA, SSRIs, DXM, or Tramadol.
dosageRemark: STRICT SCHEDULE: Taken 2 to 3 times daily AT THE END OF MEALS (reduces tyramine pressor sensitivity). The 'Heavy' threshold (300 mg) is the maximum single unit intake (maximum 600 mg/24h divided into 2-3 intakes).
generalRisks: Insomnia, dizziness, nausea, agitation, headache, and life-threatening serotonin syndrome or hypertensive crisis with interacting drugs.
longtermRisks: Minimal organ toxicity when taken alone; severe acute interaction risks remain throughout treatment.
saferUse: Take strictly at the end of meals and never exceed 300 mg in a single intake (600 mg/24h max).

ABSOLUTELY CONTRAINDICATED with SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs, Clomipramine, Vortioxetine, MDMA, MDA, Mephedrone, Amphetamines, Cocaine, Methylphenidate, Tramadol, DXM, Pethidine, Nefopam, Bupropion, Triptans, and 5-HTP!

name: Modafinil

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: not addictive with a low potential for abuse
toxicities: The median lethal dose at which 50% of participants die (LD50) from modafinil for human beings has never been reached
summary:
A wakefulness promoting, long acting stimulant which is typically only used functionally, because there is no real euphoric component to its effects. Also prescribed for daytime sleeping disorders.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to classical amphetamines and methylphenidate, modafinil (Provigil) is an atypical wakefulness-promoting agent (eugeroic) providing sustained cognitive vigilance without motor agitation, euphoric push, or severe addiction liability. It carries no abrupt post-stimulant crash, but reduces the efficacy of oral contraceptives via hepatic CYP3A4 induction.
effectsSummary:
The mechanism of action of modafinil is not yet fully understood. It is assumed that modafinil binds to the dopamine transporter and inhibits dopamine reuptake. Unlike other stimulants such as amphetamine or methylphenidate (Ritalin®, Concerta®), which in equivalent wakefulness-promoting doses increase neuronal activity throughout the brain, modafinil acts primarily on the brain regions responsible for controlling waking, sleep, wakefulness and vigilance (sustained attention).
Modafinil thus promotes alertness (physical and mental), increases attention and motor activity. Due to its stimulating, wakefulness-promoting properties, modafinil is consumed by healthy people as a so-called "smart drug" or "cognitive enhancer".According to user reports, modafinil has a much more subtle effect than other stimulants and does not trigger comparable states of intoxication. Modafinil causes less physical restlessness and the sleep-wake rhythm is less disturbed.
A mood-lifting and euphoric effect is controversial. According to a publication of the American Food and Drug Administration (FDA), modafinil causes psychoactive and euphoric effects, whereas various studies point to the lack of a euphoric effect.
dosageRemark:
The recommended daily dose when prescribed by a doctor is 200 mg at the beginning. If there is an insufficient response to this dose, a maximum daily dose of 400 mg may be administered/taken.
The long-term effect of modafinil when taken regularly and over a longer period of time has not yet been studied. If taken over a longer period of time, regular monitoring by a medical specialist is therefore recommended.
generalRisks:
In 2011, the European Medicines Agency (EMA) recommended limiting the marketing authorisation for modafinil to the treatment of adults with excessive sleepiness associated with narcolepsy. Due to the possible risks and side effects, modafinil has since not been approved for other indications, for the treatment of children and adolescents, and during pregnancy and breastfeeding.
The following side effects may occur: Headache, nervousness, palpitations, abdominal pain and/or dry mouth. In addition, modafinil can impair the effectiveness of oral contraceptives! Therefore, the use of additional contraceptive methods is recommended during intake. Further risks are cardiovascular diseases such as cardiac arrhythmias, diseases of the heart muscles, cardiac insufficiency and/or high blood pressure. Furthermore, the consumption of modafinil can have an effect on the psyche and trigger hostility, aggression ,psychoses/psychotic disorders, depression, insomnia, up to delusions and/or anxiety.
Symptoms of overdose with modafinil alone or in combination with other medicines: Insomnia; central nervous symptoms (restlessness, disorientation, confusion, agitation, hallucinations); nausea, diarrhoea; palpitations, high blood pressure, chest pain, slow heartbeat.
longtermRisks:
Since modafinil affects the dopamine balance in the brain, among other things, there is an increased potential for physical dependence. If modafinil is consumed for the purpose of performance enhancement and promotion of alertness with the intention of being able to achieve high performance with little sleep, there is also a risk of psychological dependence.
The long-term effect of modafinil when taken regularly and over a longer period of time has been little studied so far. If taken over a longer period of time, regular monitoring by a medical specialist is therefore recommended.
saferUse: Caution: The effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives may be impaired by the simultaneous intake of modafinil.
Side effects such as blurred vision and dizziness may impair the ability to drive or operate machinery.
Taking modafinil is not a substitute for sleep! Be sure to maintain good sleep hygiene.

If you are using modafinil for cognitive enhancement, try to think of alternative strategies to improve your memory and recall. Sleep deprivation after taking modafinil in particular can impair cognitive performance.
Take longer breaks (at least several days) between consumption.
The effect of modafinil can last up to 10 hours. Therefore, pay attention to the time of intake.
Remember to drink enough water. This can be forgotten during the effect of modafinil.

name: Morphine
summary:
The prototypical opioid drug, a powerful analgesic with euphoric qualities, found in the seeds and wax of the plant papaver somniferum (opium poppy).  First isolated by Friedrich Sertürner in 1805, named for its sleep-inducing qualities. Do not combine with other depressants, may cause dangerous respiratory depression in overdose.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Serving as the international benchmark Step III opioid, morphine has poor oral bioavailability (20-35%) due to extensive first-pass hepatic metabolism, unlike oxycodone (60-80% oral bioavailability). Compared to fentanyl, morphine causes significantly higher mast-cell histamine release (pruritus, flushing, potential bronchospasm) and active metabolite accumulation (M6G) in renal impairment.
effectsSummary:
Due to its strong analgesic, antitussive and psychotropic properties, morphine is used to treat severe pain in emergency and palliative care.
Due to its depressant and sedative effect, the active substance is also misused as a euphoric intoxicant. In the context of opioid agonist therapy, morphine is used as a substitute for opiate/heroin addiction.
dosageRemark: ⚖️ IV REFERENCE STANDARD (IV Heavy = 15 mg) & ORAL BIOAVAILABILITY (~20-30%): Due to extensive first-pass metabolism, 10 mg IV equals ~30-40 mg orally (Oral Heavy set at 70 mg [60-80 mg range], equivalent to 40 mg oral Oxycodone).
generalRisks:
Gastrointestinal complaints such as constipation are common side effects after taking opiates. Nausea, vomiting, dry mouth, lack of appetite, abdominal pain, sweating, skin rashes, itching, dizziness, headaches and fatigue are other common complaints. On the psychological level, confusion, nightmares and hallucinations may occur. Rather rarely, there is a drop in blood pressure, breathing difficulties and allergic reactions.
Overdoses with morphine are life-threatening, as the substance has a strong respiratory depressant effect (worsening breathing) even in low doses, which can lead to respiratory arrest and coma. Oral consumption of 0.3 - 1.5 g and intravenous consumption of 100 mg can lead to a fatal overdose. In opioid addicts, the lethal dose can be significantly higher. An overdose is treated by taking naloxone, an opioid antagonist.
longtermRisks: The consumption of morphine can lead to physical and psychological dependence after only a short time. Tolerance builds up quickly, which is why higher and higher doses have to be consumed. Strong withdrawal symptoms such as restlessness, irritability, depression, insomnia, sweating, cold shivers, vomiting, diarrhoea and painful cramps may occur. Like all opiates, morphine can lead to chronic constipation.
saferUse: Opioids are highly effective drugs that should only be used for a limited time and at best under medical supervision.
Start with a low dose and wait for the effect and tolerance before adding more. Do not exceed the maximum daily dose.

If you inject opioids, dose even more carefully, as the range between desired effect (rush) and dangerous overdose is even more difficult to assess. Avoid injecting fentanyl; the risk of overdose is particularly high. Always use new (clean and sterile) injection material! Never exchange syringes, filters, water, disinfection swabs to avoid transmission of hepatitis and HIV.
Do not rely on dosage information from colleagues who regularly use opioids. Due to habituation or dependence, their doses are much higher and can be fatal for new users.
Take longer breaks (at least several days) between consumption.
After a period of abstinence, take a much lower dose! The usual dose before the abstinence phase can otherwise quickly have life-threatening consequences.

The simultaneous consumption of depressant substances such as alcohol, ketamine, GHB/GBL, nitrous oxide, benzodiazepines and/or other opioids is dangerous as there is an increased risk of vomiting and unconsciousness. The risk of suffocation is high!
Refrain from citrus fruits (especially grapefruit) before or during consumption. The combination can lead to an increase in the effect of the opiate and/or to respiratory depression.

name: MPT

tolerance.full: almost immediately after ingestion

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary: ⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to DPT, MPT is softer and more contemplative with fewer physical tremors.
effectsSummary: Intense sensory and visual alterations, altered perception of space and time, emotional amplification, deep introspection, and potential ego dissolution.
saferUse: Strictly respect Set & Setting (positive mindset, calm and secure physical environment).
Always have a trusted, sober tripsitter present during the experience.
Never combine with lithium, tramadol, or MAOI/SSRI antidepressants.
Test substances with colorimetric reagents prior to use and start with a low test dose.

name: MXiPr

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary:
MXiPr (3-MeO-2'-Oxo-PCiPr) is a novel synthetic arylcyclohexylamine dissociative closely related to MXE and MXPr. Acting as a potent non-competitive NMDA receptor antagonist, it delivers a uniquely immersive, warm, and highly psychedelic dissociative experience.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to ketamine and MXE, MXiPr features an unusually rapid nasal onset, richly detailed hallucinatory closed-eye imagery, and intense euphoria at 20-30 mg, though carrying a higher incidence of blackouts and disoriented confusion if dosed carelessly.
effectsSummary: Rapid-onset deep dissociation, bizarre and colorful internal imagery, bodily warmth, total time dilation, and tactile anesthesia.
dosageRemark: ⚠️ POTENT DISSOCIATIVE: Active at 10-25 mg insufflated. Doses above 35 mg easily induce full amnesic sensory disconnection ('hole').
generalRisks: Total loss of motor coordination, disorientation, anterograde amnesia, tachycardia, and accidental injury.
longtermRisks: Rapid tolerance escalation, compulsive redosing tendencies, and potential bladder cystitis.
saferUse: Use a reliable milligram scale; avoid visual dosing.
Remain seated or in bed during the entire peak.
Do not mix with alcohol, opioids, or stimulants.

name: Myristicin
addictionPotential: is not known to be addictive
toxicities: can be fatal in extremely high doses
summary:
Myristicin is a natural allylbenzene compound found abundantly in the essential oil of nutmeg (Myristica fragrans). Ingested in high quantities (several tablespoons of ground nutmeg), it functions as a prolonged anticholinergic deliriant and weak MAO-inhibiting psychoactive agent with endocannabinoid system interactions.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to cannabis or synthetic deliriants (DPH), nutmeg intoxication features a notoriously delayed onset (3 to 6 hours), an exhausting duration spanning 24 to 48 hours, and a devastating somatic hangover characterized by intense dry mouth, bloodshot eyes, gastrointestinal distress, and mental fog.
effectsSummary: Heavy stuporous confusion, delirium, disjointed thoughts, time dilation, severe thirst, flushed skin, and lightheadedness.
dosageRemark: ⚠️ PROLONGED SOMATIC TOXICITY (24-48 HOURS): Active at 10-25 g of whole ground nutmeg. The overwhelming physical side effects vastly exceed recreational value.
generalRisks: Tachycardia, extreme xerostomia (dry mouth), pounding headache, urinary retention, nausea, and disorientation.
longtermRisks: Potential hepatic stress, toxic delirium, and prolonged cognitive dysphoria.
saferUse: Recreational use is strongly discouraged due to adverse toxicity profile.
Maintain constant fluid intake and rest in a safe, familiar environment.

name: N-Acetylcysteine
summary:
N-Acetylcysteine (NAC) is an acetylated precursor of the amino acid L-cysteine. Clinically indispensable as a mucolytic and the life-saving hospital antidote for acute paracetamol (acetaminophen) hepatotoxicity (by replenishing hepatic glutathione), NAC is also prominent in neuropsychiatry and addiction medicine for restoring glutamate homeostasis and reducing compulsive cravings.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to standard dietary antioxidants, NAC is the most bioavailable precursor for intracellular glutathione synthesis. In clinical trials, it significantly blunts craving and compulsive seeking behaviors for stimulants (cocaine, methamphetamine), cannabis, nicotine, and OCD-spectrum habits by regulating the cystine-glutamate antiporter.
effectsSummary: Potent cellular hepatoprotection, bronchial mucus thinning, reduction of intrusive compulsive urges, and neuroprotective cellular defense.
dosageRemark: Standard supplemental dose: 600-1200 mg daily in divided doses with water. For paracetamol overdose: specialized emergency IV protocol required.
generalRisks: Distinctive sulfur smell/taste, acid reflux, nausea, and gastrointestinal irritation.
longtermRisks: High clinical safety profile over long-term use. Caution in active peptic ulcer disease.
saferUse: Take with meals to prevent gastrointestinal upset.
In harm reduction, take 600-1200 mg several hours BEFORE alcohol consumption to neutralize toxic acetaldehyde (do NOT take while actively drinking, as it may paradoxically increase hepatic stress).

name: N-Ethylhexedrone

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary: ⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to cocaine, N-ethylhexedrone (Hexen) delivers a more caustic nasal rush and longer, more aggressive physical stimulation, paired with a harsher crash driving compulsive redosing.
effectsSummary: Heightened alertness and concentration, dopaminergic euphoria, physical and mental energy surge, increased heart rate, and appetite suppression.
saferUse: Stay hydrated regularly (water or electrolyte drinks, ~500 ml/h during exertion).
Avoid compulsive redosing which sharply escalates cardiotoxicity and hyperthermia.
Never combine with other stimulants, MAOIs, or decongestants.
Monitor blood pressure and body temperature, and ensure adequate recovery intervals.

name: N-Methylbisfluoromodafinil

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: mildly addictive with a low potential for abuse
summary:
N-Methylbisfluoromodafinil (Flmodafinil, CRL-40,941) is a bis-fluorinated synthetic derivative of modafinil. It acts as an atypical, selective dopamine reuptake inhibitor (eugeroic) promoting sustained wakefulness with minimal peripheral sympathomimetic strain.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to parent modafinil and armodafinil, flmodafinil exhibits superior bioavailability and 2 to 4-fold higher potency by weight (effective doses 50-100 mg versus 100-200 mg for modafinil), producing prolonged resistance to mental fatigue lasting 10 to 14 hours.
effectsSummary: Robust suppression of sleepiness, unwavering executive focus, mental stamina, and cognitive drive without jittery motor stimulation.
dosageRemark: Standard dose: 50-100 mg taken upon waking. Taking after 10 AM causes significant sleep latency.
generalRisks: Headaches (often alleviated with choline), insomnia, dry mouth, mild nausea, and anxiety.
longtermRisks: Induction of hepatic CYP3A4 enzymes, significantly reducing the efficacy of oral hormonal contraceptives.
saferUse: Take early in the morning with plenty of water.
Female patients using hormonal birth control must use alternative barrier protection.
Pair with a dietary choline source (Alpha-GPC) to prevent frontal headaches.

name: Nalmefene
addictionPotential: not habit-forming
toxicities: SEVERE PRECIPITATED WITHDRAWAL & analgesia blockade with any opioid!
summary:
Nalmefene (Selincro 18 mg) is a mu/delta-opioid antagonist and partial kappa-opioid agonist prescribed 'as-needed' 1 to 2 hours before anticipated alcohol consumption to reduce heavy drinking.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to naltrexone, nalmefene (Selincro) is an opioid system modulator (mu/delta antagonist and kappa partial agonist) taken as-needed 1-2 hours prior to anticipated alcohol consumption, clinically indicated for harm-reduction drinking reduction rather than total abstinence.
effectsSummary: Reduces alcohol-induced reward and urge to continue drinking; frequently causes initial nausea, dizziness, insomnia, or mild detached/weird feeling during the first intakes.
dosageRemark: STRICT 24h CAP: Take 1 tablet (18 mg) 1 to 2 hours prior to anticipated drinking. The 'Heavy' threshold (18 mg) is the strict maximum single AND 24-hour dose (NEVER exceed 1 tablet per day!).
generalRisks: Nausea, dizziness, insomnia, headache, sweating, transient dissociation/confusion, and severe precipitated withdrawal if combined with any opioid.
longtermRisks: Blocks emergency opioid pain relief for 24-48+ hours after an intake.
saferUse: Never take more than one 18 mg tablet in a 24-hour period.
STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED with all Opioids (including Codeine, Tramadol, Lamaline, Izalgi, Buprenorphine, Methadone, Kratom).

name: Naloxone
addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary:
Naloxone (Narcan, Nyxoid, Prenoxad) is a pure, competitive opioid receptor antagonist (mu, kappa, delta). Devoid of intrinsic agonist activity, it displaces opioid molecules from receptors within 2-3 minutes. It is the gold standard life-saving emergency medication for reversing opioid-induced respiratory depression and coma.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to nalmefene (a longer-acting opioid antagonist), naloxone has a relatively short elimination half-life (30 to 90 minutes). For overdoses involving long-acting opioids (methadone) or potent synthetic analogues (fentanyl, carfentanil), resedation and respiratory arrest may reoccur once naloxone clears, demanding redosing and urgent hospitalization.
effectsSummary: Rapid reinstatement of spontaneous breathing and consciousness, accompanied by precipitous acute opioid withdrawal (shivering, diaphoresis, nausea, agitation).
dosageRemark: ⚠️ LIFE SAVING PROTOCOL: 1 nasal spray (Narcan 4 mg or Nyxoid 1.8 mg) into one nostril of the unresponsive victim. Repeat in the other nostril after 2-3 minutes if breathing is not restored. CALL EMERGENCY SERVICES (911/112) IMMEDIATELY.
generalRisks: Violent precipitated opioid withdrawal, transient hypertension, tachycardia, vomiting, and pulmonary edema in rare clinical scenarios.
longtermRisks: None. Naloxone has zero abuse potential and causes no dependence.
saferUse: Always call emergency medical services immediately upon suspecting an overdose.
Place the patient in the recovery position to prevent aspiration of vomit.
Stay with the patient: naloxone half-life is shorter than most opioids, creating high risk of secondary overdose relapse.

name: Naltrexone
addictionPotential: not habit-forming
toxicities: SEVERE PRECIPITATED OPIOID WITHDRAWAL if taken while any opioid (Morphine, Heroin, Oxycodone, Codeine, Tramadol, Methadone, Buprenorphine, Kratom) is active in the body!
HIGH FATAL OVERDOSE RISK if attempting to override Naltrexone blockade with large opioid doses or after stopping Naltrexone (loss of opioid tolerance)!
summary:
Naltrexone (Revia) is a long-acting competitive mu/kappa-opioid receptor antagonist prescribed to reduce alcohol cravings/heavy drinking and to maintain abstinence after opioid detoxification (also used off-label at 1.5-4.5 mg as Low-Dose Naltrexone / LDN).

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to naloxone (the short-acting emergency overdose rescue spray), naltrexone (Revia, Vivitrol) is an orally active, long-acting opioid receptor antagonist (24-48 hour blockade). Used in addiction medicine to maintain opioid abstinence and reduce heavy drinking days in alcoholism, it completely neutralizes opioid highs.
effectsSummary: Blocks endogenous endorphin reward from alcohol and completely blocks exogenous opioid analgesics/euphoria for 24-72 hours; no psychoactive high of its own.
dosageRemark: 24h DAILY SCHEDULE: Standard dose for alcohol/opioid relapse prevention is 50 mg once every 24 hours ('Heavy' = 50 mg standard max daily single tablet; 100-150 mg only used in supervised 48-72h alternate-day clinic dosing). CRITICAL: Must be 100% opioid-free for at least 7-10 days (10-14 days after Methadone/Buprenorphine) before starting!
generalRisks: Nausea, headache, dizziness, fatigue, mild dysphoria/insomnia, elevated liver enzymes, and violent precipitated opioid withdrawal if any opioid is in your system.
longtermRisks: Lowered opioid tolerance: if Naltrexone is stopped, previously tolerated opioid doses can immediately cause fatal respiratory arrest! Carry a medical alert card noting opioid-analgesic blockade.
saferUse: NEVER take Naltrexone if you have used ANY opioid (including Codeine, Tramadol, Opium/Lamaline/Izalgi, Kratom, Buprenorphine, or Methadone) within the past 7-14 days!
NEVER try to 'break through' Naltrexone blockade by taking massive doses of opioids — leads to fatal respiratory arrest!
Inform emergency doctors/dentists/anesthesiologists that you take Naltrexone (opioid painkillers will not work).

name: Naproxen
addictionPotential: not habit-forming (no recreational or diversion potential)
toxicities: acute kidney injury and renal toxicity
increased cardiovascular thrombotic risk with high doses or prolonged use
summary:
Naproxen is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID / AINS) used to treat pain, fever, and inflammation. Longer-acting propionic acid NSAID (Apranax, Naprosyne, Aleve) requiring only 2 intakes per 24 hours. Strict dosing intervals must be respected, and two different NSAIDs must never be combined.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to ibuprofen which demands 3-4 daily doses, naproxen (Aleve) features an extended 12-15 hour half-life facilitating convenient twice-daily dosing, and is generally recognized as possessing the safest cardiovascular risk profile among non-selective NSAIDs.
effectsSummary: Analgesic (pain relief), antipyretic (fever reduction), and anti-inflammatory effects via COX-1/COX-2 prostaglandin inhibition. No psychoactive or euphoric effect.
dosageRemark: STRICT INTERVAL: Wait at least 8 to 12 hours between two intakes. The 'Heavy' threshold (550 mg) represents the maximum single unit dose per intake. Maximum cumulative daily dose: 1100 mg/24h (naproxen sodium) or 1000 mg/24h (naproxen base). Always take with food or a full glass of water to protect the stomach.
generalRisks: Stomach pain, heartburn, nausea, peptic ulcers, gastrointestinal bleeding, fluid retention, elevated blood pressure, and acute renal impairment (especially when dehydrated). Can trigger severe bronchospasm in aspirin-sensitive asthma. Must NOT be used during pregnancy (especially from the 6th month onward) or during bacterial infections like varicella/streptococcal infections without medical advice.
longtermRisks: Chronic or repeated high-dose use causes gastric/duodenal ulcers, gastrointestinal perforation, chronic kidney disease (analgesic nephropathy), hypertension, and elevated risk of myocardial infarction or stroke.
saferUse: Strictly wait at least 8 to 12 hours between two doses and never exceed 1100 mg/24h (naproxen sodium) or 1000 mg/24h (naproxen base) in 24 hours.
Never exceed 550 mg in a single intake.
NEVER combine with another NSAID (e.g., Ibuprofen, Ketoprofen, Naproxen, Diclofenac, Aspirin at anti-inflammatory doses, Celecoxib).
Take during a meal with a large glass of water and stay well hydrated to protect your kidneys and stomach.
Avoid combining with Lithium (causes severe Lithium poisoning), oral corticosteroids, anticoagulants, or heavy alcohol use.

name: Nefopam

tolerance.full: develops with repeated frequent use

addictionPotential: moderately psychologically habit-forming (documented diversion and off-label oral/parenteral misuse)
toxicities: anticholinergic delirium, confusion, and urinary retention
summary:
Nefopam (Acupan) is a centrally acting non-opioid analgesic acting as a triple monoamine (serotonin, norepinephrine, dopamine) reuptake inhibitor (SNDRI) and glutamatergic modulator. While historically administered via injectable ampoules (or diverted orally on a sugar cube), oral film-coated tablets of 30 mg are now officially approved under marketing authorization (specifically in France under AMM). The standard oral dose is 30 mg to 60 mg per intake (up to 120 mg/day max).

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to paracetamol and opioids, nefopam (Acupan) is a non-opioid central analgesic operating via triple monoamine reuptake inhibition. It causes neither respiratory depression nor constipation, but frequently triggers intense diaphoresis (sweating), nausea, tachycardia, and anticholinergic side effects.
effectsSummary: Central analgesia without respiratory depression, accompanied by mild-to-moderate psychostimulation, sweating, dry mouth, nausea, tachycardia, and at high/diverted doses confusion, dysphoria, or hallucinations.
dosageRemark: DIVERSION-ADAPTED DOSAGES: Standard medical single dose is 20 mg IM/IV (or 20 mg oral off-label), repeated every 4 to 6 hours (strict maximum 120 mg/24h medically). Diverted single intakes above 40-60 mg ('Strong'/'Heavy' >= 80 mg) sharply increase the risk of anticholinergic delirium, severe tachycardia, and generalized seizures!
generalRisks: Profuse sweating, nausea/vomiting, dizziness, dry mouth, palpitations/tachycardia, urinary retention, acute angle-closure glaucoma, agitation, hallucinations, and convulsions (contraindicated in epilepsy).
longtermRisks: Psychological dependence, chronic dose escalation, recurrent seizures, and cardiovascular strain.
saferUse: Wait at least 4 to 6 hours between two intakes and never exceed 120 mg in 24 hours.
NEVER combine with Tramadol, MAOIs, Bupropion, MDMA, or stimulants (very high risk of seizures and serotonin/sympathomimetic toxicity).
Avoid combining with anticholinergics/deliriants (Atarax, Théralène, Artane, Diphenhydramine, TCAs) due to severe anticholinergic toxicity.
Injecting oral/ampoule solutions intravenously rapidly causes severe nausea, fainting, and tachycardia — medical IV administration requires slow infusion over >15 minutes while lying down.

name: NEP

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary: ⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to cocaine and hexedrone, NEP (N-ethylpentedrone) delivers smoother, less jittery euphoria with better mood stability.
effectsSummary: Heightened alertness and concentration, dopaminergic euphoria, physical and mental energy surge, increased heart rate, and appetite suppression.
saferUse: Stay hydrated regularly (water or electrolyte drinks, ~500 ml/h during exertion).
Avoid compulsive redosing which sharply escalates cardiotoxicity and hyperthermia.
Never combine with other stimulants, MAOIs, or decongestants.
Monitor blood pressure and body temperature, and ensure adequate recovery intervals.

name: Nicotine

tolerance.full: rapidly develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: extremely addictive with a high potential for abuse
toxicities: estimated oral LD50 of 6.5 - 13 mg/kg in humans
summary:
A chemical found in tobacco, aubergines and tomatoes which is considered one of the most addictive drugs in existence. It is a mild stimulant, with stress relieving effects. It is widely used in the form of cigarettes, the use of which carries a high risk of causing cancer or heart issues over time. Increasingly, it is 'vaped' as a purportedly safer alternative to smoking.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to traditional stimulants, nicotine acts as an agonist at nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs), provoking brief dopamine surges and moderate wakefulness. Its absolute psychotropic effect magnitude is mild (strictly below weak opioids and benzos), yet its instantaneous pulmonary delivery creates one of the highest addiction and craving indices known in pharmacology.
effectsSummary: Nicotine promotes the release of the hormone adrenaline as well as the neurotransmitters dopamine and serotonin. In low quantities, nicotine thus has a stimulating effect. Nicotine briefly and reversibly accelerates the heartbeat and causes constriction of the blood vessels. The central short-term effects include above all an increase in psychomotor performance as well as attention and memory. In higher doses, nicotine has a calming and muscle-relaxing effect; it reduces feelings of hunger, anxiety and aggression. Nicotine is responsible for addiction to tobacco products.
dosageRemark: Individual and dependent on the form of consumption. The lethal dose of nicotine for adults is about 60 mg; for children and adolescents it is significantly lower.
generalRisks: Reduction of the amount of oxygen in the blood and impairment of the sense of smell and taste. With regular consumption: increase in blood pressure and heart rate, increased release of adrenaline and increased activity of the gastrointestinal tract. Mostly with first or repeated consumption: drop in blood pressure, lowered body temperature, nausea and/or nausea, headache and dizziness.
longtermRisks:
The accompanying substances of tobacco smoke (not nicotine) are responsible for the known health consequences of smoking such as increased risk of heart and lung diseases (asthma, chronic bronchitis, heart attack, stroke, thrombosis, lung cancer) and damage to the stomach lining (risk of stomach ulcers). Nicotine is suspected of having a cancer-promoting effect. Nicotine is one of the drugs with the highest dependence potential with psychological and physical symptoms. Withdrawal symptoms can include depression, anxiety, restlessness, insomnia and (in the long term with abstinence) weight gain. Taking medication (e.g. birth control pills) in combination with high tobacco consumption impairs blood circulation (risk of thrombosis!). People with cardiovascular problems, lung and respiratory problems (asthma, chronic bronchitis) should not use tobacco.

saferUse: Tobacco is a legal, freely available and socially accepted drug. However, this does not mean that this psychoactive substance is low-risk and harmless to health!
With e-cigarettes or vaporizers (vaporisers), there are ways to consume tobacco with less risk.
Nicotine is easily absorbed through all mucous membranes of the body. There are therefore lower-risk products such as snuff, chewing tobacco or nicotine gum.
If you shoot yourself, make sure you use good filtering methods.
For people with cardiovascular problems, risk of heart attack, lung and respiratory problems (asthma, bronchitis), it is recommended not to consume tobacco or to consume only small amounts.

Women who use hormonal contraception run an increased risk of circulatory disorders, thromboses, varicose veins and thus heart attacks, strokes or pulmonary embolisms (blockage of blood vessels in the lungs) when they use tobacco. Women over 30 are particularly at risk.
Smoking during pregnancy is generally not advisable, as the toxins in tobacco smoke enter the bloodstream of the foetus via the placenta.
Always press out your cigarettes well. There is a risk of fire!
Do not eat tobacco. If tobacco or tobacco dissolved in water is accidentally swallowed (especially by children), an emergency call should be made immediately. There is a danger to life!

name: Nifoxipam

tolerance.full: within a couple of days of continuous use

addictionPotential: extremely physically and psychologically addictive
toxicities: potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like alcohol or opioids
summary:
An uncommon and relatively new RC benzodiazepine, and metabolite of the hypnotic benzodiazepine flunitrazepam. Little information about the pharmacological properties of this drug exists. Likely to be a strong sedative and hypnotic.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to Flunitrazepam (Rohypnol), nifoxipam (its active metabolite) produces strong hypnotic and muscle-relaxing sedation lasting 6-8 hours.
effectsSummary: Central nervous system sedation, marked anxiolysis, muscle relaxation, psychomotor slowing, and reduction of inhibitions.
saferUse: LETHAL DANGER: Never combine with alcohol, opioids, or other respiratory depressants.
Space out intake to prevent rapid tolerance and potentially life-threatening withdrawal.
Do not drive or operate heavy machinery while under the influence.
When discontinuing prolonged use, always taper gradually to avoid seizures.

name: Nitrazepam

tolerance.full: develops rapidly within days to 2 weeks of daily use

addictionPotential: extremely physically and psychologically addictive (severe/fatal withdrawal seizures if stopped abruptly!)
toxicities: low organ toxicity alone, but HIGHLY LETHAL respiratory depression when mixed with Alcohol, Opioids, GHB/GBL, or Barbiturates
summary:
Nitrazepam is a prescription benzodiazepine acting as a positive allosteric modulator of GABA-A receptors. Long-acting nitrobenzodiazepine hypnotic and anticonvulsant (Mogadon 5 mg) with strong sedative and muscle-relaxant properties and frequent next-day hangover sedation. Approximate potency equivalence: ~10 mg Nitrazepam ≈ 10 mg Diazepam. Do not combine with other CNS depressants.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to zolpidem and triazolam, nitrazepam (Mogadon) is a long-acting hypnotic benzodiazepine (24-30 hour half-life). While highly effective for preventing nocturnal awakenings, its slow clearance frequently causes daytime sedation, cognitive sluggishness, and fall hazards in the elderly.
effectsSummary: Anxiolysis (anxiety relief), sedation, hypnosis (sleep induction), muscle relaxation, anticonvulsant action; at higher/diverted doses causes disinhibition, motor ataxia, slurred speech, and anterograde amnesia ('blackouts').
dosageRemark: DIVERSION-ADAPTED DOSAGES: Dosages reflect both therapeutic and diverted/recreational usage (~10 mg ≈ 10 mg Diazepam). Doses in the 'Strong'/'Heavy' range (>=10-20 mg) frequently cause amnesia, compulsive redosing, delusion of sobriety, and behavioral disinhibition.
generalRisks: Drowsiness, impaired driving/coordination, memory blackouts, paradoxical aggression or disinhibition, falls, and fatal respiratory arrest if combined with opioids, alcohol, GHB, or other sedatives.
longtermRisks: Severe physical and psychological dependence (medical prescriptions should normally not exceed 4-12 weeks for anxiety or 4 weeks for insomnia). NEVER stop abruptly after daily use: benzodiazepine withdrawal can cause rebound panic, insomnia, tremors, delirium, and potentially fatal generalized seizures — always taper slowly under medical supervision!
saferUse: NEVER mix with Alcohol, Opioids (Codeine, Tramadol, Morphine, Oxycodone, Heroin, Methadone, Opium), GHB/GBL, Barbiturates, or Pregabalin (life-threatening respiratory arrest!).
Beware of 'delusion of sobriety' and memory blackouts that lead to accidental compulsive redosing — log every intake immediately.
Limit continuous daily use to prevent severe physical dependence, and NEVER stop cold-turkey after prolonged use (gradual medical taper mandatory).

name: Nitrous

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: mildly addictive with a moderate potential for abuse
effectsSummary: Instant dissociative rush, distinctive flanging/echoing auditory distortions ('wah-wahs'), giggling, tingling euphoria, sensory disconnection, and floating lightness.
dosageRemark: ⚠️ CRYOGENIC BURN & HYPOXIA HAZARD: NEVER inhale directly from crackers or tanks (gas expands at -40°C, causing fatal lung rupture). Always dispense into a balloon first.
longtermRisks: Severe functional Vitamin B12 deficiency resulting in subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord (paresthesias, motor ataxia, paralysis), megaloblastic anemia, and compulsive binge behavior.
saferUse: Always fill a balloon first and allow the gas to warm up before inhaling.
Inhale only while seated or lying down to prevent fall injuries upon sudden syncope.
Never put a bag over the head or strap a mask to the face.
Space sessions by several weeks and supplement with Vitamin B12 (methylcobalamin).
summary:
Nitrous oxide (N2O, laughing gas, 'whippets') is an inhaled volatile anaesthetic used clinically in dentistry and emergency medicine (Entonox/Kalinox). Recreationally discharged from whipped cream chargers or industrial cylinders into balloons, it acts via non-competitive NMDA receptor antagonism and endogenous opioid peptide release, producing an intense 1-to-3 minute dissociative high.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to ketamine and other arylcyclohexylamines, nitrous oxide has an instantaneous onset and clears within minutes. However, repeated recreational use irreversibly oxidizes the cobalt core of Vitamin B12, causing subacute combined spinal cord degeneration and peripheral neuropathy—severe neurological harms unique to chronic nitrous consumption.
generalRisks: Hypoxia and asphyxiation, sudden falls and head trauma from fainting, vocal cord freeze burns, and nausea.

name: NM-2-AI

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary:
Stimulant that is in the aminoindane class. Is it quite close to it's bigger brother 2-AI. Yet this has a lower potency, has a longer duration though.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to methylphenidate, NM-2-AI offers steady functional concentration with very low euphoric and addictive liability.
effectsSummary: Heightened alertness and concentration, dopaminergic euphoria, physical and mental energy surge, increased heart rate, and appetite suppression.
saferUse: Stay hydrated regularly (water or electrolyte drinks, ~500 ml/h during exertion).
Avoid compulsive redosing which sharply escalates cardiotoxicity and hyperthermia.
Never combine with other stimulants, MAOIs, or decongestants.
Monitor blood pressure and body temperature, and ensure adequate recovery intervals.

name: Nortriptyline

tolerance.full: 2 - 4 weeks for antidepressant action (immediate sedation)

addictionPotential: not habit-forming (no recreational potential), causes cholinergic rebound withdrawal if stopped suddenly
toxicities: HIGHLY CARDIOTOXIC in overdose (sodium-channel blockade, QRS widening, fatal ventricular arrhythmias, seizures, coma)
serotonin syndrome with MAOIs/Tramadol/SSRIs and severe anticholinergic toxicity
summary: Nortriptyline is a tricyclic antidepressant (TCA) acting as a serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor alongside strong antihistaminic, anticholinergic, and alpha-1 blocking properties. Secondary-amine active metabolite of amitriptyline with comparatively less orthostatic hypotension and sedation, used for depression, neuropathic pain, and smoking cessation.
effectsSummary: Antidepressant, neuropathic pain relief, and strong sedation/sleep induction; causes dry mouth, constipation, orthostatic dizziness, and blurred vision.
dosageRemark: NARROW THERAPEUTIC MARGIN: The 'Heavy' threshold (75 mg) represents the maximum single outpatient unit dose per intake (higher daily totals up to 150-200 mg/24h are divided or strictly supervised). Often taken in the evening due to sedation.
generalRisks: Sedation, dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention, blurred vision, tachycardia, orthostatic hypotension, QT/QRS prolongation, lowered seizure threshold, and severe cardiotoxicity in overdose.
longtermRisks: Weight gain, dental caries (from chronic dry mouth), anticholinergic cognitive burden, and withdrawal symptoms if stopped abruptly.
saferUse: Never exceed 75 mg in a single outpatient intake — tricyclic overdose is rapidly cardiotoxic.
NEVER combine with MAOIs, Tramadol, MDMA, or Clonidine.
Avoid combining with LSD/psychedelics (markedly intensifies trips and lowers seizure threshold!), Alcohol, Benzodiazepines, Opioids, or anticholinergics.

name: O-Desmethyltramadol

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
toxicities: moderate potential toxicity relative to its dose due to its potency
potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like alcohol or benzodiazepines
summary:
A opioid analgesic which is the main active metabolite of Tramadol. Alone, it is a few times more potent than Tramadol and has additional affinity for δ and κ-opioid receptors. Has proven popular when sold, but these occasions have been rare due to patent rights.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to regular Tramadol, O-DSMT is its direct active metabolite, roughly 4 times more potent on pure mu-opioid analgesia with deeper sedation, without serotonin reuptake inhibition, completely eliminating tramadol's seizure and serotonin syndrome risks.
effectsSummary: Potent analgesia, warm sedation, opioid euphoria, sense of deep contentment, pinpoint pupils, respiratory depression, and gastrointestinal slowing.
saferUse: LETHAL OVERDOSE RISK: Always keep naloxone (Narcan, Nyxoid) immediately accessible.
NEVER combine with benzodiazepines, alcohol, pregabalin, or any CNS depressants.
Never use alone, and test with fentanyl/nitazene test strips before use.
Space doses strictly to prevent severe physical dependence and debilitating withdrawal.

name: O-PCE

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary:
Dissociative of the Arylcyclohexylamine class. Structurally related to Deschloroketamine.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to Ketamine and DCK, O-PCE is colossal in potency (active at 5 mg), easily inducing a total 'hole' state with lingering after-effects exceeding 6 hours.
effectsSummary: Somatosensory and cognitive detachment, bodily anesthesia, proprioceptive distortions, double vision, floating sensations, and deep introspective immersion (hole states).
saferUse: LETHAL DANGER: Never combine with CNS depressants (alcohol, opioids, benzodiazepines).
Always consume while seated or lying down in a safe space to prevent falls and physical injuries.
Space uses out (at least 2-3 weeks apart) to prevent urinary bladder ulceration and cognitive blunting.
Ensure a sober tripsitter is present to prevent airway obstruction or aspirational risk.

name: Olanzapine

tolerance.full: antipsychotic stabilization over 1 - 4 weeks
