name: Psilocin

tolerance.full: almost immediately after ingestion

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary:
Psilocin is a substutued tryptamine alkaloid, that is present in most psychedelic mushrooms. It is relatively unstable in solution due to the -OH group.

⚖️ Comparative profile: The direct pharmacologically active metabolite of psilocybin (4-HO-DMT), psilocin acts as a high-potency 5-HT2A agonist that penetrates the central nervous system without requiring enzymatic dephosphorylation.
effectsSummary: Intense sensory and visual alterations, altered perception of space and time, emotional amplification, deep introspection, and potential ego dissolution.
saferUse: Strictly respect Set & Setting (positive mindset, calm and secure physical environment).
Always have a trusted, sober tripsitter present during the experience.
Never combine with lithium, tramadol, or MAOI/SSRI antidepressants.
Test substances with colorimetric reagents prior to use and start with a low test dose.

name: Psilocybin mushrooms

tolerance.full: almost immediately after ingestion

toxicities: extremely low toxicity relative to dose
summary:
Fungi containing psilocybin, a prototypical psychedelic with similar effects to LSD, but with a shorter duration; also considered as being more confusing, introspective and entheogenic. Usually refers to psilocybe mushrooms rather than Amanitas, which have different effects. Are considered physically safe if properly identified, which should always be done by an expert.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to LSD, psilocybin mushrooms (metabolized into active psilocin) offer a shorter, more manageable duration (4 to 6 hours), heavier somatic sedation (yawning, nausea, bodily warmth), and an earthy, deeply introspective emotional journey prioritizing ego dissolution and nature connection.
effectsSummary: Low doses have a stimulating and strengthening effect. Medium doses have a mild hallucinogenic effect and stimulate the imagination. High doses have a strong hallucinogenic effect, very psychedelic; the environment is often perceived as dreamlike; visionary immersion in strange worlds, deep insights into oneself and a feeling of strong connection with nature.
dosageRemark:
Average dosages of dried* mushrooms:
Pointed cone bald: light 0.5-0.8 g, medium to strong 1.0-max. 2 g
Hawaiian: light 0.3-0.5 g, medium to strong 0.5-max. 1 g
Mexican: light 0.5-1.5 g, medium to strong 1.5-max. 5 g
*for fresh mushrooms approx. ten times this amount.
x mg psilocybin is stored in each fully developed fruit body. So the number of species is more relevant than the quantity.
generalRisks:
The pupils dilate, pulse and blood pressure change, increase in body temperature (sweating), breathing difficulties and palpitations may occur. Occasionally, nausea may occur. Balance disorders, an altered sense of space-time, confusion and anxiety are also possible; panic attacks may occur in the case of stimulus overload.
The use of psilocybin can trigger latent (hidden) mental disorders.
When picking mushrooms in nature, there is a risk of confusion due to deadly doppelgangers!
saferUse: Consume mushrooms only in good mental and physical condition (set).
Do not consume mushrooms alone, but with someone you trust.
Pay attention to the setting. A stress-free environment is important, preferably in nature. Mushrooms are not party drugs!
Consume mushrooms only after a light meal; it is best to eat very little for 6 to 8 hours to avoid nausea and other unpleasant side effects. Chew mushrooms well!
Use dried mushrooms if possible; wash raw mushrooms well before eating.
In delicate moments during the trip: let yourself go, try not to fight the effect of the mushrooms.
Avoid mixed consumption, never consume mushrooms together with alcohol or medication!
Avoid roads and other "dangerous" places, your orientation may be disturbed.
In case of panic attacks or horror trips: see General Information under Emergency.
After the trip, allow yourself plenty of rest and recovery, at least the day after, to be able to process the experience.

name: Pyrazolam

tolerance.full: within a couple of days of continuous use

addictionPotential: extremely physically and psychologically addictive
toxicities: potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like alcohol or opioids
summary:
RC benzodiazepine discovered by Hoffman-LaRoche in the 1970s. Came to the RC market in the early 2010s. At lower doses it is mainly an anxiolytic compound, yet at higher doses can be quite sedating, hypnotic, amnesic, and can cause loss of inhibitions. Structurally similar to Alprazolam, Bromazepam, and Triazolam. Is 12x as potent as Diazepam.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to Lorazepam (Ativan), pyrazolam selectively alleviates anxiety without causing drowsiness, muscle relaxation, or amnesia, leaving physical coordination completely intact.
effectsSummary: Central nervous system sedation, marked anxiolysis, muscle relaxation, psychomotor slowing, and reduction of inhibitions.
saferUse: LETHAL DANGER: Never combine with alcohol, opioids, or other respiratory depressants.
Space out intake to prevent rapid tolerance and potentially life-threatening withdrawal.
Do not drive or operate heavy machinery while under the influence.
When discontinuing prolonged use, always taper gradually to avoid seizures.

name: Quetiapine

tolerance.full: within a week of continuous use

addictionPotential: moderately physically and psychologically addictive
summary:
An atypical antipsychotic medication under the brand name Seroquel. Also used to treat insomnia and mood swings. This drug is very sedating and can stop/slow down psychedelic drug trips. Infrequently abused.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to fellow antipsychotics, quetiapine (Seroquel) has rapid D2 dissociation kinetics and potent H1 histamine and alpha-1 adrenergic antagonism. At low doses (25-100 mg), it functions essentially as a heavy antihistaminic sedative; true antipsychotic and mood-stabilizing efficacy requires titration to 300-800 mg daily.
effectsSummary: Modulation of central neurotransmitters (dopamine, serotonin, norepinephrine), reduction of psychotic agitation or depressive mood, emotional stabilization, and variable sedation.
saferUse: Strictly adhere to the prescribed clinical dosage and schedule established by the treating physician.
Never discontinue treatment abruptly due to the risk of severe discontinuation syndrome or symptom rebound.
Avoid alcohol and illicit psychoactive substances which compromise therapeutic outcomes and augment toxicity.
Immediately report any movement disorders (extrapyramidal symptoms) or cardiovascular alterations to a physician.

name: Risperidone
summary:
Risperidone (Risperdal) is a second-generation atypical antipsychotic combining potent serotonin 5-HT2A and dopamine D2 receptor antagonism, prescribed for schizophrenia, bipolar mania, and severe irritability associated with autism spectrum disorders.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to olanzapine and quetiapine, risperidone (Risperdal) exerts higher-affinity D2 antagonism among atypicals. Highly effective for positive psychotic symptoms, it carries the highest rate of hyperprolactinemia (gynecomastia, amenorrhea) and dose-dependent extrapyramidal symptoms above 4-6 mg daily.
effectsSummary: Modulation of central neurotransmitters (dopamine, serotonin, norepinephrine), reduction of psychotic agitation or depressive mood, emotional stabilization, and variable sedation.
saferUse: Strictly adhere to the prescribed clinical dosage and schedule established by the treating physician.
Never discontinue treatment abruptly due to the risk of severe discontinuation syndrome or symptom rebound.
Avoid alcohol and illicit psychoactive substances which compromise therapeutic outcomes and augment toxicity.
Immediately report any movement disorders (extrapyramidal symptoms) or cardiovascular alterations to a physician.

name: Rizatriptan
addictionPotential: not habit-forming (risk of medication-overuse headache if >10 days/month)
toxicities: 70% increased plasma levels when combined with Propranolol
summary:
Rizatriptan (Maxalt) is a fast-acting oral 5-HT1B/1D agonist triptan for acute migraine attacks. Notably interacts with Propranolol (which increases rizatriptan exposure by ~70%).

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to sumatriptan, rizatriptan (Maxalt) exhibits faster oral bioavailability, delivering acute migraine abortive relief within 30 minutes, available in convenient orally disintegrating wafers.
effectsSummary: Fast migraine relief within 30-60 minutes; may cause mild dizziness, drowsiness, dry mouth, or transient chest/neck heaviness.
dosageRemark: STRICT INTERVAL: Wait at least 2 hours before a second dose (only if headache recurs). The 'Heavy' threshold (10 mg) is the maximum single unit dose (MAX 5 mg per intake and 10 mg/24h if taking Propranolol, spaced >=2 hours from Propranolol!). Standard maximum 24-hour dose without Propranolol: 20 mg/24h.
generalRisks: Dizziness, somnolence, palpitations, chest/throat pressure, hypertension, and rare coronary vasospasm.
longtermRisks: Medication-overuse headache with frequent (>10 days/month) usage.
saferUse: Wait at least 2 hours between intakes; never exceed 10 mg per intake (5 mg if on Propranolol).
Space Rizatriptan by at least 2 hours from Propranolol, and NEVER combine with MAOIs or other triptans.

name: Rolicyclidine

tolerance.full: with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: highly addictive with a high potential for adverse side effects such as psychosis
summary:
Rolicyclidine, also known as PCPy, is a dissociative with effects similar to PCP. While this dissociative anesthetic has hallucinogenic and sedative effects, it is said to be much less stimulating than PCP. In this sense it is more similar to opioids, or other central nervous system depressants.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to PCP, rolicyclidine (PCPy) produces sedating dissociative effects with less motor excitation.
effectsSummary: Somatosensory and cognitive detachment, bodily anesthesia, proprioceptive distortions, double vision, floating sensations, and deep introspective immersion (hole states).
saferUse: LETHAL DANGER: Never combine with CNS depressants (alcohol, opioids, benzodiazepines).
Always consume while seated or lying down in a safe space to prevent falls and physical injuries.
Space uses out (at least 2-3 weeks apart) to prevent urinary bladder ulceration and cognitive blunting.
Ensure a sober tripsitter is present to prevent airway obstruction or aspirational risk.

name: Salvinorin A
addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary:
A plant which, when smoked, causes short but very intense psychedelic experiences. It is considered physically safe, though users of high dosages often experience bizarre other-worldly scenarios which may be confusing or terrifying.

⚖️ Comparative profile: The active terpene in Salvia divinorum, Salvinorin A is a non-nitrogenous, ultra-potent selective kappa-opioid receptor (KOR) agonist with zero 5-HT2A activity. Vaporized, it triggers instantaneous dimensional dissociation within seconds, lasting 5 to 15 minutes.
effectsSummary: Intense sensory and visual alterations, altered perception of space and time, emotional amplification, deep introspection, and potential ego dissolution.
saferUse: Strictly respect Set & Setting (positive mindset, calm and secure physical environment).
Always have a trusted, sober tripsitter present during the experience.
Never combine with lithium, tramadol, or MAOI/SSRI antidepressants.
Test substances with colorimetric reagents prior to use and start with a low test dose.

name: SAM-e
addictionPotential: not habit-forming with a low potential for abuse
summary:
S-Adenosylmethionine (SAM-e) is an endogenous physiological co-substrate present in all living cells, serving as the principal biological methyl donor. It is essential for transmethylation pathways synthesizing monoamine neurotransmitters (dopamine, serotonin, norepinephrine), membrane phospholipids, and glutathione. Clinically approved for major depression, osteoarthritis, and cholestasis.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to prescription SSRI antidepressants, SAM-e features a more rapid onset of therapeutic response (days rather than weeks) without causing sexual dysfunction or weight gain. However, it carries a significant risk of inducing manic switching in patients with bipolar diathesis.
effectsSummary: Mood brightening, alleviation of emotional apathy, joint pain reduction, and hepatic antioxidant support.
dosageRemark: Standard therapeutic dose: 400-1600 mg daily, taken strictly on an empty stomach with water 30 minutes before breakfast.
generalRisks: Nausea, gastrointestinal discomfort, agitation, and sleep onset latency.
longtermRisks: STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED in bipolar disorder due to high risk of triggering manic or hypomanic switches. Risk of serotonin toxicity with concurrent antidepressants.
saferUse: Utilize only enteric-coated, individually foil-blistered tablets (SAM-e rapidly hydrolyzes and degrades on air exposure).
Do not combine with prescription serotonergic drugs without close medical monitoring.

name: Secobarbital
addictionPotential: extremely physically and psychologically addictive
summary:
A Barbiturate derivative that possesses all the classic effects of todays Benzodiazepines, and the old Barbiturates. It's used in the treatment of Epilepsy, short term treatment for insomnia, and a preoperative medication for anaesthesia and anxiolysis for short surgical/diagnostic/therapeutic procedures.

⚖️ Comparative profile: A short-acting barbiturate (Seconal), secobarbital was historically among the most potent hypnotics, defined by rapid sedation, high addiction liability, and high lethality in accidental overdose.
effectsSummary: Central nervous system sedation, marked anxiolysis, muscle relaxation, psychomotor slowing, and reduction of inhibitions.
saferUse: LETHAL DANGER: Never combine with alcohol, opioids, or other respiratory depressants.
Space out intake to prevent rapid tolerance and potentially life-threatening withdrawal.
Do not drive or operate heavy machinery while under the influence.
When discontinuing prolonged use, always taper gradually to avoid seizures.

name: Selegiline

tolerance.full: irreversible MAO-B inhibition lasting 14 days

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
toxicities: hypertensive crisis and fatal serotonin syndrome with serotonergics or sympathomimetics (selectivity for MAO-B is lost above 10 mg/day oral!)
summary:
Selegiline (Deprenyl / Eldepryl) is an irreversible selective MAO-B inhibitor at low oral doses (<=10 mg/day) used in Parkinson's disease and depression; above 10 mg/day it inhibits MAO-A as well, carrying full irreversible MAOI risks.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Selegiline (Eldepryl, Emsam) is an irreversible MAO-B inhibitor at low doses (Parkinson's therapy sparing dopamine) that becomes a non-selective MAO-A/B inhibitor at high doses (transdermal Emsam patch for major depression).
effectsSummary: Elevates brain dopamine and phenethylamine levels, promoting dopaminergic drive and alertness. Metabolizes partially into L-methamphetamine and L-amphetamine.
dosageRemark: MORNING/NOON TIMING: Take in the morning (or split morning/noon) to avoid insomnia. The 'Heavy' threshold (10 mg) is the maximum selective oral single/daily dose — exceeding 10 mg/day abolishes MAO-B selectivity and triggers tyramine 'cheese reaction' hypertensive crises!
generalRisks: Insomnia, orthostatic hypotension, dizziness, dry mouth, dyskinesia, and fatal hypertensive/serotonergic crisis with interacting drugs.
longtermRisks: Irreversible enzyme inhibition requires a full 14-day washout before taking any interacting medication (5 weeks before/after Fluoxetine).
saferUse: Never exceed 10 mg/day orally without strict low-tyramine MAOI dietary restrictions.
NEVER combine with MDMA, Amphetamines, Cocaine, SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs, Tramadol, DXM, Pethidine, or Triptans (wait at least 14 days after stopping Selegiline!).

name: Sertraline

tolerance.full: steady-state therapeutic effect after 2 - 4 weeks
tolerance.zero: requires gradual taper over weeks to avoid withdrawal

addictionPotential: not addictive (no recreational/diversion potential), but abrupt discontinuation causes SSRI withdrawal syndrome
toxicities: serotonin syndrome when combined with MAOIs, Tramadol, DXM, MDMA, or other serotonergics
increased gastrointestinal bleeding risk when combined with NSAIDs or Aspirin
summary:
Sertraline is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) antidepressant prescribed for major depressive disorder, generalized/social anxiety, panic disorder, OCD, and PTSD. One of the most widely prescribed first-line SSRIs worldwide (50-200 mg once daily); best absorbed when taken with food.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to fellow SSRIs, sertraline (Zoloft) exhibits modest dopamine reuptake inhibition (DAT) at higher therapeutic doses, offering a mildly activating, alertness-promoting profile beneficial for atypical depression marked by psychomotor retardation.
effectsSummary: Gradually stabilizes mood and reduces anxiety/obsessive symptoms over 2-4 weeks; markedly blunts the subjective effects of classic psychedelics and MDMA while raising serotonin toxicity risk with serotonergic releasers/MAOIs.
dosageRemark: DAILY SCHEDULE: Usually taken once every 24 hours at a consistent time. The 'Heavy' threshold (200 mg) represents the maximum single unit dose per intake. Maximum daily and single intake dose is 200 mg/24h. Never double a dose if missed, and never stop abruptly without a medical tapering plan.
generalRisks: Initial nausea, diarrhea, headache, transient anxiety/insomnia or somnolence, sweating, sexual dysfunction (anorgasmia/low libido), bruxism, hyponatremia, and suicidal ideation monitoring during the first weeks in young adults.
longtermRisks: Discontinuation syndrome upon abrupt cessation ('brain zaps' / electric shock sensations, dizziness, rebound anxiety, flu-like symptoms), emotional blunting, weight changes, and persistent sexual side effects.
saferUse: Take at a fixed 24-hour interval and never exceed 200 mg in a single intake.
NEVER combine with MAOIs (wait at least 14 days after stopping SSRIs, or 5 weeks after Fluoxetine, before starting an MAOI), Tramadol, or Dextromethorphan (high Serotonin Syndrome risk!).
Avoid combining with NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Ketoprofen, Aspirin, etc.) without gastric protection due to elevated GI bleeding risk.
Do not take higher doses of MDMA or psychedelics to 'overcome' SSRI blunting — doing so risks fatal serotonin toxicity without restoring euphoria.
Taper gradually with your doctor when stopping treatment.

name: Solriamfetol

tolerance.full: develops to mild stimulant effects with high-dose misuse

addictionPotential: low-to-moderate psychological habit formation at supratherapeutic doses
toxicities: dose-dependent hypertension, tachycardia, anxiety, and insomnia
summary:
Solriamfetol (Sunosi) is a dopamine-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (DNRI) wakefulness-promoting agent prescribed for excessive daytime sleepiness in narcolepsy and obstructive sleep apnea.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to modafinil and methylphenidate, solriamfetol (Sunosi) is a selective dopamine and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (DNRI) indicated for daytime sleepiness in narcolepsy and obstructive sleep apnea, offering strong wake-promotion without altering oral contraceptive clearance.
effectsSummary: Sustained daytime alertness and wakefulness for ~9-12 hours; higher/diverted doses (>150 mg) cause jitteriness, blood pressure elevation, palpitations, and insomnia.
dosageRemark: MORNING SCHEDULE: Take upon awakening (at least 9 hours before planned bedtime!). Maximum medical dose is 150 mg once daily; single intakes >= 225 mg ('Heavy') exceed therapeutic limits and provoke cardiovascular and anxious overstimulation.
generalRisks: Headache, nausea, decreased appetite, anxiety, insomnia, palpitations, and dose-dependent increases in blood pressure and heart rate.
longtermRisks: Sustained hypertension (monitor blood pressure regularly); renal dose adjustment required in kidney impairment.
saferUse: Take upon waking at least 9 hours before sleep and do not exceed 150 mg medically.
NEVER combine with MAOIs (14-day washout) and avoid combining with other dopaminergic stimulants or Cocaine (additive hypertension/tachycardia).

name: STS-135

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary: ⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to natural THC, STS-135 is a fluorinated cannabinoid that frequently causes severe tachycardia and panic from just a few puffs.
effectsSummary: Physical relaxation, altered sensory perception, appetite stimulation, short-term memory impairment, and gentle cognitive deceleration.
saferUse: For synthetic cannabinoids, dose at microgram precision: high risk of seizures and cardiac arrest.
Never drive or operate machinery during or shortly after consumption.
If acute anxiety or tachycardia occurs, rest in a quiet environment and consider CBD to mitigate effects.
Prefer dry herb vaporization or oral ingestion over harmful smoke inhalation.

name: Sufentanil
summary:
An synthetic analgesic drug that is roughly between 5-10x the potency of it's parent drug, (Fentanyl); It's use is very contained to surgery and post-operative pain.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to fentanyl, sufentanil (Sufenta) is 5 to 10 times more potent by weight (500 to 1000 times more potent than oral morphine). Reserved for cardiac surgery and intensive care, it elicits profound analgesia and lethal respiratory arrest at minute microgram thresholds (10-25 µg).
effectsSummary: Potent analgesia, warm sedation, opioid euphoria, sense of deep contentment, pinpoint pupils, respiratory depression, and gastrointestinal slowing.
saferUse: LETHAL OVERDOSE RISK: Always keep naloxone (Narcan, Nyxoid) immediately accessible.
NEVER combine with benzodiazepines, alcohol, pregabalin, or any CNS depressants.
Never use alone, and test with fentanyl/nitazene test strips before use.
Space doses strictly to prevent severe physical dependence and debilitating withdrawal.

name: Sumatriptan
addictionPotential: not habit-forming (frequent use >10 days/month causes medication-overuse rebound headaches)
toxicities: serotonin syndrome when combined with MAOIs/serotonergics
summary:
Sumatriptan (Imigrane) is a selective 5-HT1B/1D serotonin receptor agonist used for the acute abortive treatment of migraine attacks and cluster headaches.

⚖️ Comparative profile: As the prototype antimigraine triptan, sumatriptan (Imitrex) is a selective 5-HT1B/1D agonist causing targeted vasoconstriction of distended cranial arteries and inhibiting trigeminal neuropeptide release, uniquely aborting acute migraines where standard analgesics fail.
effectsSummary: Cranial vasoconstriction and inhibition of trigeminal neuropeptide release, relieving migraine pain, photophobia, and nausea. Often causes transient chest/throat tightness, tingling, flushing, or drowsiness.
dosageRemark: STRICT INTERVAL: Wait at least 2 hours after the first oral dose (1 hour for subcutaneous) ONLY if the migraine improved and then recurred — never repeat for the same attack if the first dose had zero effect! The 'Heavy' threshold (100 mg oral / 6 mg SC) is the strict maximum single unit dose. Maximum 24-hour dose: 200 mg oral (or 12 mg subcutaneous).
generalRisks: Chest pressure/tightness, throat heaviness, flushing, dizziness, drowsiness, transient blood pressure elevation, and rare coronary vasospasm/arrhythmia (contraindicated in ischemic heart disease or uncontrolled hypertension).
longtermRisks: Medication-overuse headache (chronic daily rebound migraine) if used more than 9-10 days per month.
saferUse: Wait at least 2 hours before a second oral dose, and never exceed 100 mg per single oral intake or 200 mg/24h.
NEVER combine with another triptan or ergotamine/lysergamides within 24 hours (severe vasospasm risk).
Contraindicated with MAOIs; use caution with SSRIs, SNRIs, MDMA, or Tramadol (serotonin syndrome risk).

name: Tapentadol

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
toxicities: potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like alcohol or benzodiazepines
summary:
An opioid analgesic drug with potency somewhere between tramadol and morphine, and with a similar action to Tramadol. Also an adrenergic reuptake inhibitor. High addiction potential. Potential for respiratory depression in overdose. Should not be combined with depressants or stimulants.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to Tramadol, tapentadol is a stronger direct mu-opioid agonist combined with noradrenaline reuptake inhibition without major serotonin action, proving more effective for neuropathic pain.
dosageRemark: ⚠️ NORADRENERGIC, SEIZURE & DELIRIANT RISK (PsychonautWiki thresholds preserved): Dual µ-opioid agonist and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (NRI). PsychonautWiki thresholds (Oral Heavy = 150 mg) are preserved due to adrenergic overload and seizure/hallucinatory risks at higher doses.
effectsSummary: Potent analgesia, warm sedation, opioid euphoria, sense of deep contentment, pinpoint pupils, respiratory depression, and gastrointestinal slowing.
saferUse: LETHAL OVERDOSE RISK: Always keep naloxone (Narcan, Nyxoid) immediately accessible.
NEVER combine with benzodiazepines, alcohol, pregabalin, or any CNS depressants.
Never use alone, and test with fentanyl/nitazene test strips before use.
Space doses strictly to prevent severe physical dependence and debilitating withdrawal.

name: Temazepam

tolerance.full: within a couple of days of continuous use

addictionPotential: extremely physically and psychologically addictive
toxicities: potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like alcohol or opioids
summary:
Temazepam's brand name is Restoril. It is a hypnotic benzodiazepine with effects similar to clonazepam, frequently prescribed as a sleep aid. Some users report mild euphoria alongside the hypnotic effects.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to nitrazepam, temazepam (Restoril) is an intermediate-acting hypnotic benzodiazepine (8-15 hour half-life) cleared via glucuronidation, providing restorative sleep with significantly lower next-day hangover.
effectsSummary: Central nervous system sedation, marked anxiolysis, muscle relaxation, psychomotor slowing, and reduction of inhibitions.
saferUse: LETHAL DANGER: Never combine with alcohol, opioids, or other respiratory depressants.
Space out intake to prevent rapid tolerance and potentially life-threatening withdrawal.
Do not drive or operate heavy machinery while under the influence.
When discontinuing prolonged use, always taper gradually to avoid seizures.

name: Theacrine

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: produces dependence with chronic use and has a low abuse potential
summary:
Small alkaloid which can be seen as a structurally modified version of caffeine, with similar stimulating effects. It also shares anti-inflammatory and analgesic effects with caffeine.

⚖️ Comparative profile: A purine alkaloid found in Camellia kucha, theacrine (TeaCrine) is a structural analogue of caffeine acting as an adenosine antagonist and dopamine modulator, uniquely resisting rapid tolerance development compared to caffeine.
effectsSummary: Heightened alertness and concentration, dopaminergic euphoria, physical and mental energy surge, increased heart rate, and appetite suppression.
saferUse: Stay hydrated regularly (water or electrolyte drinks, ~500 ml/h during exertion).
Avoid compulsive redosing which sharply escalates cardiotoxicity and hyperthermia.
Never combine with other stimulants, MAOIs, or decongestants.
Monitor blood pressure and body temperature, and ensure adequate recovery intervals.

name: Theanine

tolerance.full: after prolonged and repeated usage

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary:
L-Theanine is a unique non-proteinogenic amino acid found predominantly in green tea (Camellia sinensis). Structurally analogous to glutamate, it crosses the blood-brain barrier to modulate excitatory neurotransmission, augment GABA and dopamine synthesis, and increase cortical alpha-wave activity (8-12 Hz), fostering relaxed mental alertness without sedation.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to pharmaceutical GABAergic anxiolytics, L-theanine causes zero motor impairment, amnesia, or physical dependence. Its combination with caffeine in a 2:1 ratio (200 mg theanine to 100 mg caffeine) is clinically established to abolish caffeine-induced jitters, anxiety, and vasoconstriction while sharpening working memory.
effectsSummary: Calm, focused mental clarity, reduction of sympathetic nervous stress, sustained concentration, and attenuation of stimulant jitteriness.
dosageRemark: Typical supplemental dose: 100-200 mg per serving, 1-2 times daily. Exceptional safety and therapeutic window.
generalRisks: Mild hypotensive effect, transient lightheadedness at massive doses (>600 mg).
longtermRisks: No reported physical dependence, withdrawal, or organ toxicity.
saferUse: Pair with morning coffee (200 mg theanine + 100 mg caffeine) to optimize cognitive performance.
Use in the evening to quiet racing thoughts and ease into natural sleep.

name: Thiocolchicoside
addictionPotential: not habit-forming
toxicities: genotoxicity / aneugenicity metabolite (M2) above 16 mg/day or >7 days
summary:
Thiocolchicoside (Miorel, Coltramyl) is a semi-synthetic colchicoside muscle relaxant subject to strict regulatory intervals (every 12 hours, max 7 days) due to seizure and genotoxicity risks.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Thiocolchicoside is a semi-synthetic muscle relaxant derived from colchicine with GABA-A and glycinergic affinity, strictly restricted to short-term therapy due to an aneugenic metabolite that damages dividing chromosomes.
effectsSummary: Relieves painful muscle contractures; may cause diarrhea, gastralgia, or drowsiness/agitation. Acts as a GABA-A receptor antagonist in the CNS (lowers seizure threshold).
dosageRemark: STRICT 12-HOUR INTERVAL: Must be spaced by strictly 12 hours between two oral intakes! The 'Heavy' threshold (8 mg) is the strict maximum single oral unit dose. Never exceed 16 mg/24h, and never use for more than 7 consecutive days!
generalRisks: Diarrhea, stomach pain, drowsiness, allergic reactions, hepatotoxicity, and seizures (strictly contraindicated in epilepsy, pregnancy, breastfeeding, and women of childbearing age without contraception).
longtermRisks: Cellular aneuploidy / fertility and teratogenic risk from metabolite M2 if dosage or 7-day duration limits are exceeded.
saferUse: Strictly respect a 12-hour interval between two intakes (maximum 8 mg per intake, 16 mg/24h, max 7 days).
Do not combine with seizure-threshold-lowering drugs (Tramadol, Bupropion, Nefopam, stimulants).

name: THJ-018

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary: ⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to historical JWH-018, THJ-018 is an indazole analog delivering extremely potent, short-lived cannabinoid effects.
effectsSummary: Physical relaxation, altered sensory perception, appetite stimulation, short-term memory impairment, and gentle cognitive deceleration.
saferUse: For synthetic cannabinoids, dose at microgram precision: high risk of seizures and cardiac arrest.
Never drive or operate machinery during or shortly after consumption.
If acute anxiety or tachycardia occurs, rest in a quiet environment and consider CBD to mitigate effects.
Prefer dry herb vaporization or oral ingestion over harmful smoke inhalation.

name: THJ-2201

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary: ⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to plant THC, THJ-2201 is a fluorinated compound of extreme intensity, exerting severe strain on the cardiovascular and nervous systems.
effectsSummary: Physical relaxation, altered sensory perception, appetite stimulation, short-term memory impairment, and gentle cognitive deceleration.
saferUse: For synthetic cannabinoids, dose at microgram precision: high risk of seizures and cardiac arrest.
Never drive or operate machinery during or shortly after consumption.
If acute anxiety or tachycardia occurs, rest in a quiet environment and consider CBD to mitigate effects.
Prefer dry herb vaporization or oral ingestion over harmful smoke inhalation.

name: Tianeptine

tolerance.full: with prolonged use

addictionPotential: mildly addictive
toxicities: large therapeutic index and margin of safety
summary:
A Tricyclic antidepressant, that has quite unique pharmacological properties than others in its class. Such as the possible indirect action on NMDA/AMPA and a full agonist at the μ-opioid receptor. While abuse of this substance is uncommon, it has been shown in a few countries.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to standard antidepressants, tianeptine (Stablon) acts atypically as a neuroplasticity enhancer and a full mu-opioid receptor agonist at elevated doses. While well-tolerated therapeutically (12.5 mg TID), high-dose recreational misuse generates rapid opioid-like physical dependence and brutal withdrawal.
effectsSummary: Subtle cognitive enhancement, improved mental clarity, support of working memory, and neuroprotection without acute intoxication.
saferUse: Follow recommended physiological dosing guidelines and cycle periodic washout breaks.
Check hepatic and renal clearance pathways when co-administering with prescription medications.
Prioritize nutritional balance and consistent restorative sleep as the foundational baseline.

name: Tiapride

tolerance.full: antipsychotic stabilization over 1 - 4 weeks
tolerance.zero: taper gradually to prevent rebound symptoms

addictionPotential: not habit-forming (abrupt cessation causes rebound insomnia, nausea, or psychotic relapse)
toxicities: QT interval prolongation / cardiac arrhythmia risk
extrapyramidal motor symptoms (akathisia, dystonia, parkinsonism) and rare neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS)
summary:
Tiapride is a prescription antipsychotic (neuroleptic) medication used in schizophrenia, bipolar mania/maintenance, or severe agitation. Selective D2/D3 benzamide neuroleptic (Tiapridal) widely prescribed in Europe for agitation in alcohol withdrawal, behavioral agitation, tics/Tourette syndrome, and chorea.

⚖️ Comparative profile: A benzamide antipsychotic related to amisulpride, tiapride (Tiapridal) selectively antagonizes D2/D3 receptors with minimal cortical sedation, frontline for motor dyskinesias, chorea, and psychomotor agitation during alcohol withdrawal or elderly delirium.
effectsSummary: Dopamine D2 / serotonin receptor antagonism (or partial agonism) reducing hallucinations, delusions, mania, agitation, and psychedelic 5-HT2A/dopaminergic effects.
dosageRemark: 6-8h DIVIDED SCHEDULE: Usually taken in 2 to 3 divided daily intakes (50-200 mg per intake; max 400-600 mg/24h). The 'Heavy' threshold (200 mg) represents the maximum single unit oral intake. Never stop antipsychotic treatment abruptly without medical guidance.
generalRisks: Sedation or akathisia (inner restlessness), orthostatic hypotension, dizziness, weight gain, elevated prolactin, extrapyramidal stiffness/tremor, QT prolongation, and rare Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (high fever + muscle rigidity = medical emergency).
longtermRisks: Weight gain, insulin resistance/type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hyperprolactinemia, and tardive dyskinesia with chronic exposure.
saferUse: Respect your prescribed schedule and never exceed 200 mg in a single intake.
Avoid Alcohol, Opioids, and unprescribed sedatives (additive CNS depression and hypotension).
Avoid combining with other QT-prolonging medications (Escitalopram, Citalopram, Hydroxyzine, Methadone) without ECG monitoring.
Seek immediate emergency care if high fever, severe muscle stiffness, and confusion occur (Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome).

name: Tiaprofenic acid
addictionPotential: not habit-forming (no recreational or diversion potential)
toxicities: acute kidney injury and renal toxicity
increased cardiovascular thrombotic risk with high doses or prolonged use
summary:
Tiaprofenic acid is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID / AINS) used to treat pain, fever, and inflammation. Propionic acid NSAID (Surgam) widely prescribed in ENT, stomatology/dental inflammation, and musculoskeletal pain. Can cause sterile cystitis/bladder irritation. Strict dosing intervals must be respected, and two different NSAIDs must never be combined.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Tiaprofenic acid (Surgam) is a propionic acid NSAID with potent anti-rheumatic properties, marked by a rare adverse risk of drug-induced aseptic severe cystitis.
effectsSummary: Analgesic (pain relief), antipyretic (fever reduction), and anti-inflammatory effects via COX-1/COX-2 prostaglandin inhibition. No psychoactive or euphoric effect.
dosageRemark: STRICT INTERVAL: Wait at least 6 to 8 hours between two intakes. The 'Heavy' threshold (200 mg) represents the maximum single unit dose per intake. Maximum cumulative daily dose: 600 mg/24h (maximum 200 mg three times daily). Always take with food or a full glass of water to protect the stomach.
generalRisks: Stomach pain, heartburn, nausea, peptic ulcers, gastrointestinal bleeding, fluid retention, elevated blood pressure, and acute renal impairment (especially when dehydrated). Can trigger severe bronchospasm in aspirin-sensitive asthma. Must NOT be used during pregnancy (especially from the 6th month onward) or during bacterial infections like varicella/streptococcal infections without medical advice.
longtermRisks: Chronic or repeated high-dose use causes gastric/duodenal ulcers, gastrointestinal perforation, chronic kidney disease (analgesic nephropathy), hypertension, and elevated risk of myocardial infarction or stroke.
saferUse: Strictly wait at least 6 to 8 hours between two doses and never exceed 600 mg/24h (maximum 200 mg three times daily) in 24 hours.
Never exceed 200 mg in a single intake.
NEVER combine with another NSAID (e.g., Ibuprofen, Ketoprofen, Naproxen, Diclofenac, Aspirin at anti-inflammatory doses, Celecoxib).
Take during a meal with a large glass of water and stay well hydrated to protect your kidneys and stomach.
Avoid combining with Lithium (causes severe Lithium poisoning), oral corticosteroids, anticoagulants, or heavy alcohol use.

name: Tilidin
summary:
Tilidine (Valoron) is a synthetic Step II opioid widely prescribed in Central Europe (notably Germany, Belgium, Switzerland) for moderate to severe pain. It operates as a prodrug converted in the liver to active nortilidine, a potent mu-opioid receptor agonist. To deter parenteral and high-dose oral abuse, pharmaceutical tablets are co-formulated with naloxone (e.g., 50 mg tilidine / 4 mg naloxone).

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to tramadol and codeine, tilidine provides superior and more consistent analgesia without tramadol's SNRI serotonergic activity (eliminating serotonin syndrome risks), but carries a more pronounced dopaminergic euphoric profile that has led to notable recreational misuse in Europe.
effectsSummary: Effective analgesia, bodily warmth, physical and psychological relaxation, mild sedation, mood elevation, and anxiolysis.
dosageRemark: Standard medical dose: 50-100 mg every 6-8 hours (extended-release). Daily ceiling typically 400-600 mg tilidine.
generalRisks: Nausea, dizziness, drowsiness, constipation, diaphoresis, and life-threatening respiratory depression in overdose or polysubstance misuse.
longtermRisks: Substantial physical and psychological dependence, rapid tolerance, and classic opioid withdrawal upon cessation.
saferUse: Do not crush or snort extended-release formulations containing naloxone, which precipitates immediate withdrawal.
Never combine with alcohol, benzodiazepines, or other CNS depressants.
Space therapeutic doses by at least 6 to 8 hours.

name: Tizanidine

tolerance.full: develops with chronic daily use
tolerance.zero: taper gradually to prevent rebound hypertension

addictionPotential: low; abrupt discontinuation after chronic high doses causes rebound hypertension and tachycardia
toxicities: severe hypotension and bradycardia (especially with CYP1A2 inhibitors like Fluvoxamine or Ciprofloxacin)
summary:
Tizanidine (Sirdalud / Zanaflex) is a centrally acting alpha-2 adrenergic agonist muscle relaxant (related to clonidine) used for spasticity and painful muscle spasms.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to baclofen and benzodiazepines, tizanidine (Zanaflex) is a centrally acting alpha-2 adrenergic agonist (clonidine analogue) reducing spasticity and muscle hypertonia with minimal loss of functional muscle power.
effectsSummary: Reduces muscle spasticity while producing pronounced sedation, muscle relaxation, dry mouth, and blood pressure lowering.
dosageRemark: STRICT INTERVAL: Space intakes by 6 to 8 hours (up to 3 times daily). The 'Heavy' threshold (12 mg) is the maximum single unit dose per intake. Maximum daily dose: 36 mg/24h.
generalRisks: Marked drowsiness, orthostatic hypotension, syncope, bradycardia, dry mouth, dizziness, and elevated liver enzymes.
longtermRisks: Rebound hypertension and tachycardia upon sudden cessation; rare liver injury.
saferUse: STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED with Fluvoxamine or Ciprofloxacin (increases Tizanidine blood levels >30-fold, causing life-threatening hypotension collapse!).
Space doses by 6 to 8 hours and avoid Alcohol, Benzodiazepines, Opioids, or Clonidine.

name: TMA-2

tolerance.full: almost immediately after ingestion

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary:
Trimethoxyamphetamine-2, a psychedelic amphetamine and stimulant first synthesised by Alexander Shulgin. An uncommon compound of similar activity to other psychedelic amphetamines. Short history of human use.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to Mescaline, TMA-2 is roughly 10 times more potent per milligram, lasting 8-12 hours with dense geometric hallucinations.
effectsSummary: Intense sensory and visual alterations, altered perception of space and time, emotional amplification, deep introspection, and potential ego dissolution.
saferUse: Strictly respect Set & Setting (positive mindset, calm and secure physical environment).
Always have a trusted, sober tripsitter present during the experience.
Never combine with lithium, tramadol, or MAOI/SSRI antidepressants.
Test substances with colorimetric reagents prior to use and start with a low test dose.

name: TMA-6

tolerance.full: almost immediately after ingestion

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary:
A rarely seen Psychedelic Amphetamine and Mescaline analogue. First synthesised by Alexander Shulgin, who descrived it as  "one of the most rewarding and pleasurable of the methoxylated amphetamines."

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to TMA-2, TMA-6 is more stimulating and can cause heavier physical muscle tension.
effectsSummary: Intense sensory and visual alterations, altered perception of space and time, emotional amplification, deep introspection, and potential ego dissolution.
saferUse: Strictly respect Set & Setting (positive mindset, calm and secure physical environment).
Always have a trusted, sober tripsitter present during the experience.
Never combine with lithium, tramadol, or MAOI/SSRI antidepressants.
Test substances with colorimetric reagents prior to use and start with a low test dose.

name: Topiramate
addictionPotential: not habit-forming
toxicities: acute myopia and secondary angle-closure glaucoma
cognitive word-finding difficulty ('Dopamax' brain fog) and teratogenicity
summary:
Topiramate (Epitomax / Topamax) is a sulfamate-substituted monosaccharide anticonvulsant and migraine prophylaxis medication (also used off-label in binge-eating and alcohol dependence).

⚖️ Comparative profile: Topiramate (Topamax) possesses broad actions (sodium channel blockade, GABA enhancement, AMPA inhibition, carbonic anhydrase inhibition). Widely used for migraine prophylaxis, it reliably suppresses appetite/weight but frequently induces cognitive slowing and word-finding difficulty ('Dopamax').
effectsSummary: Reduces seizure and migraine frequency; commonly causes tingling in fingers/toes (paresthesia, carbonated drinks tasting flat), appetite loss, cognitive/word-finding slowing, and drowsiness.
dosageRemark: STRICT 12-HOUR INTERVAL: Usually divided into 2 daily intakes (50 mg BID for migraine; 100-200 mg BID for epilepsy). The 'Heavy' threshold (200 mg) is the maximum single unit intake.
generalRisks: Paresthesias, word-finding difficulty, memory/concentration slowing, fatigue, appetite/weight loss, metabolic acidosis, kidney stones, decreased sweating (oligohidrosis/hyperthermia), and sudden blurred vision/eye pain (acute glaucoma).
longtermRisks: Kidney stones (drink plenty of water daily!), osteomalacia, and severe fetal teratogenicity (strictly contraindicated in pregnancy; reduces hormonal contraceptive efficacy at >=200 mg/day!).
saferUse: Drink plenty of water throughout the day to prevent kidney stones.
Avoid Alcohol and CNS depressants; note that doses >= 200 mg/day reduce Hormonal Birth Control efficacy.
Seek immediate ophthalmic care if acute blurred vision or eye pain develops.

name: Tramadol

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
toxicities: potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like alcohol or benzodiazepines
summary:
A synthetic opioid analgesic, tramadol is used to treat moderate pain and can be considered a medium-strength opioid. Tramadol also has the unusual effect of being a serotonin releasing agent and a serotonin reuptake inhibitor, and as a consequence should not be taken in excess due to the risk of serotonin syndrome. Risk of seizures above 300mg doses.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to codeine, tramadol features a dual mechanism: weak mu-opioid agonism (via its active metabolite O-DSMT) paired with serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibition (SNRI). While superior for neuropathic pain, it lowers the seizure threshold (high seizure risk above 300-400 mg) and carries a fatal serotonin syndrome hazard when combined with antidepressants.
effectsSummary:
Analgesic, anxiety-relieving, euphoric, mood-lifting, causes a general feeling of contentment.
The human body has its own pain-relieving system. The endogenous substance endorphin ensures that pain messages are sent to the human brain in a reduced form by docking to certain receptors in the human body. The active ingredient tramadol has a similar mode of action in that the active ingredient attaches to neurotransmitter docking sites (opioid receptors) and transmits a signal to the brain, which subsequently triggers pain relief. In addition, tramadol inhibits the reuptake of certain nerve messengers (noradrenaline and serotonin), which in turn increases the amount of free messengers in the tissue and supports the analgesic effect.
dosageRemark: ⚠️ SEIZURE & SEROTONIN SYNDROME CEILING (PsychonautWiki thresholds preserved): Although its µ-opioid potency is ~0.15-0.2x oral morphine, the Oral Heavy threshold is strictly kept at 300 mg (max 400 mg/24h) due to high seizure risk above 300 mg.
generalRisks:
Adverse side effects may include: headache, malaise/nausea, vomiting, dry mouth, dizziness, drowsiness, constipation, drowsiness, circulatory problems (palpitations, fainting spells, etc.).
In higher doses, seizures, speech disorders, paraesthesias (unpleasant bodily sensations, e.g. parts of the body falling asleep), tremor (muscle tremor), coordination disorders and circulatory collapse may occur. Hallucinations, confusion, delirium, anxiety, sleep disorders and nightmares can also be triggered.
longtermRisks:
Tramadol has a low dependence potential with moderate use. However, regular and long-term use can lead to psychological and physical dependence. Immediate discontinuation of the drug after prolonged use can lead to negative withdrawal symptoms, which may manifest as dizziness, physical weakness, inner restlessness, tremors, sleep disturbances, headaches, sweating, nausea, hallucinations and depression.
Prolonged use can lead to general mood changes, changes in decision-making behaviour or perceptual and reaction disorders.
saferUse: Opioids are highly effective drugs that should only be used for a limited time and at best under medical supervision.
Start with a low dose and wait for the effect and tolerance before adding more. Do not exceed the maximum daily dose.

If you inject opioids, dose even more carefully, as the range between desired effect (rush) and dangerous overdose is even more difficult to assess. Avoid injecting fentanyl; the risk of overdose is particularly high. Always use new (clean and sterile) injection material! Never exchange syringes, filters, water, disinfection swabs to avoid transmission of hepatitis and HIV.
Do not rely on dosage information from colleagues who regularly use opioids. Due to habituation or dependence, their doses are much higher and can be fatal for new users.
Take longer breaks (at least several days) between consumption.
After a period of abstinence, take a much lower dose! The usual dose before the abstinence phase can otherwise quickly have life-threatening consequences.

The simultaneous consumption of depressant substances such as alcohol, ketamine, GHB/GBL, nitrous oxide, benzodiazepines and/or other opioids is dangerous as there is an increased risk of vomiting and unconsciousness. The risk of suffocation is high!
Refrain from citrus fruits (especially grapefruit) before or during consumption. The combination can lead to an increase in the effect of the opiate and/or to respiratory depression.

name: Tranylcypromine

tolerance.full: irreversible MAO-A/B inhibition

addictionPotential: low (rare stimulant-like dose escalation reported at supratherapeutic doses)
toxicities: potentially fatal hypertensive crisis with tyramine or sympathomimetics
summary:
Tranylcypromine (Parnate) is a potent, activating, irreversible non-selective MAO-A/B inhibitor structurally related to amphetamine, reserved for severe treatment-resistant depression.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Tranylcypromine (Parnate) is a non-hydrazine irreversible MAOI with structural amphetamine kinship, delivering activating antidepressant efficacy for treatment-resistant anergic depression.
effectsSummary: Activating antidepressant action elevating serotonin, norepinephrine, and dopamine; frequently causes afternoon fatigue alongside evening insomnia and postural blood pressure drops.
dosageRemark: DIVIDED MORNING/EARLY-AFTERNOON DOSING: Usually taken 2 to 3 times daily (avoid late evening intakes due to severe insomnia). The 'Heavy' threshold (20 mg) represents the maximum single unit intake (maximum 60 mg/24h divided). Requires strict low-tyramine diet and 14-day washout!
generalRisks: Postural hypotension, paradoxical transient hypertension, insomnia, anxiety, dry mouth, and fatal hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage or serotonin syndrome with banned foods/drugs.
longtermRisks: Hypertensive crises and withdrawal symptoms upon abrupt cessation.
saferUse: Follow a strict low-tyramine diet and take doses earlier in the day.
NEVER combine with SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs, MDMA, Stimulants, Cocaine, Tramadol, DXM, Nefopam, Bupropion, or Triptans (14-day washout mandatory!).

name: Trazodone

tolerance.full: 2 - 4 weeks for antidepressant action

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary:
Trazodone (Desyrel, Trittico) is a serotonin antagonist and reuptake inhibitor (SARI: potent 5-HT2A and alpha-1 antagonist) widely prescribed at 25-100 mg for insomnia and 150-400 mg/day for depression. Also terminates 5-HT2A psychedelic trips.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Trazodone (Desyrel) is a serotonin antagonist and reuptake inhibitor (SARI). At low doses (25-100 mg), potent antagonism at 5-HT2A, H1, and alpha-1 receptors makes it a frontline, non-addictive sleep aid that preserves slow-wave sleep without dependence.
effectsSummary: Rapid sleep induction, anxiety reduction, and 5-HT2A blockade; commonly causes nasal congestion, postural dizziness upon standing, and morning grogginess.
dosageRemark: BEDTIME / DIVIDED DOSING: Take shortly after a meal or snack right before bed (food prevents sharp peak dizziness). The 'Heavy' threshold (200 mg) is the maximum single immediate-release unit intake (higher antidepressant daily totals up to 300-400 mg/24h are split).
generalRisks: Drowsiness, orthostatic hypotension (fainting if standing up quickly at night), nasal stuffiness, dry mouth, QT prolongation, and rare painful prolonged erection (priapism — requires urgent ER care if >4 hours).
longtermRisks: Rebound insomnia or anxiety if discontinued abruptly after long-term daily use.
saferUse: Take right before lying down in bed (preferably after a light snack) to avoid orthostatic fainting.
Do not combine with MAOIs, Alcohol, Opioids, Benzodiazepines, or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ritonavir, ketoconazole, grapefruit).

name: Triazolam

tolerance.full: within a couple of days of continuous use

addictionPotential: extremely physically and psychologically addictive
toxicities: potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like alcohol or opioids
summary:
An uncommon and very short acting benzodiazepine. Sedating and hypnotic, and may induce amnesia and lowered inhibitions at high doses.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to flunitrazepam and temazepam, triazolam (Halcion) is an ultra-short-acting hypnotic benzodiazepine (half-life 2-4 hours) with extreme milligram potency (0.25 mg). While rapidly inducing sleep, it carries high historical rates of anterograde amnesia, bizarre behavioral blackouts, and intense next-day rebound anxiety.
effectsSummary: Central nervous system sedation, marked anxiolysis, muscle relaxation, psychomotor slowing, and reduction of inhibitions.
saferUse: LETHAL DANGER: Never combine with alcohol, opioids, or other respiratory depressants.
Space out intake to prevent rapid tolerance and potentially life-threatening withdrawal.
Do not drive or operate heavy machinery while under the influence.
When discontinuing prolonged use, always taper gradually to avoid seizures.

name: Trihexyphenidyl

tolerance.full: develops rapidly with repeated high-dose use
tolerance.zero: 1 - 2 weeks (taper gradually to avoid cholinergic rebound)

addictionPotential: moderately habit-forming (well-documented euphoric/stimulant/hallucinogenic diversion in psychiatry & addictovigilance)
toxicities: central anticholinergic toxidrome (hyperthermia, tachycardia, urinary retention, mydriasis, severe confusion, true deliriant hallucinations)
summary:
Trihexyphenidyl (Artane, Parkinane) is a central antimuscarinic anticholinergic prescribed to treat antipsychotic-induced parkinsonism/dystonia and Parkinson's disease. Possesses well-documented diversion potential: mild euphoria/disinhibition at moderate doses progressing to dangerous anticholinergic delirium above 10-15 mg.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Trihexyphenidyl (Artane) is a central anticholinergic used to suppress antipsychotic-induced motor rigidity, carrying notable recreational diversion potential due to intense deliriant hallucinations at supra-therapeutic doses.
effectsSummary: Relieves neuroleptic muscle stiffness/tremor at 2-5 mg; causes dry mouth, blurred vision, mild mood elevation/stimulation at intermediate doses, and disorienting deliriant hallucinations, amnesia, and tachycardia at high doses.
dosageRemark: DIVERSION-ADAPTED DOSAGES: Therapeutic single intakes are 2-5 mg (taken 2-3 times daily, max 10-15 mg/24h divided). Single intakes >= 10-15 mg ('Strong'/'Heavy') provoke severe anticholinergic delirium, hyperthermia, urinary retention, and cardiac arrhythmias!
generalRisks: Severe dry mouth, blurred vision (cycloplegia), acute angle-closure glaucoma, urinary retention, constipation/ileus, anhidrosis (inability to sweat -> heatstroke!), tachycardia, confusion, and true deliriant hallucinations.
longtermRisks: Cognitive and memory impairment, dementia risk with chronic anticholinergic load, dependence, and severe cholinergic rebound (sweating, nausea, stiffness) if stopped abruptly.
saferUse: NEVER combine with other anticholinergics (TCAs like Laroxyl/Anafranil, Cyamemazine/Tercian, Diphenhydramine, Doxylamine, Théralène, Nefopam) — additive anticholinergic poisoning!
Avoid overheating or physical exertion (anticholinergics block sweating and cause heatstroke).
Never stop abruptly if co-prescribed with an antipsychotic (triggers acute dystonia and cholinergic rebound).

name: Tropatepine

tolerance.full: develops with repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately habit-forming (documented anticholinergic diversion similar to Artane)
toxicities: anticholinergic delirium, hyperthermia, tachycardia, acute glaucoma, and urinary retention
summary:
Tropatepine (Lepticur) is a central antimuscarinic anticholinergic widely prescribed in France to prevent and treat neuroleptic-induced extrapyramidal syndromes; carries documented stimulant/deliriant diversion potential.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Tropatepine (Lepticur) is an anticholinergic corrector widely prescribed in French psychiatry to treat extrapyramidal parkinsonian side effects and acute dystonias induced by neuroleptic therapy.
effectsSummary: Relieves antipsychotic stiffness and acute dystonia at 5-10 mg; produces intense dry mouth, blurred vision, restlessness/euphoria, and at high doses full anticholinergic delirium.
dosageRemark: DIVERSION-ADAPTED DOSAGES: Therapeutic dose is 5-10 mg per intake (10-20 mg/24h divided; max medical daily dose 30 mg). Single intakes >= 20-30 mg ('Strong'/'Heavy') cause dangerous anticholinergic confusion, hallucinations, and tachycardia.
generalRisks: Dry mouth, blurred vision, acute angle-closure glaucoma, tachycardia, urinary retention, constipation, hyperthermia, confusion, and realistic deliriant hallucinations.
longtermRisks: Memory impairment, psychological dependence, and rebound extrapyramidal symptoms upon sudden discontinuation.
saferUse: Do not combine with other anticholinergic drugs (Artane, Akineton, TCAs, Tercian, Nozinan, Diphenhydramine, Doxylamine, Nefopam).
Do not discontinue abruptly without consulting your psychiatrist.

name: Tyrosine

tolerance.full: after repeated and frequent usage

addictionPotential: mildly habit forming
summary:
L-Tyrosine is a dietary amino acid and the direct rate-limiting precursor to L-DOPA, dopamine, norepinephrine, and epinephrine. Under acute environmental stress, intense cognition, or post-stimulant exhaustion, brain catecholamine pools become depleted; tyrosine supplementation replenishes these neurotransmitter reserves and prevents cognitive decline.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to direct stimulants (amphetamine, caffeine) which force catecholamine release and deplete stores, tyrosine merely supplies the biosynthetic raw material. It produces no artificial euphoric rush but sustains executive function and working memory during acute physical or mental stress.
effectsSummary: Preservation of cognitive clarity under acute stress, mitigation of mental burnout, and attenuation of post-stimulant dysphoria.
dosageRemark: Effective supplemental dose: 500-2000 mg taken on an empty stomach 30-45 minutes before a demanding stressor or during recovery.
generalRisks: Mild restlessness, transient headache at excessive doses, and stomach upset on an empty stomach.
longtermRisks: Contraindicated in hyperthyroidism, melanoma, or in patients taking Monoamine Oxidase Inhibitors (MAOIs).
saferUse: Take strictly on an empty stomach (competes with other Large Neutral Amino Acids for blood-brain barrier transport).
NEVER combine with non-selective MAOIs due to hypertensive crisis risk.

name: U-47700

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
toxicities: high toxicity relative to its dose due to its extreme potency
potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like alcohol or benzodiazepines
summary:
A µ-opioid receptor agonist that is related to AH-7921. Having a very short duration.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to Morphine, U-47700 ('Pinky') is roughly 7.5 times more potent with a very brief euphoric rush (1-2h) driving compulsive redosing and constant fatal overdose danger.
effectsSummary: Potent analgesia, warm sedation, opioid euphoria, sense of deep contentment, pinpoint pupils, respiratory depression, and gastrointestinal slowing.
saferUse: LETHAL OVERDOSE RISK: Always keep naloxone (Narcan, Nyxoid) immediately accessible.
NEVER combine with benzodiazepines, alcohol, pregabalin, or any CNS depressants.
Never use alone, and test with fentanyl/nitazene test strips before use.
Space doses strictly to prevent severe physical dependence and debilitating withdrawal.

name: Valproate
addictionPotential: not habit-forming
toxicities: HIGHLY TERATOGENIC (severe congenital malformations & neurodevelopmental disorders in pregnancy)
doubles Lamotrigine blood levels (Stevens-Johnson syndrome risk)
summary:
Valproate (Dépakine, Dépakote, Dépamide) is a broad-spectrum GABAergic/sodium-channel anticonvulsant, antimanic bipolar mood stabilizer, and migraine preventative.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to lithium, sodium valproate (Depakote) is a broad-spectrum mood stabilizer superior for rapid-cycling and mixed bipolar states. However, its severe teratogenicity (neural tube defects and cognitive deficits in offspring) places it under strict regulatory contraindication in women of childbearing potential.
effectsSummary: Suppresses epileptic seizures and acute mania/agitation; may cause mild sedation, tremor, GI upset, and appetite increase.
dosageRemark: STRICT 8-12h SCHEDULE: Usually divided into 2 or 3 daily intakes with meals (typically 500-2000 mg/24h total). The 'Heavy' threshold (1000 mg) represents the maximum single unit intake.
generalRisks: Nausea, stomach pain, tremor, drowsiness, thrombocytopenia (bruising/bleeding), hyperammonemia (lethargy/confusion), acute pancreatitis, and severe hepatotoxicity.
longtermRisks: Weight gain, hair thinning/alopecia, polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), liver toxicity, and severe fetal teratogenicity (strictly contraindicated in pregnancy and women of childbearing potential without strict pregnancy prevention program!).
saferUse: Take consistently with meals and never stop abruptly (especially in epilepsy — status epilepticus risk!).
CAUTION with Lamotrigine: Valproate inhibits Lamotrigine glucuronidation and doubles its blood levels, risking severe skin rash unless Lamotrigine is specifically low-dose titrated.
Avoid Alcohol, Barbiturates, Benzodiazepines, and high-dose Aspirin (displaces Valproate from protein binding and inhibits its metabolism!).

name: Venlafaxine

tolerance.full: 2 - 4 weeks for full antidepressant effect
tolerance.zero: requires slow medical taper (severe withdrawal within 12-24h of a missed dose!)

addictionPotential: not addictive, but produces intense and rapid withdrawal ('brain zaps', vertigo, nausea) if a dose is missed by even a few hours
toxicities: serotonin syndrome with MAOIs, Tramadol, DXM, or MDMA
summary:
Venlafaxine (Effexor) is a serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (SNRI) used for major depression, generalized/social anxiety, panic disorder, and neuropathic pain. Known for rapid withdrawal symptoms if an intake is delayed.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to pure SSRIs, venlafaxine (Effexor) is a dual serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (SNRI). At low doses (<150 mg), it functions essentially as an SSRI; at higher doses, robust noradrenergic reuptake inhibition activates, boosting executive energy while elevating blood pressure and causing intense discontinuation symptoms.
effectsSummary: Acts primarily as an SSRI at 37.5-75 mg and recruits norepinephrine reuptake inhibition at >=150 mg/day, increasing energy, focus, sweating, and blood pressure.
dosageRemark: STRICT REGULAR TIMING: Take at the exact same time(s) with food (every 8-12h for immediate-release tablets, or 24h). The 'Heavy' threshold (150 mg) marks the maximum single immediate-release unit intake (daily totals up to 225-375 mg/24h are divided or extended-release).
generalRisks: Nausea, sweating, elevated blood pressure, tachycardia, headache, insomnia, mydriasis, sexual dysfunction, and GI bleeding risk with NSAIDs.
longtermRisks: Sustained hypertension (monitor blood pressure regularly) and severe discontinuation syndrome ('brain zaps', dizziness, dysphoria) upon missed doses or abrupt stopping.
saferUse: Take strictly on schedule with food to avoid nausea and rapid withdrawal symptoms.
NEVER combine with MAOIs, Tramadol, Dextromethorphan, or serotonin releasers (MDMA).
Monitor blood pressure regularly, especially at doses >= 150 mg/day, and avoid NSAIDs without medical advice.

name: Vortioxetine

tolerance.full: 2 - 4 weeks

addictionPotential: not habit-forming
summary:
Vortioxetine (Brintellix / Trintellix) is a multimodal serotonergic antidepressant (SERT inhibitor + 5-HT1A agonist + 5-HT3/5-HT7/5-HT1D antagonist) used for major depressive disorder, particularly with cognitive slowing.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Vortioxetine (Trintellix) is a multimodal antidepressant combining serotonin transporter inhibition with 5-HT3, 5-HT7, and 5-HT1D antagonism and 5-HT1A agonism, proven to restore executive cognitive processing and working memory in major depressive disorder.
effectsSummary: Antidepressant and pro-cognitive action with lower sexual dysfunction and milder discontinuation symptoms than classic SSRIs, though early dose-related nausea is very common.
dosageRemark: DAILY SCHEDULE: Taken once every 24 hours (with or without food). The 'Heavy' threshold (20 mg) is the strict maximum single and daily dose.
generalRisks: Frequent nausea (especially during the first 2 weeks), itching, vivid dreams, dizziness, and increased bleeding tendency with NSAIDs/Aspirin.
longtermRisks: Long 66-hour half-life; wait at least 14-21 days after stopping before starting an MAOI.
saferUse: Take once every 24 hours (maximum 20 mg/day); Reduce dose by half if co-prescribed Bupropion (strong CYP2D6 inhibitor doubles Vortioxetine levels!).
NEVER combine with MAOIs, Tramadol, Dextromethorphan, or MDMA, and use caution with NSAIDs.

name: Zaleplon

tolerance.full: develops within 1 - 2 weeks

addictionPotential: moderately physically and psychologically addictive
toxicities: amnesia, parasomnias/sleepwalking, visual hallucinations, and fatal respiratory depression when mixed with alcohol/opioids
summary:
Zaleplon (Sonata) is an ultra-short-acting pyrazolopyrimidine Z-drug hypnotic (alpha-1 selective GABA-A modulator, ~1-hour half-life) prescribed for sleep-onset insomnia. Like Zolpidem, staying awake on higher/diverted doses causes vivid visual distortions, amnesia, and disinhibition.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to zolpidem and zopiclone, zaleplon (Sonata) has the shortest elimination half-life among Z-drugs (~1 hour). It induces rapid sleep onset and can be safely taken for middle-of-the-night awakenings without morning hangover, provided at least 4 hours of sleep remain.
effectsSummary: Rapid sleep induction, anxiety reduction, muscle relaxation; if sleep is resisted or at higher doses, causes dreamy dissociation, visual warping/hallucinations, and anterograde amnesia.
dosageRemark: DIVERSION-ADAPTED DOSAGES: Therapeutic bedtime dose is 5-10 mg (max 10 mg medically). Doses >= 20-30 mg ('Strong'/'Heavy') or insufflation cause intense short-lived Z-drug hallucinations and total memory blackouts.
generalRisks: Amnesia, complex sleep behaviors (sleep-walking, sleep-driving, compulsive redosing), hallucinations, falls, and respiratory depression with downers.
longtermRisks: Rebound insomnia, tolerance, and benzodiazepine-like dependence with chronic daily use.
saferUse: If taking medically for sleep, take ONLY while already in bed and put the box away to prevent amnesic redosing.
NEVER mix with Alcohol, Opioids, Benzodiazepines, or GHB/GBL.

name: Zolmitriptan
addictionPotential: not habit-forming (risk of medication-overuse headache if >10 days/month)
summary:
Zolmitriptan (Zomig / Zomigoro) is a second-generation 5-HT1B/1D agonist triptan for acute migraine attacks with higher oral bioavailability than sumatriptan.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to sumatriptan, zolmitriptan (Zomig) features superior blood-brain barrier penetrance and is available as a fast-acting nasal spray for acute migraine and cluster headache abortion.
effectsSummary: Aborts migraine headache, nausea, and sensory hypersensitivity; may cause transient paresthesia, neck/chest tightness, or fatigue.
dosageRemark: STRICT INTERVAL: Wait at least 2 hours before a second dose (only if symptoms recurred after initial relief). The 'Heavy' threshold (5 mg) is the maximum single unit dose per intake. Maximum 24-hour dose: 10 mg/24h.
generalRisks: Sensations of warmth/tingling, chest or jaw tightness, dizziness, somnolence, blood pressure rise, and rare coronary vasospasm.
longtermRisks: Medication-overuse rebound headaches if used >= 10 days per month.
saferUse: Wait at least 2 hours between two doses; never exceed 5 mg per intake or 10 mg in 24 hours.
NEVER mix with another triptan, ergot derivatives, or MAOIs within 24 hours.

name: Zolpidem
addictionPotential: moderately addictive
toxicities: potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like alcohol or opioids
summary:
Commonly prescribed for insomnia, Ambien (zolpidem) can cause realistic hallucinations similar to those of deliriants, and is very likely to cause amnesia at higher doses. Take care when using this drug, as it tends to lower inhibitions to a level which causes the user to do things they might not normally do when sober.

⚖️ Comparative profile: Compared to zopiclone and classic benzodiazepines, zolpidem (Ambien) selectively targets the alpha-1 subunit of GABA-A receptors with an ultra-short half-life (2 to 3 hours). It delivers rapid sleep induction without morning sedation, but carries a well-documented risk of complex sleep-related behaviors (sleep-eating, sleep-driving) and anterograde blackouts if the user remains awake after ingestion.
effectsSummary: Intense sensory and visual alterations, altered perception of space and time, emotional amplification, deep introspection, and potential ego dissolution.
saferUse: Strictly respect Set & Setting (positive mindset, calm and secure physical environment).
Always have a trusted, sober tripsitter present during the experience.
Never combine with lithium, tramadol, or MAOI/SSRI antidepressants.
Test substances with colorimetric reagents prior to use and start with a low test dose.
